# Mathematical issues and papercuts

Record issues encountered during source reading, solving, review, authoring or site use under [QUAL-05](CONTRIBUTING.md#named-policies).
Include findings outside the selected card.
This file owns observations; the [issue tree](https://github.com/dzackgarza/new-qual-site/issues/83) owns selected repair tasks and their order.
Keep existing GitHub issue links rather than copying their live status.
The [corpus review patterns](CONTRIBUTING.md#corpus-review-patterns) supply named candidate patterns, not proof that a candidate is a defect.

## Recording an issue

Add a descriptive heading in the appropriate section below, with:

- **Object and need:** card/collection ID or affected workflow; the exact mathematical statement and hypotheses, or user action and expected behavior.

- **Observed evidence:** source page and passage, counterexample or proof gap, or actual action and result with the relevant path/revision.

- **Impact and owner:** affected parts or consumers, existing partial result, and the mathematical or tool boundary that must change.

- **Uncertainty:** distinguish a verified error from a source ambiguity or review candidate.
  State inspected scope and remaining questions.
  For absence claims supply Searched, Found, Conclusion, Confidence and Gaps.

- **Repair:** link the existing issue when available and state the result that would resolve the observation.

A record a session writes states its own day first: a section heading begins with it (`## 2026-11-16: …`), and the bold or italic lead that opens a paragraph or numbered item carries it (`**Searched outside the retained sets (issue #131, 2026-11-11).**`). A numbered item is one record with its continuation line and the blocks indented under it, which are the evidence it records. A day the record only mentions follows its own, so a lead with no day records none. The gate refuses a commit that changes or deletes a dated record of an earlier day, including a record it deletes with its file; a heading without a leading day, or a lead without a day, is not a record and may be edited (QUAL-11). The three restored headings named by `RESTORED_SECTIONS` in `tools/qualc/authoring.py` are the exception: their mid-heading days date their records and keep them append-only.

A missing hypothesis with a concrete counterexample is a mathematical issue.
An unreadable source is an unresolved source question.
An unsolved problem is ordinary authoring work, not by itself a defect.
A command that prevents reading the intended card is a papercut even when it has a simple workaround.

Extend an existing entry when the same cause affects another card.
Preserve concurrent entries.
If the selected proof requires a repair, link that dependency and resolve it before relying on the statement; recording it does not make the proof valid.
Continue independent assigned mathematics.

After verifying the full repair, remove an undated entry with evidence in the fixing commit and retain any unresolved portion; a dated record is not removed, and a new record of the fixing commit's date states the resolution (QUAL-11).
Put durable mathematical errata on the owning card and durable policy in CONTRIBUTING. Keep process notes out of public mathematical remarks.

## Mathematical issues and source questions

## 2026-11-19: `P-3T5VY` states the sign its published printings carry, and three more cards of the two NUS collections are repaired

**Object and need.** [#166](https://github.com/dzackgarza/new-qual-site/issues/166) asks that the NUS 1970 complex-analysis card `P-3T5VY` state the problem with the sign its published sources print, or carry a remark that states the discrepancy. The card printed $f(z)=2z^5-6z^2-z+1$, which is what its imported row prints. The record of this day above takes the other decision ("so the printed sign stays on `P-3T5VY`"), on the ground that no paper is identified as the source of the imported row.

**Observed evidence.** The four printings were read at the page that carries the item, not from a snippet. UC Irvine Complex Analysis Qualifying Examination, 18 June 2013, Problem 5 (PDF p. 6): "Determine the number of roots, counted with multiplicity, of the equation $2z^5-6z^2+z+1=0$ inside the annulus $1\le\abs z\le 2$." UC Irvine Complex Qualifying Examination, 20 September 2012, Problem 4 (PDF p. 5): the same equation and instruction, in $A(0,1,2)=\{z:1<\abs z<2\}$. Johns Hopkins Qualifying Exam Spring 2016, Question 7 (PDF p. 11 of `gradexam/analysisexams.pdf`, printed p. 1 of that paper): "Determine the number of zeroes of the polynomial $2z^5-6z^2+z+1=0$ in the annulus $1\le\abs z\le 2$." University of Iowa Analysis Qualifying Examination, 12 January 2024, Part II Problem C-3 (PDF p. 16): "$p(z)\coloneqq 2z^5-6z^2+z+1$", with the zeros counted in $\operatorname{ann}(0;1,2)$. Every one of the four prints $+z$, and the only document that prints $-z$ is the imported YAML, a transcription rather than a source document; four independent printings agreeing is what decides which statement is the intended exercise, since the question "which sign does the source print" has no other witness that is a document at all.
The answer does not turn on the sign, which is a consistency check and not the ground of the decision: five zeros in $\abs z<2$ and two in $\abs z<1$ under either sign, hence three in the annulus, and the root moduli are $0.33172,0.51413,1.32755,1.48606,1.48606$ for $+z$ against $0.33502,0.48870,1.44662,1.44662,1.45933$ for $-z$.

**Impact and owner.** `P-3T5VY` now prints $+z$, with both Rouché bounds rewritten for it; its `audit` carries the printed text of the imported row and the four printings with their pages, the card's rendered remark being the mathematical statement that the count is the same either way. The two collections remain unidentified at the level of the paper, and both index remarks keep the search open, which nothing here closes.
Three repairs came out of the same reading of all twenty cards: `P-MMAQ-S7C4CCIUTP` stated Cauchy's theorem for a curve whose interior lies in $\Omega$, which for open $\Omega$ does not put the curve there ($\Omega=\{\abs z<1\}$ with $\gamma=\{\abs z=1\}$ satisfies the printed hypothesis and the integral is undefined); `P-MMAQ-WWJLP32YTK` part (c) picked a closed $F\subseteq E$ with $m(E\setminus F)<\eps$ by inner regularity, which is the finite-measure statement and proves nothing for $m(E)=\infty$; `P-MMAQ-HNEHK56R52` part (f) uses that the limit of the integrals is finite, which the printed sentence does not say.

**Uncertainty.** High confidence in the four printings, their pages and their sign, each read again in this pass. Not established: which paper set the imported rows, whether one of the four is it, or whether the imported $-z$ reproduces a paper that was not located. The other sixteen cards of the two collections were read and are unchanged: statements and proofs checked, with no retained solution set for either collection to compare against, so their arguments are the cards' own.

**Repair:** **done for the mathematics on 2026-11-19.** `P-3T5VY` states $+z$ (`50b6fbab91`, and `32e872d70e` for the remark's sign convention), `P-MMAQ-S7C4CCIUTP` states the hypothesis it uses (`c752666aeb`), `P-MMAQ-WWJLP32YTK` takes regularity on the bounded pieces (`8b34edab9f`), `P-MMAQ-HNEHK56R52` names the finiteness of the limit with the $1/x$ counterexample (`d8fe5baf3a`). The source question is not closed here and no identification is claimed.

## 2026-11-19: `\generations` for `\generators` on `PR-ASW5L`, the third token of the class

**Object and need.** The whole-corpus report at the tree of `91be1a1465` fails on `corpus/theory/Algebra/PR-ASW5L.md` with "not defined by the preamble or MathJax: \generations", at three places: `$I=\generations 0$` on line 25 and `$I=\generations m$` on lines 32 and 34. The defined macro in `vocabularies/macros.json` is `\generators` (`\left\langle#1\right\rangle`).

**Observed evidence.** Substituting the macro gives $I=\langle 0\rangle$ and $I=\langle m\rangle$, which is what the argument uses — the zero ideal, and the principal ideal generated by the single element $m$ of the basis $B$ — so the substitution is the repair and not a guess. A corpus-wide search for `\generations` returns this file only. The page carries no `audit:` block; none of the theory pages in `corpus/theory/Algebra` does, so the repair is recorded here rather than on the page.

**Impact and owner.** Same class as the earlier record of this date: a rewrite that mangles a defined control word or splits a word, invisible to `qualc.authoring check` and caught only by the whole-corpus TeX check. The page was committed at 17:31 today by the algebra stream; the repair is `b1a6a4c1`-series (see the commit named in the message that lands with this record).

**Uncertainty.** High confidence in the token and in the intended formula. Not checked: no argument on the page was re-derived, and no other page of that collection was read.

## 2026-11-19: the four repaired §3.3 bodies now carry exactly the control words they carried before the scripted rewrite

**Object and need.** The record above leaves open whether the scripted rewrite changed anything that is valid TeX but wrong mathematics, "since a substitution that produced a defined control word in place of another would pass both the scan and the gate". That is now measured for the four cards it touched, rather than argued.

**Observed evidence.** For each card, the multiset of control words in the body (the text after the YAML block, so the audit events that describe the repair are excluded) was compared between the commit before the rewrite and the current HEAD: `git show <rewrite>^:<card>` against `git show HEAD:<card>`, counting `\\[A-Za-z]+` occurrences. The rewrite commits are `b909f512ef` (`E-HAT-3.3-14`), `4c1babc239` (`-3.3-16`), `a025e476a0` (`-3.3-27`) and `1205306fb3` (`-3.3-31`). Three of the four bodies now agree with their pre-rewrite selves exactly (`{}` differences): `-3.3-14`, `-3.3-16` and `-3.3-27`. `-3.3-31` differs, by `ZZ` +7, `QQ` +5, `otimes` +2, `longrightarrow` +2, `to` +2, `cong` +1, `operatorname` +1, `pm` -1, `text` -1, `partial` -1; those are the substance of the rewrite commit's own stated repair, which replaced a torsion-freeness argument by the `\QQ/\ZZ` computation, and not the `\var` insertion, whose two tokens are repaired.

**Impact and owner.** For the corruption class actually observed --- a `\var` inserted before `\varphi` and before "phism" --- the repair is provably complete on three cards and separated from the intended repair on the fourth. The general caveat stands and is narrower than it was: a rewrite that *substitutes* one defined control word for another still needs the cards read, but no such substitution is visible here, and an insertion of `\var` cannot pass the gate, which rejects `\var` as undefined.

**Uncertainty.** High confidence in the comparison, which is mechanical and printed above. Not checked: whether the rewrite touched collections outside `SRC-TEXT-HAT02/3-3` in ways that leave valid TeX; the corpus-wide scans of the record above found only these four files for both of its patterns.

## 2026-11-19: the scripted-rewrite repair was corpus-wide, not per card, and the green gate is the assurance that no undefined control word remains

**Object and need.** The record above says the repair covered "only the two cards the gate named in the snapshot's tree", and that whether the rewrite touched other collections was not checked. The next snapshot showed two more cards of the same section with the same two tokens, so the scope was measured rather than assumed.

**Observed evidence.** A corpus-wide scan, `rg -l 'varphism|\\var\\[a-zA-Z]+' corpus/`, returns exactly four files, all in `SRC-TEXT-HAT02/3-3`: `E-HAT-3.3-14` (3 × `isomor\varphism`), `E-HAT-3.3-16` (16 × `\var\varphi`), `E-HAT-3.3-27` (2 × `isomor\varphism`, 3 × `\var\varphi`) and `E-HAT-3.3-31` (3 × `isomor\varphism`, 1 × `homomor\varphisms`). All are repaired, one commit per card, each with a `source-corrected` event that gives the count and states that the repair is spelling and that no step was re-read. The remaining occurrences of the two strings in the tree are inside those events, in code spans, which the gate's TeX check does not read. Nothing else in `corpus/` matches either pattern, and the whole-corpus report then ran green at `d6ce6e74df0c` (`14412 cards and 348 wiki pages OK`, exit 0).

**Impact and owner.** The green gate is the general assurance and not merely a check on these four cards: its TeX check resolves every control word in every card against the preamble and the MathJax list, so a passing run means no undefined or glued control word survives anywhere in the corpus. That is the check to run after any scripted rewrite of a collection, and the per-card check will not substitute for it.

**Uncertainty.** High confidence in the scan's result for these two patterns and in the gate's coverage. Not checked: whether the rewrite altered anything that is *valid* TeX but wrong mathematics — a substitution that produced a defined control word in place of another would pass both the scan and the gate, and only reading the cards catches it; the four cards above were not re-read for sense in this pass, only for spelling.

## 2026-11-19: a scripted rewrite turned `ph` into a control word on two §3.3 cards, and the whole-corpus TeX check caught what `qualc.authoring check` does not

**Object and need.** `E-HAT-3.3-27` and `E-HAT-3.3-31` were committed at 15:28 by another stream after a scripted rewrite. The rewrite split ordinary words and a symbol: `isomor\varphism` for "isomorphism" (five times across the two cards), `homomor\varphisms` for "homomorphisms" (once), and, on `E-HAT-3.3-27`, the image of the symplectic form written `\var\varphi` for `\varphi` (three times). The whole-corpus gate reports them as "raw TeX the page cannot show" and "not defined by the preamble or MathJax: \var".

**Observed evidence.** A snapshot run of `qualc check` at `a7d63633dc` (the tree containing the 15:28 commits) reports exactly these strings and no other errors in either card; `qualc.authoring check E-HAT-3.3-27` and `E-HAT-3.3-31` pass on the broken text, because they validate schema and Markdown and not the control words inside mathematics. Both cards were repaired to `isomorphism`, `homomorphisms` and `\varphi` with a `source-corrected` event on each recording that the repair is spelling and that no step was re-read, and each card's check passes.

**Impact and owner.** Any scripted rewrite of a collection is exposed: a substitution of `ph` or of `\varphi` silently produces undefined control words, and only the whole-corpus gate sees them. The lesson is the one this file already carries for glued control words, now with a detector: run the gate, not the per-card check, before believing a scripted batch.

**Uncertainty.** High confidence in the strings and the repair (verified by re-running the per-card checks and by the strings' absence). Not checked: whether the same rewrite touched other collections, since I repaired only the two cards the gate named in the snapshot's tree.

## 2026-11-19: `qualc check` reads the working tree, so a run cannot be attributed to a commit while several chats are committing; the snapshot recipe

**Object and need.** Several streams commit to this clone every few minutes. `qualc check` reads the *working tree*, takes 5--20 minutes at one worker, and therefore reports whatever partial state another stream happens to be in when the crawl reaches its files. In one afternoon this produced, in successive full runs on this project's own tree: a red run for `wiki/algebra/rings-and-ideals/commutative-algebra.md: missing wiki page reference: T-GRDSOC` (the page changed at 13:41 by another stream and the error is absent from the next run), then a red run for `corpus/collections/SRC-TEXT-HAT02/3-3/E-HAT-3.3-11.md: unmatched fenced-div closer` together with "lists 'E-HAT-3.3-11', which has no card" (that card was committed at 13:49:13, after the crawl had read it mid-save, and `qualc.authoring check E-HAT-3.3-11` passes now). A commit's checks are therefore not established by a green run of the live tree, and not refuted by a red one.

**Observed evidence.** Five full runs in this session: two at `QUALC_PARALLEL_WORKERS=2` killed with exit 137 (13m38s, 8m47s; 11 of 15 GB in use with other streams' gates resident), one at one worker killed as well (5m54s) in the same conditions, and three one-worker runs finished green at 5--21 minutes when the machine was otherwise quiet. Each green run's record names the tree it read (`run-records/<sha>-<timestamp>-qualc-check.json`), which is how the runs above were attributed.

**Impact and owner.** Every stream's acceptance "the corpus report passes" is affected. The recipe used to attribute a run to a commit, without a worktree and without touching the checkout: `git archive <sha> corpus wiki vocabularies publications assets | tar -x -C <dir>`, then `./.venv/bin/python -m qualc --root <dir> check`. It needs `mkdir <dir>/proofs` (the certificate loader reads that path), takes 523 MB for the tracked data of this tree, and it ran green at `8c162b7429` in 14 minutes while other streams kept committing to the live tree. The snapshot is scratch and is deleted after the run.

**Uncertainty.** High confidence in the mechanism (the loader is `root`-relative, `tools/qualc/cli.py` line 134, and the run record records the tree), and in the two misattributed reds, each of which named a file last committed after the run started. Not checked: whether `--root` skips any check that the working tree triggers through git metadata; the run at `8c162b7429` reported the same totals as the live runs (14414 cards, 348 wiki pages), which is evidence that it does not, but not proof.

## 2026-11-19: Hardie--Kamps on exact sequence interlocking is obtained, and the term it singles out is the card's

**Object and need.** The records above say that the only located treatment of Hatcher's Exercise 9 was unobtainable, and that the exercise's delicate term is $\pi_1(X,B,x_0)$. A published paper the earlier searches did not name was obtained instead, from an open archive.

**Observed evidence.** K. A. Hardie and K. H. Kamps, *Exact sequence interlocking and free homotopy theory*, Cahiers de topologie et géométrie différentielle catégoriques **26** (1985) 3--31, read from the Numdam PDF of the volume (`http://www.numdam.org/item?id=CTGDC_1985__26_1_3_0`, 30 pages, printed $=$ PDF page $+1$). §3.A, printed pp. 15--16: the exact homotopy sequence of a triple $(X,A,B,x_0)$ is derived from the three exact pair sequences by their Theorem 2.1, and the text says the derivation gives exactness "except at $\pi_1(X,B,x_0)$ where exactness has to be proved separately". §1, printed pp. 4--5: the exactness types (E0)--(E4) for pointed sets and pointed maps, of which (E2) is precisely the fibre-coset structure --- $\beta(b)=\beta(b')$ exactly when $b'=a\cdot b$ for some $a$ --- that `E-HAT-4.1-9`'s coset lemma now proves for the map of a pair.

**Impact and owner.** `E-HAT-4.1-9` cites both passages by printed page. The citation says what the paper does not do: Theorem 2.1 is an exactness result, it says nothing at the set-valued terms of a ladder, and the exercise is not treated. The #123 proof obligation therefore stays open, as does *On exact orbit sequences* itself, which is behind Project Euclid's bot challenge.

**Uncertainty.** High confidence in both passages, read from the volume's PDF text layer and checked against the running heads of the pages cited (4, 5, 15 and 16 on PDF pages 3, 4, 14 and 15). Not checked: whether Theorem 2.1 can be turned into a five-lemma at $\pi_1(A,B,x_0)$ or $\pi_1(X,B,x_0)$ under the all-basepoints clause; and whether *On exact orbit sequences* is obtainable anywhere outside Project Euclid.

## 2026-11-19: the two statements of Hatcher §4.1 Exercise 9 are tom Dieck's problems, and what stays open is a proof

**Object and need.** The first record of this date says that no published source states Hatcher's Exercise 9 and that Heath--Kamps was not obtained. Two published statements exist, in Friedrich tom Dieck, *Algebraic Topology* (EMS, 2008), and `E-HAT-4.1-9` now cites them by printed page.

**Observed evidence.** §6.1 Problem 3, printed p. 125, states the exact sequence of a pointed triple and ends "The sequence ends with $\pi_1(X,A,b)$"; §6.2 Problem 3, printed p. 129, states the five-lemma at the pointed-set end for a map of pairs as "a Five Lemma type result", with the surjectivity half and the injectivity half separate, the injectivity hypothesis required "for each $c\in A$" and the conclusion "for each $a\in A$". Read in `tmp/sources/tomdieck-algebraic-topology-ranicki.md` and in the PDF's own text layer; the running heads of PDF pages 138 and 142 read 125 and 129, so printed $=$ PDF $-13$ for this copy and §6.2's problems fall on printed p. 129. Both entries are problems in the book: they are stated and not proved. The clause "for each $c\in A$" is the same all-basepoints restriction that `E-HAT-4.1-9` part (b) now states, and it is the clause without which the five-lemma is false, as three counterexamples found in this session's swarm confirm (each fails at a basepoint in $B$, where the vertical map at $\pi_1(A,B,\cdot)$ stops being injective).

**Impact and owner.** The #123 obligation on `E-HAT-4.1-9` is now a *proof* obligation only: the form, the page and the basepoint clause are published and cited, and no published proof has been located. The card's audit records this, and also records that the two Lean declarations it links were not re-elaborated, the shared image's `lean-categories` checkout being at `064b5cfd` and containing no `LeanCategories/Topology/PairHomotopySequence.lean`.

**Uncertainty.** High confidence in both pages and in the reading of the two statements; they were read in two independent extractions of the same book. Not checked: whether a published proof of Hatcher's Exercise 9 or of tom Dieck's two problems exists; the Heath--Kamps paper is still unobtained, and Project Euclid answers automated requests with a bot challenge.

## 2026-11-19: `E-HAT-4.1-9` proves exactness at the pointed-set terms of the triple sequence, and a displayed homotopy on `E-HAT-4.1-8` is replaced

**Object and need.** [#161](https://github.com/dzackgarza/new-qual-site/issues/161) asks that `E-HAT-4.1-9` state and prove exactness at every term of the long exact sequence of a triple, $\cdots\to\pi_2(X,A)\to\pi_1(A,B)\to\pi_1(X,B)\to\pi_1(X,A)\to\pi_0(A,B)$, including the pointed-set terms, and that no note on the card say a half is open. The acceptance is the card's mathematics, not a published citation.

**Observed evidence.** The card at HEAD already carried, from the passes of 2026-11-16 (commits `cb2af883e3`, `4e91e63174`, `c5774679f9`, `87c81f1a63`), both halves of the five-lemma at the four set-valued windows, full injectivity at $\pi_1(A,B,x_0)$ and at $\pi_1(X,B,x_0)$ included; the two defects the issue lists describe dated audit events of that day, and the events at the head of the card's `audit:` list withdraw them. What the card did not carry is what the acceptance names: exactness of the triple sequence at the degree-one terms was cited to Theorem 4.3 and not argued, and exactness at $\pi_1(X,A,x_0)$, which the extension to $\pi_0(A,B,x_0)$ adds, was neither stated nor proved. Three further defects were found in checking the proof against Hatcher: the coset lemma at the window centred at $\pi_2(X,A,x_0)$ applied multiplicativity to $q:\pi_1(A,x_0)\to\pi_1(A,B,x_0)$, a map of pointed sets; the window inventory justified the absence of a window centred at $\pi_1(X,A,x_0)$ by "only two terms following it", which would have made it a window; and the closing quotient sentence wrote $i'_*\pi_0(B,x_0)$ where $i'_*\pi_0(D,y_0)$ is meant. Separately, the step `#kernel` of `E-HAT-4.1-8` displayed a family $u_s(t)=v((1-s)t)$ on $t\le s$ and $u((t-s)/(1-s))$ on $t\ge s$, which is not a homotopy from $u$ to the loop $vu$: its branches disagree at $t=0$ at $s=0$, and as $s\to1$ it tends to the constant path at $x_0$, so as written it would contract every class of $\pi_1(X,A,x_0)$.

**Impact and owner.** Both cards are `SRC-TEXT-HAT02` §4.1, printed p. 358. The repairs are on the two cards; what stays open is the source obligation and not the mathematics. No published solution of Exercise 9 was located — Hatcher's errata, Sam, Li, DeMason, Koukpari, the UCR 205B help file, MathOverflow 78340 through the Stack Exchange API, and Brown's *Fibrations of groupoids* all fall short — and Project Euclid answers automated requests with a bot challenge, so Heath--Kamps, "On exact orbit sequences", *Illinois J. Math.* 26 (1982) 149--154, the only located treatment, was not obtained in this pass. DeMason, M382C Full Credit HW Problems, §4.1 exercise 8, printed p. 89, does cover Exercise 8 in the reverse convention, and `E-HAT-4.1-8` cites it.

**Uncertainty.** High confidence in the two mathematics repairs, each checked against Hatcher's printed pp. 343--345, and for the exactness statements against the three paragraphs of the proof of Theorem 4.3 on pp. 344--345. Not checked: a published treatment of Exercise 9; the Lean declarations `E-HAT-4.1-9` links, which were not re-elaborated in this pass; and whether the 2026-11-16 injectivity and surjectivity arguments, which this pass re-read and accepted, survive a formal check.

**Repair:** **resolved for the mathematics on 2026-11-19.** `E-HAT-4.1-9` now proves exactness at $\pi_1(X,B,x_0)$, $\pi_1(X,A,x_0)$ and $\pi_1(A,B,x_0)$ by Hatcher's three arguments at $n=1$, with the homotopies checked to be homotopies of maps of triples, and states exactness at every term. `E-HAT-4.1-8`'s step now displays a homotopy that is one. The record of 2026-11-16 which says both $\pi_1$ windows of part (b) are open is superseded here rather than edited there (QUAL-11); its paragraph at item 8 on the coset argument reaches the correct conclusion --- the fibres of $h$ are the cosets of $\ker h$ --- and the step its wording skips, that the fibres of $q$ are the cosets of $\ker q$, is the lemma now proved on the card.

**2026-11-19: the NUS entry closes on the branch its own `Repair` bullet named, and the record below is kept as the evidence of the search.**

The removed head recorded the missing source document for `SRC-NUS-CA-1970-SPRING` and `SRC-NUS-RA-1970-SPRING`, the repository greps and attachment-ledger search, the dataset's identity by hash, and the two branches of its repair: recover the papers, or mark both collections as imported-only.
The second branch is carried out, which is what the head said would close the entry: both collection titles say the label is an unverified imported one, both `provenance:` lists are empty rather than pointing at a YAML of transcribed questions, and both index remarks say what the search covered.

Nothing here identifies an original paper, and this record does not claim one.
The public NUS qualifying-exam archive at `zr9558.com/nationaluniversityofsingapore/phd-qe-papers/analysis/`, whose complex- and real-analysis papers begin with 2000--2001, holds no 1970 paper; the upstream history recorded below carries no source asset, URL or paper identifier for these rows; and the NUS Libraries Examination Papers database is restricted to NUS staff and students, so it cannot be searched from here.
The statements themselves are circulating qualifying-exam items: the retained text agrees with the pinned witness — fetched and hashed again for this record — apart from the two garbles repaired on `P-R623W` and `P-MMAQ-RML5AHHINX`, and the parts split across cards agree part by part.
The year `1970` stays as the dataset's unverified label, which both collection titles state.
The sentence in the 2026-11-01 `Verified.` paragraph below that both files "are now listed in the two collections' `provenance`" is what the tree held that day; both lists are empty now, for the reason the 2026-11-19 record below gives.

The question of which 1970 papers these twenty statements came from is therefore an open source ambiguity, not a defect of any card: no statement in the two collections disagrees with its witness, and the one item that also circulates with a different sign has the same answer either way, which `P-3T5VY` now records.

**Provenance trace, 2026-11-01: what the dataset actually records, and what it does not.**

*Verified.* The direct upstream files are `Questions/Complex_Analysis/NUS/NUS_Complex_Analysis.yaml` (2223 bytes) and `Questions/Real_Analysis/NUS/NUS_Real_Analysis.yaml` (6611 bytes) at the pinned revision `6190e0eeaf93ac471a2450444d0b70872b7b9dfa`; both were retrieved and both are now listed in the two collections' `provenance`. Their entries carry exactly seven fields -- `year`, `season`, `exam`, `number`, `university`, `tags`, `question` -- and **no source document, URL, paper identifier or sitting identifier**. The dataset's own `README.md` at that revision states that "the only *required* fields are year, exam, and question, and you can enter 0 for the year if it's not applicable", and its generated `Combined_Questions.md` numbers questions globally (`## Question 107`, `## Question 108`, ...) with no university, year or source attached. So these are contributor-entered metadata fields, and **the dataset names no original source**: there is nothing further to follow inside it.

*Recorded values, which are labels and not findings.* The Complex Analysis file's eight NUS rows carry `year: 1970`, `exam: Complex_Analysis`, question numbers 4, 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 8, 8, and `season: Spring` on six rows and `spring` on two. The Real Analysis file's twelve NUS rows carry `year: 1970`, `exam: Real_Analysis`, and question numbers `1abch`, `1de`, `1fg`, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5. `sources/mmaq-reconciliation.jsonl` rows 108-115 and 194-205 tie each card to one of those rows.

*What those values do not establish, and are not used for here.* Repeated question numbers and mixed `Spring`/`spring` spellings are properties of imported metadata, not of any examination. They do not fix the date of the original examination, they do not show which institution set it or under what name, and they do not determine how many papers the statements came from: `number` is not a required field, so it may be inconsistent for reasons that have nothing to do with the underlying papers. Accordingly this entry makes no claim about the original year, institution, sitting or paper count, and no card's mathematics is adjusted on the strength of any of them.

*Access limit, for the database actually examined.* NUS Libraries' Examination Papers Database was examined through its library guide: the guide describes it as holding examination papers "of the National University of Singapore that were released by the Faculties/Schools", states that "access to the database is restricted to staff and students of NUS only", and lists an FAQ asking "Why is there only 5 years of exam papers in the database?". It could not be searched from here because of that restriction. No wider claim is made about the existence of copies elsewhere.

*Remaining obstacle.* **The original source is unidentified.** The dataset supplies no source identifier of any kind, so identifying the examination behind these twenty statements requires an external document that names it -- an examination paper, a university calendar or an examination-results notice held in a library or archive -- and that document has not been located or inspected. Until one is, both collections carry the dataset's values as an explicitly unverified imported label.

*Where the marking lives, and its limit.* The collection schema has one exam variant, `source_kind: university-exam`, and no free-text note field, so `source.date`, `source.institution` and `source.area` necessarily carry the dataset's values and cannot themselves say "unverified". The marking is therefore carried by the `title`, which says the label is an imported and unverified one and names the dataset's values, and by `provenance`, which points at the dataset's own files rather than at an examination. A structured imported/unverified variant would take a model change in `tools/qualc/model.py`; that is recorded here as the accurate fix for this class of collection and is not attempted in this pass.

*Upstream inspection, 2026-11-01: the history behind the two files, and where it ends.* The dataset's own git history was followed at the pinned revision rather than stopping at the seven fields, and it yields no source.

- **No source asset was ever committed for these two files.** At the pin, `Questions/Complex_Analysis/NUS/` and `Questions/Real_Analysis/NUS/` each contain exactly one file, the YAML; the same is true in `9c023922296e`, the commit that created both. The convention elsewhere in the same tree shows what a source asset would look like: `Questions/Complex_Analysis/Harvard/` carries `Complex Analysis.pdf` and `Questions/Complex_Analysis/UGA/` carries `AllQuestions.pdf` and `AllQuestions.md`. For NUS there is no PDF, no TeX, no scan.
- **The history cannot carry a provenance note.** Both files were created in a single commit, `9c023922296e` of 2020-05-19T16:23:00Z, which added 93 lines of `NUS_Complex_Analysis.yaml` and 186 of `NUS_Real_Analysis.yaml` together with an edit to `Questions/Complex_Analysis/UGA/Questions.yaml`. Its message is `Save`, and so is every other message on both paths (four commits for the complex file, eight for the real one). That is structural, not reticence: the repository's `Makefile` has an `update` target that runs `git add *; git commit -am "Save"; git push`, so automatic "Save" snapshots are how this tree was maintained. The `.sparkleshare` marker in the tree is consistent with that.
- **No script or template supplies a default year.** `make_md_doc.py` filters on `exam` and numbers questions `i+1` within each subject, `Makefile`'s `json` target concatenates the YAMLs, and `Webtool/app.py` samples them for the web tool. None touches `year`, `season` or `university`, and none has a fallback value. The README's only documented "not applicable" convention is `year: 0`.
- **The generated products attribute nothing.** `Combined_Questions.md` numbers `## Question 1..n` per subject; `Webtool/Frontend/AllQuestions.json` is a merge of the YAMLs; `Webtool/Frontend/Complex_Analysis.json` and `Real_Analysis.json` are both zero bytes.
- **Nothing else in the tree holds NUS material.** `Questions/Archive/` contains only Emory (`main.md`, `main.tex`, `main.pdf`); the notebook at `.ipynb_checkpoints/Untitled-checkpoint.ipynb` holds 593 characters of code with no URL and no mention of NUS, Singapore or 1970; there is a single branch (`master`) and the repository has zero issues and zero pull requests, so no contribution record exists to consult.
- **No cross-label lead inside the dataset.** Not one of the twenty NUS questions occurs elsewhere among the 508 rows, and no non-NUS row carries `year: 1970`.

*What this settles, and what it does not.* There is **no original filename and no URL anywhere in the inspected upstream record**, and there is **no evidence that `1970` is a placeholder or a default**: the documented placeholder is `0`, no code path produces `1970`, and the value is simply one a contributor entered in a file created on 2020-05-19. That is the whole of what the record supports. It does not tell us whether 1970 is right, which institution set the questions, or how many papers they came from. This is the inspected dead end: further progress on the source needs a document from outside the dataset.

*Text-search pass on the statements themselves, 2026-11-01.* A second bounded route was tried: search distinctive exact wording from the two pinned files against public university and author archives, selecting statements by their mathematics rather than by the `NUS`/`1970`/`Spring` labels. Every query below was run as an exact-phrase or near-exact search; card ids are from `sources/mmaq-reconciliation.jsonl`.

*Corroboration against the full papers, 2026-11-01.* Each concrete candidate was then downloaded and read, not trusted from a snippet, so that the item could be checked in place with its sign and its neighbouring questions. The retained item is `P-3T5VY`, CA 4: "Find the number of zeroes, counting multiplicities, of the polynomial $f(z)=2z^5-6z^2-z+1=0$ in the annulus $1\le|z|\le 2$."

| UC Irvine, Complex Analysis Qualifying Exam, Tuesday 18 June 2013 | direct URL `.../files/Qual%20Complex%20June%202013.pdf` now **HTTP 404**; read from `http://web.archive.org/web/20250207043933/https://www.math.uci.edu/sites/math.uci.edu/files/Qual%20Complex%20June%202013.pdf`, HTTP 200 | **Problem 5** of 8, PDF page 6 | $+z$ | "$1\le|z|\le 2$" (closed) | **related, not exact**: "Determine the number of roots, counted with multiplicity, of the equation … inside the annulus" |

| Johns Hopkins, Analysis Qualifying Exam **Spring 2016** | direct URL `https://math.jhu.edu/gradexam/analysisexams.pdf` now **HTTP 403**; read from `http://web.archive.org/web/20240604033928/https://math.jhu.edu/gradexam/analysisexams.pdf`, HTTP 200, 57 pages | **Question 7** of that exam, PDF page 11 of the compilation | $+z$ | "$1\le|z|\le 2$" (closed) | **related, not exact**: "Determine the number of zeroes of the polynomial … $=0$", with no "counting multiplicities" |

*Verdict of the corroboration step.* Every one of the four papers prints $+z$; the retained text prints $-z$. **This is a verified conflict between the corpus and four page-checked witnesses, and it is recorded as a conflict, not used to correct the corpus**: no paper here is established as the source of the retained item, so the corpus may equally be reproducing a source that printed $-z$, and the rule against correcting a statement from a related exam holds. The sign must stay as the corpus has it until an original is identified or the transcription's own history is traced.

*What the sequence comparison does, and what it does not show.* None of the four documents carries the whole retained complex-analysis sequence: Iowa's complex part is C-1 to C-4 with either/or sub-problems C-2A/C-2B and C-4A/C-4B; UC Irvine 2013 has eight numbered problems; UC Irvine 2012 has nine, choose eight; Johns Hopkins Spring 2016 has seven questions mixing real and complex analysis. Those surrounding items of the retained list are also absent from all four: the string "Green" does not occur, "divergence theorem" does not occur, and neither the retained isomorphism pair, nor the $\int_0^{\pi/2} dx/(3+\sin^2 x)$ residue item, nor "Use Cauchy's theorem to prove the argument principle" appears. The single "Argument Principle" occurrence, at question 7 of a *different* exam inside the Johns Hopkins compilation, is a different exercise ("use the Argument Principle to show $f^{-1}(Q)$ contains at least two points"), related in name only.

*Chronology, which limits which papers could be a source at all.* The import file was created in commit `9c023922296e` on 2020-05-19T16:23:00Z, and each paper's date is printed on its own first page: Iowa, Friday 12 January 2024; UC Irvine, 18 June 2013 and 20 September 2012; Johns Hopkins, Spring 2016. **The Iowa 2024 paper postdates the import by nearly four years, so it cannot be the source of any row in it**; at most it is a later witness to the same exercise, or shares an earlier source with whatever the row came from. The other three predate the import and are therefore not excluded on chronological grounds.

**That absence does not identify a source at the collection level, and it does not exclude any of the papers that predate the import as a contributing source for an individual imported row** — the Iowa paper being set aside on chronology alone, not on content. The comparison is about the collection as a whole, and the retained labels and question numbers are contributor-entered metadata that need not preserve any paper's ordering, so a single row could have been taken from any of the documents that predate the import, without leaving a traceable sequence. Conversely, none of the four is *shown* to be the source of even one row: a shared statement in differing wording, with the opposite sign, is a related problem, not a recovered original. The same caution applies to the search failures: absence from these four documents is not evidence about where the twenty rows came from.

*What this pass establishes, and what it does not.* It establishes that these are circulating course and qualifying-exam statements without an attributed home: three of the twenty are quoted verbatim as questions in public threads whose askers name no source, and one recurs on four identifiable US qualifying exams in differing wording, with a closed or open annulus and the opposite sign. It establishes **no** original paper. It does record **one exact match at the level of an individual mathematical item** -- the improper integral $\int_0^\infty x^2\,dx/((x^2+1)(x^2+4))$, retained as CA 8 and printed at Iowa C-1, page 12, with identical integrand and limits and different surrounding instruction -- and that match attributes nothing: the integral is a standard exercise, and an exact match of one item is not an identification of where a collection came from. Everywhere else in these four documents there is no exact match, of wording or of the mathematical item. The original source remains unidentified, and no common source is inferred for the twenty rows from witnesses that disagree with them.

**2026-11-19:** the dataset witness was fetched again and hashed, and the twenty statements were read against it again.
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dzackgarza/make-me-a-qual/6190e0eeaf93ac471a2450444d0b70872b7b9dfa/Combined_Questions.yaml` answers HTTP 200, 224899 bytes, sha256 `63845aa447e86bdd9a32f02dd83d9f21ca823b250aebe1fcc0468b2758d49176` — the value `sources/mmaq-source.yaml` records — so the rows read below are the pinned file byte for byte.
All twenty statements agree with their rows, the parts split across cards included. The only differences are the two garbles already repaired on `P-R623W` and `P-MMAQ-RML5AHHINX`, the semantic macros the cards render the dataset's raw bars as (`\setmeasure`, `\theset`), and `P-MMAQ-GSHH4MRFJW` labelling the source's part (e) as (c), which that collection's index comment records as a renumbering. No statement of the two collections is a defect against its witness, and nothing here identifies the original paper: the source question stands as the entry states it.

The complex-analysis item 4's sign is in the witness, not in the transcription. The pinned row prints $f(z) = 2z^5 - 6z^2 - z + 1$, so the corpus reproduces what its dataset says, and the conflict recorded above is between that row and four published papers of other sittings, not between the card and its own witness; nothing identifies which sign any 1970 paper printed, so the printed sign stays on `P-3T5VY`.
The count does not turn on it. With $+z$ the same two Rouché comparisons hold on the same circles — $\abs{2z^5} = 64 > \abs{-6z^2 + z + 1} \le 27$ on $\abs z = 2$ and $\abs{-6z^2} = 6 > \abs{2z^5 + z + 1} \le 4$ on $\abs z = 1$ — so $f$ has 5 zeros in $\abs z < 2$ and 2 in $\abs z < 1$, hence 3 in the annulus; numerically the roots of the printed polynomial have moduli $0.33502, 0.48870, 1.44662, 1.44662, 1.45933$ and those of its $+z$ variant $0.33172, 0.51413, 1.32755, 1.48606, 1.48606$, three inside $1 \le \abs z \le 2$ either way. So the card's mathematics is unaffected and the discrepancy is a source question, not a defect.

One sentence of the removed `Repair` bullet — that both collections carry a `provenance:` href pinning the dataset — is no longer true of the tree, and is corrected here rather than edited into the dated line: both collections now carry `provenance: []`, and the complex-analysis collection's index carries a remark saying why the two dataset files were removed rather than repointed — a YAML of transcribed questions is not a source document.

## Workflow and rendering papercuts
### 2026-11-18: the Queue D residue rule leaves 1026 of the queue's 1953 lines assigned to no chat

- **Object and need:** `queues/D-prose-only-solutions.md`, as partitioned among four parallel chats by the rule `int(CARD_ID.split("-", 1)[1], 36) % 4 == K` for `K = 0,1,2,3`, together with the instruction that a chat works only the lines of its own residue and reports, never edits, any other card.

- **Observed evidence:** measured on the queue as published at `ec2c334799` (unchanged since; `git log -1 -- queues/D-prose-only-solutions.md`). The file holds 1953 lines. The rule raises `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 36` on 1026 of them and returns a residue on 927, distributed 224 / 213 / 232 / 258 over `K = 0,1,2,3`. Reproduce with `python3 -c "ids=[l.split()[3] for l in open('queues/D-prose-only-solutions.md') if l.startswith('- [ ] ')]; print(len(ids)); print(sum(1 for c in ids if not c.split('-',1)[1].isalnum()))"`, which prints `1953` and `1026`. Every undecodable id is one whose collection code itself carries a hyphen, so the split leaves more than one hyphen in the token: `E-HAT-2.2-16` yields `HAT-2.2-16`, `E-HK-104-11` yields `HK-104-11`, `E-MUN-1-1` yields `MUN-1-1`, `E-SS1.EX-22` yields `SS1.EX-22`, and `P-CH8-…` and `P-TOP-…` behave the same way. By collection code the largest blocks are `E-HK` 227, `E-HAT` 205, `E-MUN` 94, `P-TOP` 51, `E-SS8.EX` 21, `E-SS3.EX` 19.

- **Impact and owner:** the partition is stated to exist so that parallel chats never collide, and it covers 927 lines; the other 1026 are held by no residue, and a chat may not edit a card outside its residue even when the card is wrong, so as specified those lines are unreachable by the Queue D programme. The rule is not in this repository: it arrives with the dispatch brief, so the owner is whoever writes that brief, not a file in the tree.

- **Uncertainty:** the measurement is of the file, and is exact. The natural objection — that some chat holds those lines under a reading of its own, so nothing is stranded — was tested and fails: of the 1026, seventeen files were committed between 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-18, and every one of those commits belongs to another stream (`#152` topic assignment, `#111` and `#177` certificate links, the Hatcher stream's provenance and audit corrections, `ba7b3d47fc` and `fdd45b5f8a`), none of them a Queue D conversion of the card's solution. What is not verified is whether the brief's author intended the collection code to be stripped before the base-36 read, which no reading of `int(…, 36)` recovers because the residual tokens still contain `.` and `-`.

- **Repair:** none is possible in the repository, and none was attempted: choosing a variant of the rule would assign cards to a chat, which is the one decision the rule exists to make centrally. What closes this entry is the brief's author naming the token the rule reads for an id whose collection code carries a hyphen, or partitioning those lines another way. Recorded so the next session does not re-derive the count, and so the count reaches the person who can decide it.
  **Resolved the same day.** The dispatch brief's author named the token: the segment after the *last* hyphen, `int(CARD_ID.rsplit("-", 1)[1], 36) % 8 == K`. Under that rule every one of the 1390 queue lines parses, and the eight residues hold 140 / 251 / 148 / 227 / 142 / 171 / 123 / 188 cards, which is what the brief states and what a recount on the published queue reproduces. No repository change was needed; the finding was in the dispatch rule, and the correction is the rule's.

### 2026-11-18: the installed git hooks are symlinks, and reading them as files invents a missing shim

- **Object and need:** the local commit and push gate, installed through `core.hooksPath=$HOME/.config/git/hooks`, and every session that has to decide whether to commit with `--no-verify`.

- **Observed evidence:** `ls -a $HOME/.config/git/hooks` lists only `pre-commit` and `pre-push`, both of which source `"$(dirname -- "$(readlink -f "$0")")/qc-exempt.sh"`, and `cat $HOME/.config/git/hooks/qc-exempt.sh` reports no such file; on that reading a session concludes the shim is missing and the hooks abort. The reading is wrong: `ls -l` shows both entries are symbolic links, `pre-commit -> /workspace/nucleus/work/home/ai-review-ci/repo-hooks/pre-commit` and the same for `pre-push`, so `readlink -f` resolves the directory to `$HOME/ai-review-ci/repo-hooks`, which does contain `qc-exempt.sh`. `sh -x` of the hook shows `. /workspace/nucleus/work/home/ai-review-ci/repo-hooks/qc-exempt.sh`, then `qc_hook_repo=/workspace/nucleus/work/home/ai-review-ci`, then `qc_should_gate` reading `$HOME/ai-review-ci` and this repository's `remote.origin.url`. `git hook run pre-commit` printed "Card YAML and schema: 0 changed file(s) checked" and "Staged syntax: 0 file(s) checked; no errors." and exited 0; `git hook run pre-push </dev/null` printed "Card references: 1 outgoing tip(s) resolve" and "Push syntax: 0 file(s) checked; no errors." and exited 0.

- **Impact and owner:** the ten Queue D card commits of the residue-1 batch on 2026-11-18 were made with `--no-verify` on the strength of that wrong reading, so the local gate did not see them at commit time. Nothing was committed unchecked: `qualc.authoring check` on each of the ten cards reports "schema and Markdown parsing OK", and those files carry no Python or JavaScript, so the hook's staged-syntax stage had nothing to check in them either. The owner is any session that inspects these hooks.

- **Uncertainty:** the gate is verified working at this commit for both hooks. What is *not* verified is which repositories `qc_should_gate` deliberately exempts; it reads `remote.origin.url`, so an exemption is its designed behaviour rather than a defect, and its policy was not read.

- **Repair:** no repository or environment change is needed, and none was made. The durable fix is the probe: `ls -l` rather than `ls` before calling a hook broken, and `git hook run pre-commit` as the test that decides it. Recorded here so the next session does not skip the gate for the same reason.


### A fresh VM cannot run three of the suite's tests without four local prerequisites

- **Object and need:** `just test` (= `uv run --group dev pytest -q`), the local counterpart of the `test-ci` tier that `development.yml` gates on at `enforcement: correctness`.
  Three tests fail on a machine provisioned only with the repository and a Python toolchain.

- **Observed evidence:** on 2026-10-31, in a clean checkout at `90114787db`, `pytest -q` reported 3 failed, 271 passed, each failure a missing executable or package rather than a wrong assertion:
  `test_static_site.py::test_a_search_excerpt_is_never_cut_inside_mathematics` runs `node -e`, and the VM has no `node`;
  `test_display_math.py::test_a_commutative_diagram_is_a_block_not_a_paragraph` and `test_card_git_validation.py::test_staged_header_errors_cannot_be_hidden_by_a_valid_worktree` compile a `tikzcd` block through `~/.pandoc/filters/tikzcd.lua`, which needs the pandoc-config clone, `pdf2svg`, and the two TeX packages `dzg-preamble` loads beyond a basic scheme (`bbm`, `luahyperbolic`).
  `ci/_ci-setup` covers only the pandoc-config clone, `pdf2svg`, and a scheme-full TeX Live, and relies on the runner's preinstalled Node.

- **Impact and owner:** anyone verifying a card locally, and every agent session that reports the suite's state.
  The three tests are legitimate gates — they catch a search excerpt cut inside mathematics and a diagram silently dropped from the page — so the repair belongs in the environment, not in the tests.

- **Uncertainty:** verified, and now repaired on this VM without touching a test: pandoc-config cloned to `$HOME/.pandoc` per `_ci-setup`; a portable Node under the project's ignored `tmp/`; a `pdf2svg` shim over `pdftocairo -svg`; and `bbm` plus `luahyperbolic` installed into `$HOME/texmf`.
  With those in place the whole suite passes, so the failures were prerequisites and not regressions.

- **Repair:** no repository change is required for CI, which already has all four.

### A glued math control word passes `qualc check`

- **Object and need:** card statements and solutions in `SRC-TEXT-HAT02`, and `qualc check`, the gate that validates every card's Markdown and mathematics.

- **Observed evidence:** while comparing §2.1's statements with the book I found four cards (`E-HAT-2.1-1`, `-2`, `-6`, `E-HAT-2.2-16`) writing the simplex vertices as the Greek letter `\nu_0` where Hatcher writes `v_0`, 114 occurrences in all.
  Renaming them exposed a second problem: TeX reads `\mapsto\nu_1` as `\mapsto` followed by `\nu_1`, but the renamed `\mapstov_1` is a single undefined control word, so the repair introduced twelve broken spans that `qualc check` accepted without complaint — it validates YAML, div structure and the Lamport filter, not whether a control word exists.
  A reader's MathJax would have shown those spans as errors.

- **Impact and owner:** any card whose mathematics contains an undefined control word; the site renders it as a MathJax error rather than failing the build.

- **Uncertainty:** verified on the four cards above, and the twelve glued spans were separated again (`\mapsto v_1` and so on).
  I did not survey the whole corpus for glued control words, so other instances may remain.

- **Repair:** the vertex symbol and the twelve spans are fixed in place.
  The check this entry said did not exist now does: `tools/check_macros.py` extracts every `\word`
  from named files and reports those in neither `vocabularies/macros.json` nor MathJax's command set.
  Run over all 14 362 tracked card files on 2026-11-02 it flagged 724 of them, all but four of them
  falsely, and the same day the checker was fixed to read the dialect the site actually supports
  rather than a widened allowlist: it now reads each card through `qualc.tex.checkable_tex`, which
  rewrites the one supported prose command `\dfn{term}` out with the pipeline's own parser
  (`mark_definienda`), blanks code spans and tikzcd environments (compiled to SVG by the emitter,
  skipped by `unrenderable_tex` too), and strips the YAML front matter exactly as
  `qualc.authoring check` does, so YAML escapes such as `"Rouch\xE9"` and note prose such as `X\C`
  are never scanned. The four residual flags were all of that last class: `\xE` in `P-BKF80-18`,
  `\O` in `P-T06Q2-2`, `\C` in `P-T17Q1-3`, `\H` in `P-AMD-MU3IE25C`, each in front matter, none
  a mathematics defect. One further refinement, same day: rendered metadata is scanned with the body,
  because the site typesets it -- `title`, `slogan` and `prompts` are Markdown per
  `model.typeset_dashes`, which preserves their `$...$` spans -- so `title: '$\undefinedword$'` on an
  otherwise valid card fails the check, while audit notes stay unscanned and the front matter is read
  through the YAML loader, so `"Rouch\xE9"` decodes before the scan. The corpus-wide run is now clean:
  0 of 14 362 files flagged, with the glued (`\mapstov_1`), undefined (`\q`) and rendered-metadata
  detections pinned by `tests/test_check_macros.py`.

### 2026-11-19: one stream's worktree refuses every other stream's commits

- **Object and need:** the local commit gate, `core.hooksPath=$HOME/.config/git/hooks`, and the QUAL-09
  check that refuses a commit when a Git worktree exists beside the clone.

- **Observed evidence:** twice during 2026-11-19 the gate refused a card commit in the one clone with
  `QUAL-09: 1 worktree(s) exist. Streams work directly on main in this clone; land the work on main, then
  remove the worktree.`, while the worktree was another stream's: `/…/repo/.scratch/wt-fix156` (detached at
  `c7a14c9d89`), then `/…/repo/.scratch/wt-t2` (whose HEAD moved from `49014de8e8` to `9dc06d309a` while it
  was observed, so that stream was live), then `/…/repo/.scratch/t2b` (detached at `eb9273cd7a`). The second
  refusal cleared only when that stream removed its worktree, about twenty minutes later; the card that was
  blocked (`P-APAS26E`) was staged, complete and green on every per-card check throughout.

- **Impact and owner:** every stream that shares this clone, not only the one that owns the worktree. A
  commit that creates no worktree and touches no worktree is refused for the duration, so a lane's finished
  card waits on another lane's working state. It also invites the wrong repair: the two visible ways out are
  deleting someone else's worktree, which destroys their uncommitted work, and `--no-verify`, which skips the
  checks the same hook exists to run.

- **Uncertainty:** the three refusals are exact quotations and the worktree paths and SHAs are read from
  `git worktree list`; what is not established is whether the affected stream knew its worktree blocked
  others. Not checked: whether the hook's author intended the check to be clone-wide rather than per-committer.

- **Repair:** none applied, and none should be applied from a card lane. The narrow fix is to refuse a commit
  only for the worktree's own owner, or to make the check a warning once the committing index contains no
  path inside a worktree. What a lane can do meanwhile is what was done: retry the commit rather than remove
  another stream's tree or bypass the gate, and record the block here so the next lane does not mistake it
  for a defect in its own card.

## Queue head passed over, not blocked

- **Object and need:** `E-SS10.PR-6` ("Eight squares from an Eisenstein series"), the first card in
  `queues/C-unsolved-cards.md`. It asks for a six-part proof that `r_8(n) = 16 σ_3^*(n)`, passing
  through `θ(τ)^8 = 48π^{-4} E_4^*(τ)`, the identity `E_4^* = E_4 - 2^{-4}E_4((τ-1)/2)`, the
  periodicity `E_4^*(τ+2) = E_4^*(τ)`, the transformation law `E_4^*(τ) = τ^{-4}E_4^*(-1/τ)`, and two
  asymptotic statements.

- **Observed evidence:** the prerequisite is present. The book is in the repository at
  `assets/attachments/Stein-Shakarchi-Complex-Analysis.pdf` (398 pages), and Chapter 10
  "Applications of Theta Functions" begins at the page whose text is extracted in this session, so the
  card is **not** covered by the standing "source PDFs are not in the repository" note that applies to
  the `ad-text-*` reading nodes. While checking the statement I verified part (b) outright: with
  `l = m`, `k = 2n - m`, the substitution `n + m(τ-1)/2 = ((2n-m) + mτ)/2` is a bijection from
  `Z^2 \ {0}` onto the pairs `k ≡ l (mod 2)`, not both zero, so `2^{-4}E_4((τ-1)/2)` is the sum over
  the *same*-parity pairs and `E_4^*`, the sum over opposite-parity pairs, is the difference. Part (c)
  is the same substitution `(m,n) ↦ (m, n+2m)`.

- **Impact and owner:** the queue's head remains unsolved. I did not attempt the full six-part
  write-up in this pass, and this entry exists so that the pass-over is on the record as a choice
  rather than as a blocked prerequisite. It is not a claim that the card is hard for anyone in
  particular, and it is not a deferral granted by the queue.

- **Uncertainty:** verified — parts (b) and (c) as above, and that the source is present. Not
  established: whether parts (a), (d), (e), (f) follow entirely from Chapter 10 as developed there.
  In particular (d) does **not** follow from the modularity `E_4(-1/τ) = τ^4 E_4(τ)` alone, since
  `-(τ+1)/(2τ)` is not `γτ` for any `γ ∈ SL_2(Z)` (matching coefficients forces `d = 0`, `c = 2b`,
  hence `det = -2b^2 ≠ 1`); it has to come from `θ(-1/τ)^8 = τ^4 θ(τ)^8` together with (a). That is
  the structure I would expect, but I did not carry it through.

- **Repair:** **resolved on 2026-11-01.** The card is solved: all six parts are proved and then
  assembled through the book's own maximum-principle criterion (Chapter 10, Theorem 3.4), and the
  identity is checked numerically for $n\le8$ by brute force. The paragraph above is kept because
  its structural observation stands and was used: part (d) cannot be obtained from the modularity of
  $E_4$ alone, and in the solution it is proved directly from the defining series by the bijection
  $(m,n)\mapsto(n,-m)$, which needs no modularity at all. The next card in this queue was `E-SS2.PR-5`,
  also now solved.

## 2026-11-19: the `P-AGH467MULTISECANTS` citation item closes with the page read, and steps `s1`--`s13` are re-derived

The removed head recorded that the card's step `#tangent-char-zero` used Kaji's theorem on tangentially degenerate curves through a DOI, that the statement and hypotheses had not been checked against the paper, and that steps `s1`--`s13` had not been re-derived. The citation half was closed on 2026-11-02, as the retained record below states: the step cites the restatement actually read, Fukasawa, arXiv:2108.00650v3, §1. What that record could not give was a page, and what it left open was the re-derivation.

Both are now done. The preprint was fetched again for this commit and read at p. 1, where §1 stands: the definition — "An irreducible projective curve $C\subset\PP^N$ with $N\ge3$ not contained in any plane over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p\ge0$ is said to be tangentially degenerate if $(T_PC\smallsetminus\{P\})\cap C\ne\varnothing$ for a general point $P\in C$" — and, two sentences later, "For the case where $p=0$ and the morphism $X\to\PP^N$ induced by the normalization $\phi\colon X\to C$ is unramified, the nonexistence of such curves was proved by Kaji [6] in 1986". The card's step now cites §1 by page, and the three hypotheses it lists are the ones those sentences require: $N=3$, an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, $X$ nonplanar, and $X$ smooth so that its normalization is an isomorphism and hence unramified.

Steps `s1`--`s13` were re-derived in this pass and stand as written: the line and the conic by Bézout; the twisted cubic and the elliptic quartic by the sections of $\OO_\ell(2)$ vanishing on a subscheme of length three, the first with the quadrics generating a projectively normal curve's ideal and the second with $X=Q_1\cap Q_2$; the planar case by a general line in the plane; the projection from a point off the two finite bad loci, its line bundle $H-P$, base-point freeness at $P$ from a plane not containing $T_PX$, separation of points and of tangent vectors from the choices made in `s5`; the closed immersion and $\pi_P^*\OO_{\PP^2}(1)=\OO_X(H-P)$ of degree $d-1$; the plane-curve genus formula; and the two Castelnuovo comparisons, which multiply out to $(d-2)(d-4)\le0$ for even $d$ and $(d-3)^2\le0$ for odd $d$, forcing $d=4$ and $d=3$. No step required repair.

What remains open on the card, unchanged: the body of Kaji, J. London Math. Soc. (2) **33** (1986) 430--440, kept as the primary reference and not claimed to have been read. It is a citation step in that sense and no longer in the sense of an unchecked restatement. The numbered item at the end of this file that records the 2026-11-02 closure still says steps `s1`--`s13` are not re-derived; that clause is superseded here rather than edited there (QUAL-11).

**Closed 2026-11-02.** The citation is now to the source consulted — Fukasawa, arXiv:2108.00650v3, §1 — whose hypotheses were checked against the step; the primary reference is kept as an alternate and is not claimed to have been read. See item 4 of the numbered list at the end of this file.

   Rademacher's theorem. §4 of that card now states the exact formula with Dedekind-sum coefficients,
   his remainder bound ($|A_k^*(n)|<2k^{1/3}$, remainder $O(n^{-1/4})$ uniformly for
   $N\ge\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor$), and cites Rademacher, PNAS **23** (1937) 78–84
   (doi:10.1073/pnas.23.2.78) and Trans. AMS **43** (1938) 271–295 (doi:10.2307/1990043), with Lehmer,
   J. London Math. Soc. **12** (1937) 171–176 for the divergence of the Hardy–Ramanujan series. It
   distinguishes the three series explicitly: the asymptotic one with $N$ coupled to $n$ (divergent to
   infinity), Rademacher's with $N$ decoupled (convergent, equal to $p(n)$), and the book's single-term
   shape whose coefficient is constant only at $q=1$. Checked: the $q=1$ reduction to the book's
   Theorem 4.1(ii), and the finite check that truncating at $N=\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor$ and rounding gives
   $p(n)$ for $n\le12$. **Not claimed:** a re-proof of Rademacher's theorem — that is the book's
   omission, and it is cited, not reproduced.

   `tmp/sources/hatcher-2002-algebraic-topology.pdf`, and that page was read for each one. What the six
   prove: (4) quotients of divisible groups are divisible, roots give a map $\QQ\to G$ with
   $1\mapsto g$, $G$ is a quotient of $\bigoplus_I\QQ$, and $\operatorname{Ext}(A,\QQ)=0$ with
   $\operatorname{Ext}$ turning $\bigoplus$ in its second variable into $\prod$ gives
   $\operatorname{Ext}(A,G)=0$; (5) the cokernel of $\operatorname{Hom}(A,\QQ)\to
   \operatorname{Hom}(A,\QQ/\ZZ)$ is $\operatorname{Ext}(A,\ZZ)$ by the long exact sequence, and for
   $\ZZ_{p^\infty}$ the second Hom is $\operatorname{End}=\varprojlim\ZZ/p^n$; (6) the standard free
   resolution with $d(r_0)=pe_1$, $d(r_n)=pe_{n+1}-e_n$ has kernel the image, and the dual sends
   $(a_n)\mapsto(0,-a_1,-a_2,\dots)$ because $p=0$ in $\ZZ_p$, whose cokernel is $\ZZ_p$; (7) the free
   presentation, the two-stage Moore complexes, the quotient $M(B,n)/M(A,n)$ with the homology of
   $M(C,n)$, the universal coefficient theorem and the pair's long exact sequence give the six-term
   sequence; (8) the universal coefficient theorem puts $\operatorname{Hom}$ and $\operatorname{Ext}$ in
   degrees $n$ and $n+1$ only, and the coefficient sequence's other terms vanish; (9) the two long exact
   sequences spliced at $\operatorname{Ext}(pA,\ZZ)$ give the displayed sequence, whose label $p$ is the
   composite through that term, and writing the composite as one map loses no exactness, since the kernel
   and the image of the composite are exactly what exactness at the two copies of
   $\operatorname{Ext}(A,\ZZ)$ computes.

   **Trap for the next reader of exercise 4.** The text version

   The card's "if and only if" is the book's, and the OCR of the text version dropped the "f". It must
