### §V.2 of `SRC-TEXT-HART77`: four cards still have no complete published solution, and two more have a partial one

**Object and need.** Ten requests in `SRC-TEXT-HART77` §V.2 were proved on their cards without a complete published argument to check them against, and the per-card bullets below record where each now stands; the ten were: `P-AGH521BASEUNIQUE` (V.2.1, printed p. 383), `P-AGH522DECOMPSECT` (V.2.2, p. 383), `P-AGH523SUCCEXT` (V.2.3, pp. 383--384), `P-AGH525INVARIANTE` (V.2.5(a) and (c), p. 384), `P-AGH528STABLEBUNDLE` (V.2.8(c), p. 384), `P-AGH5210CANONSCROLL` (V.2.10, p. 385), `P-AGH5212ELLRULEDAMPLE` (V.2.12, p. 385), `P-AGH5213ELLSCROLL` (V.2.13, p. 385), `P-AGH5215FROBENIUSRULED` (V.2.15(c), p. 385) and `P-AGH5217CONORMALSPLIT` (V.2.17, p. 386).

**Observed evidence.** For Chapter V the retained sets are Andrew Egbert, *Solutions to Hartshorne's Algebraic Geometry* (October 3, 2013), PDF pp. 261--273 for §V.2, and Jinhyun Park's *Algebraic Geometry by Robin Hartshorne, Exercises solutions*, whose Chapter V is §V.5 alone and begins at the section cover page after his §IV.1; Borcherds, Cais, Cutrone--Marshburn, Kim, Lomont, Okamoto, Saglam--Chris, Sam, Stein and Troiani have no Chapter V. What Egbert has: V.2.1 is two lines, "Suppose that $C_0\times\PP^1\cong X\cong C_1\times\PP^1$. But two curves which are birational are isomorphic", asserting rather than proving the birationality of the bases; V.2.2 is the citation "Marumaye, Remark 1.20"; V.2.3(a) is the citation "Miyanishi, Algebraic Geometry Lemma 12.1", and his adjacent Chern-class computation is for the tangent bundle $T_{\PP^2}$ ($d_1+d_2=3$, $d_1d_2=3$, discriminant $-3$) rather than the sheaf of differentials the exercise names; V.2.5(a) ends "This is F,P thm 4.12.4" and (c) is "given by 3.13 in Maruyama"; V.2.8(c) runs a Harder--Narasimhan filtration, cites Potier for uniqueness, and concludes "Since the filtration was unique we have this up to isomorphism" without noticing that the maximal destabilizing subbundle, and hence the tensor twist, is not part of the data; V.2.10 is "See example 2.10 in Kollar's Complex Algebraic Geometry"; V.2.12 is "This is Fuentes, Pedreira Prop 1.3" and "Fuentes, Predeira prop 1.4"; V.2.13's dimension count reads $h^0=2n-1=d-1$, dropping $e$; V.2.15(c) is "To see the curve $Y\equiv3C_0-3f$ is inseparable is Miyanishi, *Open Algebraic Surfaces*, lemma 2.5.2.2"; V.2.17 is entered as "starred" with no argument. Fuentes--Pedreira, Maruyama, Miyanishi and Kollár are not among the retained files.

**Impact and owner.** The cards keep complete proofs: V.2.1 descends through the generic $\PP^1$-fibre and recovers inverse birational maps of the bases; V.2.2 compares the kernel line bundles of the two quotient sections fibrewise; V.2.3 filters a rank-$r$ bundle by saturation of a generic section; V.2.5(a) uses $H^1(\OO_C(K_C-A))^\vee\cong H^0(\OO_C(A))\ne0$ and (c) counts the bad extension classes in $\PP H^1(\OO_C(-D))$ as at most $2d-3$ against $g+d-2$; V.2.8(c) classifies up to tensor equivalence; V.2.10 constructs the canonical curve as $D=H-K_X\sim3C_0+(n+e+2)f$; V.2.12 handles $e\ge0$ and the exceptional $e=-1$ separately, the latter through the stability of a normalized bundle of degree one; V.2.13 gets $h^0=2n-e=d$ and the scroll in $\PP^{d-1}$; V.2.15(c) builds $Y$ from the splitting of $f^*\mathcal E$; V.2.17 computes the extension class $(n-1)\eta$ of the conormal sequence and reproduces the book's printed answers $-5$, $-7$ and $(-6,-8)$ in characteristic $2$. Two of these cards also carry a defect in the printed text, recorded on the card: V.2.8(c)'s "up to isomorphism" fails because $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal A$ with $\deg\mathcal A\ne0$ carry the same triple $(e,\mathcal L,\xi)$ and have different determinants, and V.2.15(c)'s "nonsingular" fails because adjunction gives $p_a(3C_0-3f)=4$ while a purely inseparable degree-three cover of the genus-three curve has genus $3$.

**Uncertainty.** Searched: all twelve retained Hartshorne solution files in `tmp/sources` by `pdftotext -layout` extraction --- Borcherds, Cais, Cutrone--Marshburn, Egbert, Kim, Lomont, Okamoto, Park, Saglam--Chris, Sam, Stein, Troiani --- and `assets/attachments/Hartshorne_Solutions.pdf`, the Cais notes. The Chapter V occurrences in Cutrone--Marshburn, Kim, Saglam--Chris and Lomont are all in Chapter II material on blowing up, with one cross-reference to "geometrically ruled surface (V, §2)" in Kim. Conclusion: no complete published solution for the ten requests above. Confidence: high for these sets. Gaps: a published treatment may exist outside them.

**Located sources.** Algebraic Geometry II, National Taiwan University, 2020 Spring (course of Chin-Lung Wang), *Chapter V Surfaces* homework, in `tmp/sources/ntu-ag2-chapter5.md` beside its PDF, covers five of the ten with arguments: V.2.1 (Exercise 1 of §2, PDF p. 5), V.2.2 (Exercise 2, PDF pp. 5--6), V.2.3 (Exercise 3, PDF p. 6), V.2.8 (Exercise 8, PDF p. 8, whose (c) is a citation to the proof of 2.12), V.2.10 (Exercise 10, PDF p. 8), and it has no entry for V.2.5, V.2.12, V.2.13, V.2.15 or V.2.17. Yang Pi-Yeh, *Hartshorne Solutions* (`tmp/sources/lfwin-hartshorne-solutions.pdf`, 2019), gives printed pp. 101--107: V.2.1 by $K(X)=L(x)$ (which assumes what the exercise proves), V.2.2 by two assertions, V.2.3 with a sign error in (b), V.2.5 with an invalid inference from nonnegative degree in (a), V.2.8 repeating the printed "up to isomorphism", V.2.10 without nonsingularity or canonicity, V.2.12 with garbled $e=-1$ computations, V.2.13 correctly, V.2.15 with the (a) computation and garbled (b) and (c), and V.2.17 by the Jacobian presentation but with characteristic 3 wrongly added to the split case. The cards now record, per exercise, which published argument exists and where it fails; V.2.4, V.2.6, V.2.7, V.2.9, V.2.11 and V.2.14, whose Egbert entries are complete, were not in this batch.



**Searched outside the retained sets (2026-11-16).** Two further published sources were read for this batch. Luis Fuentes and Manuel Pedreira, *The Projective Theory of Ruled Surfaces*, arXiv:math/0006204v3 (2002), was saved whole as `tmp/sources/projective-theory-ruled-surfaces.pdf`; its §2 proves base-point and very-ampleness criteria for the linear system of $C_0+\mfb f$ and its §3 treats decomposable ruled surfaces. Math StackExchange threads were read through the API and are cited below by question and answer id. Per card:

- V.2.1. Fuentes--Pedreira Proposition 1.7, printed p. 5, builds the incidence variety of a linearly normal scroll and concludes that the scroll determines its ruled surface; that is uniqueness of the ruling of an embedded scroll, not the birational uniqueness this exercise asks for, so it does not reach the exercise. Math StackExchange question 1715815, saved whole as `tmp/sources/mse-1715815-hart77-v21-uniqueness-of-ruling.md`, asks the isomorphism form --- if $C_1\times\PP^1\cong C_2\times\PP^1$, show $C_1\cong C_2$ --- which is strictly weaker than the birational statement here. It has no answer and four comments, the saved file now holding all of them: Mohan's sketch through $C_1\times\{p\}\to C_2$, with the genus read off $h^1$ of the product, the rational case, Hurwitz for genus above one, and a remark that genus one needs an extra argument; the poster's question whether that last step is Hurwitz's theorem; Mohan's confirmation that it is; and Takumi Murayama's pointers to Ohm following Nagata and to Deveney, with his remark that Mohan's argument covers the birational case too. The Ohm and Deveney pointers are Murayama's and not Mohan's, which is the one thing the earlier record got wrong; that the thread is a sketch in a comment and not a published argument stands, so the published argument remains the National Taiwan University set's. Chao Li's Columbia notes, "Enriques classification of complex algebraic surfaces", were read as well: Theorem 7 and its proof show that every minimal model of $C\times\PP^1$ with $C$ irrational is geometrically ruled over $C$, which recovers the base from a minimal model but never states that $C$ is determined by the birational class. The complete published argument is the National Taiwan University set's Exercise 1 of §2, printed p. 5, whose two cases are steps `s2` to `s4` of the card; its last case, "if $C=\PP^1$ then $\widetilde f$ is a constant, which means $f$ is a constant, a contradiction", is valid, and the earlier record that it was invalid is withdrawn: a constant $\widetilde f$ confines the image of the birational map to one fibre of $p'$, a curve.
- V.2.2. Fuentes--Pedreira Remark 3.3, printed p. 15, is the conclusion in one sentence, two disjoint unisecant curves coming from the two summands, with neither direction proved; its Theorem 3.2, printed p. 15, cites the book's Theorem V.2.12 and Nagata and concerns only the possible values of $e$. The National Taiwan University set is a complete published treatment of both directions, but it is not the card's argument: it reads $\Rightarrow$ off $C_1\cdot C_2=0$ and $\Leftarrow$ off $\pi^*$ with the flatness and surjectivity of $\pi$, where steps `s1` and `s3` of the card use the fibres of $\mathcal E$ and the determinant.
- V.2.3. Nothing in Fuentes--Pedreira. The book's own Corollary V.2.7, printed p. 372 (PDF p. 387), proves the rank-two case of (a) completely, and Remark V.2.7.1 on the same printed page sends the general rank to this exercise. Part (b) does have a complete published argument, the National Taiwan University set's Exercise 3 of §2, printed p. 6: an extension $0\to\OO(n)\to\Omega\to\OO(m)\to0$ forces $H^1(\PP^2,\Omega)=0$ by III.5.1(b), printed p. 225, against $H^1(\PP^2,\Omega)\cong k$ from the Euler sequence. Steps `s3` and `s4` of the card are its own Chern-class route to the same contradiction; step `s1` is likewise its own, starting from $\mathcal E(n)$ rather than the set's $\mathcal E^\vee(n)$.
- V.2.5. Fuentes--Pedreira Theorem 3.2, printed p. 15, restates the book's Theorem V.2.12, printed p. 376, with a sharper lower bound: the book prints $e\ge0$ in the decomposable case and $-2g\le e\le2g-2$ in the indecomposable one, which is what its own proof yields, and sends the sharper $e\ge-g$ to its Exercise V.2.5, whose Note attributes it to Nagata [8]; the paper states the sharper bound and cites the book and Nagata for it. It says nothing about existence for every $e$ with $0\le e\le2g-2$, which is (a), nor about the range $-g\le e<0$, which is (c). Its Theorem 4.12(4), printed pp. 31--32, which Egbert cites for (a), is the paper's only construction of an indecomposable ruled surface: an elementary transformation of a decomposable surface at a point off $X_0$ and $X_1$, over a base point $P$ of the linear system of $-\mfe$, gives an indecomposable surface with invariant $e-1$. Applied once to the decomposable surface of invariant $e+1$, which exists for every $e\ge0$ by the book's Theorem V.2.12(a), it returns an indecomposable surface of invariant $e$, so no iteration is needed and the theorem covers every $0\le e\le2g-2$ as soon as a base point $P$ is produced; the paper leaves that to the reader, and it is available whenever $h^0(-\mfe)=1$, the system then having the single member $-\mfe$ whose support is its base locus. Part (a) therefore has a published argument modulo that one condition, and the card's steps `s1` to `s4` prove it without any condition. Math StackExchange question 4398506, saved as `tmp/sources/mse-4398506-hart77-v25-linear-system-notation.md`, concerns only the notation $\linearsystem{D+K-E}+E$ of part (b). No complete published argument for (c). Part (d) is open in this entry and is not proved on the card, whose step `s15` records the printed Note and the reference to Nagata rather than deriving the bound, the book's own argument reaching only $e\ge-2g$, that is $e\ge-4$ at $g=2$: it needs Nagata's $e\ge-g$, which the printed Note, Fuentes--Pedreira's introduction and its Theorem 3.2(2) all attribute to M. Nagata, "On self-intersection number of a section on a ruled surface", Nagoya Math. J. 37 (1970), 191--196 --- Hartshorne's own reference [8] and Fuentes--Pedreira's [15] --- and that paper was not read: Project Euclid serves an automated-access check for its PDF and Cambridge Core holds it for subscribers. An attempt to download it produced `tmp/sources/nagata-1970-self-intersection-section-ruled-surface.pdf`, which is not the paper --- it is 1157 bytes of Incapsula access-check HTML served under a .pdf name --- and no card cites that file. Step `s15` therefore rests on the printed Note and on two secondary statements of the bound.
- V.2.8(c). Nothing in Fuentes--Pedreira on stability of locally free sheaves on a curve. The printed "up to isomorphism" stays defective as recorded on the card.
- V.2.10. Fuentes--Pedreira §2 and §3 give criteria for the system of $C_0+\mfb f$ and never place a canonical curve on the rational scroll. Their §5 and §6 introduce "canonical surfaces" and "canonical scrolls" in the sense of scrolls of speciality one, deferring the characterization to their own "Canonical geometrically ruled surfaces", reference [5], which is not retained and was not read; that is not the canonical curve inside a rational scroll asked here. A search outside the checkout for a construction returned arXiv:1502.07556 and arXiv:1803.10899, both of which begin with a trigonal curve and study its canonical model rather than constructing one; Markwig and Zheng, "Trigonal and embedded tropical curves of low genus" (arXiv:2602.02257), read in its introduction, gives the class $3E_n+((g+3n+2)/2)F_n$ of a trigonal curve of genus $g$ and Maroni invariant $n$ and likewise begins with the curve. No complete published argument.
- V.2.12. Fuentes--Pedreira Theorem 3.9(3), printed p. 18, states for a decomposable ruled surface that the system of $C_0+\mfb f$ is very ample exactly when $\mfb$ and $\mfb+\mfe$ are; for $e\ge0$ on an elliptic base that gives $\deg\mfb\ge3$ and $\deg\mfb-e\ge3$, that is the printed bound $e+3$. That theorem is a complete published argument, and its proof is one too: it rests on the paper's Corollary 2.13, printed p. 14, whose criterion is $h^0(H-(P+Q)f)=h^0(H)-4$ for all $P,Q$ in the base, and that corollary is proved --- the forward direction by Theorem 2.11, printed pp. 12--13, and the converse by Proposition 2.3, printed p. 8, applied to $|H-Pf|$: a point at which the map fails is a base point of some $|H-Pf|$ by Theorem 2.11, and Proposition 2.3 then produces $Q$ with $h^0(H-(P+Q)f)\ge h^0(H-Pf)-1=h^0(H)-3$ once $|H|$ is base-point-free. The earlier record in this file, and on the card, that the converse was an assertion and that a two-fibre condition cannot see a tangent direction transverse to a fibre is withdrawn: the case $Q=P$ is what Theorem 2.11 covers. Proposition 2.15, printed p. 15, rests on the same corollary and is sound on the same footing. What the paper leaves open is what its Section 3, being about decomposable surfaces, does not reach: the Atiyah surface $e=-1$, handled by the card's `s8` and `s9`, and the indecomposable bundles of invariant $e=0$, handled by `s7` and `s10` through the book's Exercise V.2.11(b), which needs no decomposability.
- V.2.13. Fuentes--Pedreira's introduction cites the classification of elliptic scrolls of Corrado Segre, its reference [17] --- Segre, Ricerche sulle rigate ellittiche di qualunque ordine, Atti Acc. Torino 21 (1885), 868--891, not retained and not read --- and says that that classification does not follow directly from the very-ampleness criterion. The paper's own reference [4], the authors' "The classification of elliptic scrolls", appears only in its bibliography and is never cited in its text. What the paper does settle is every $e\ge0$ on a decomposable surface: Theorem 3.2(1), printed p. 15 (every $e\ge0$ occurs), Theorem 3.9(3), printed p. 18 (very ampleness), and Theorem 3.10(1), printed p. 19 ($N=h^0(\mfb)+h^0(\mfb+\mfe)-1$, degree $2\deg\mfb-e$). Only $e=-1$, the Atiyah surface, is open there, its bundles being indecomposable; the card's `s1` and its `s3` to `s7` carry that case, and Yang Pi-Yeh's count agrees with the card's.
- V.2.15(c). Fuentes--Pedreira carries no Frobenius statement. Question 4553266, saved as `tmp/sources/mse-4553266-hart77-v215c-genus-inseparable.md`, asks for the genus of exactly the curve of (c) and has no answer. Miyanishi, *Open Algebraic Surfaces*, Lemma 2.5.2.2, carried by Egbert's entry, is not retained and was not read. No complete published argument, and the defect of the printed "nonsingular" recorded on the card stands.
- V.2.17. Part (a) has a complete published argument: Math StackExchange answer 1583486 by Ted Shifrin, to question 1583326, in `tmp/sources/mse-1583326-hart77-v217-twisted-cubic-normal-bundle.md`, computes the conormal bundle of the twisted cubic by transition functions in the two charts and reads off $\OO(-5)\oplus\OO(-5)$; the transition matrix, the change of coordinates its answer leaves to the reader, and its reduction to $t^{-5}$ times the identity are now carried in step `s5` of the card. Equivalently the normal bundle is $\OO(5)\oplus\OO(5)$, which answer 569653 to question 569237, in `tmp/sources/mse-569237-hart77-v217-twisted-cubic-normal-bundle-2.md`, records as Proposition 6 of Eisenbud and Van de Ven. Answer 2664944 to question 2664333, in `tmp/sources/mse-2664333-hart77-v217-conormal-sheaf-twisted-cubic.md`, reaches the conormal sequence and the Jacobian matrix and stops at "it is easy to check that the conormal sheaf is $\OO(-5)$ squared", which the degree does not give, since $4(-3)-2(-1)=-10$ admits $\OO(-4)\oplus\OO(-6)$ as well. No published treatment of (b) or of its characteristic-two answer was located, and steps `s2` and `s3` remain the card's own general computation for both parts.

**Where this batch stands.** Complete published arguments are now recorded on six of the ten, and on part (a) alone of a seventh: V.2.1 through the National Taiwan University set, whose last case is valid; V.2.2 and V.2.3 through that set, by routes other than the cards' own; V.2.12 and V.2.13 through Fuentes--Pedreira for every $e\ge0$ on a decomposable surface, whose Theorem 3.9(3) and Corollary 2.13 are complete; and V.2.17 on part (a) through the two Stack Exchange answers. Two of these are partial: V.2.12 leaves the Atiyah surface $e=-1$ and the indecomposable bundles of invariant $e=0$ outside the published argument, and V.2.13 leaves $e=-1$ outside it, both of which the cards' own steps supply. The four without a complete published argument are V.2.5, whose (a) the paper gives only up to the base point its own theorem asks for and which the card proves outright, whose (c) is the card's, and whose (d) rests on Nagata's paper, unread; V.2.8(c), whose printed "up to isomorphism" is defective; V.2.10, where Fuentes--Pedreira's canonical surfaces are not the canonical curve inside a rational scroll; and V.2.15(c), whose printed "nonsingular" is defective.


**Repair.** Discharged for V.2.1, V.2.2, V.2.3, V.2.12, V.2.13 and V.2.17(a) on the arguments recorded above, with the two partial closures stated on the cards. V.2.5, V.2.8(c), V.2.10 and V.2.15(c) still need a complete published argument, and V.2.5(d) needs Nagata's paper itself, which is behind an automated-access check at Project Euclid and a subscription at Cambridge Core; the card records the bound and lists the part open.

**2026-11-16, §V.2: V.2.5 and V.2.10 close on published statements, V.2.8(c) on Gunning's Theorem 14, and the parts left open are named.** Seven sources named for this batch were read in their text versions on 2026-11-16 and transcribed onto the cards with the numbered statement and printed page of each step. V.2.5: part (a) is Gunning, *Lectures on vector bundles over Riemann surfaces*, Theorem 13, printed pp. 71--74 (extension classes are a first cohomology group, and the split extension is the zero class), and Theorem 14, printed pp. 87--90 (the indecomposable bundles with a given subbundle $\varphi$ and determinant $\xi$ are parametrized by $\PP H^1(C,\OO(\varphi^2\xi^{-1}))$), with the duality half of the book's proof of Theorem 2.12, printed p. 376, for the nonvanishing of $H^1(C,\mathcal L^{-1})$ at $\varphi=\OO_C$; part (b) is Proposition 1.1, printed p. 57, and Lemma 2.3, printed pp. 58--59, of Lange and Narasimhan, *Maximal subbundles of rank two vector bundles on curves*, Math. Ann. 266, whose criterion is the kernel of the canonical map $H^0(K_C\otimes L)^*\to H^0(K_C\otimes L(-D))^*$ in both directions, the same square the book's proof of Theorem 2.15, printed pp. 377--379, runs in one direction, and the printed "Cf. proof of (2.15)" points at; part (c) is their Corollary 1.2, printed p. 58, applied to line bundles of degrees $d$ and $2d$ with $d=-e$, since twisting by the inverse of the extension's subbundle returns a normalized bundle with determinant of degree $d$, with Example 2.11.6, printed p. 375, and Theorem 2.15 for genus one; and part (d) is Lange, *Higher secant varieties of curves and the theorem of Nagata on ruled surfaces*, Manuscripta Math. 47 (1984), §2 Theorem $s(E)\le g$, printed pp. 267--268, on the dimension theorem of §1, printed p. 266: for a normalized bundle $s(E)=\deg\det E=-e$, so $e\ge-g$ and $e\ge-2$ at $g=2$. That replaces the unread Nagata paper, which the printed Note and Fuentes--Pedreira both cite for the same bound. What stays open in part (d): the paper's proof reduces at its start to extensions whose quotient has degree $d>3$ and does not argue the reduction, while its §1 needs only $d\ge2$ when $g\ge2$. V.2.8(c): Gunning's §(c), printed pp. 82--83, Lemma 14, printed pp. 81--82, Lemma 15, printed pp. 83--85, and Theorem 14, printed pp. 87--90, are the stability criterion, the decomposable case, the uniqueness of the maximal subbundle and the classification with $\varphi=\OO_C$; the bound $0<e\le2g-2$ is the argument of the book's Theorem 2.12, printed p. 376. The printed "up to isomorphism" of the exercise remains defective, and the card classifies tensor-equivalence classes in terms of the printed data. V.2.10: Hartshorne's own Corollary 2.18(b), printed p. 380, states that $\linearsystem{D}$ contains an irreducible nonsingular curve exactly when $a>0$ and $b>ae$, or $e>0,a>0,b=ae$, and so covers $D=H-K_X=3C_0+(n+e+2)f$ under exactly the hypothesis $n\ge2e-2$ the exercise imposes; the proof of Corollary 2.19, printed p. 380, is the count $h^0(\OO_X(H))=2n-e+2$; and Reid, *Chapters on Algebraic surfaces*, §2.8 Theorem with (2.8.1), printed p. 19, §2.9, printed p. 20, and §2.10, printed pp. 20--21, give the class $\alpha A+3B$ with $\alpha=a+a_2+2$, the criterion $\alpha-3a=B\cdot(\alpha A+3B)\ge0$, and the Maroni inequality $3a\le g+2$ that is the same condition. The one step of that card not stated in either source is the restriction isomorphism $H^0(\OO_X(H))\cong H^0(Y,K_Y)$, which it assembles from the book's count with $H^0(\OO_X(K_X))=H^1(\OO_X(K_X))=0$. V.2.15(c) is untouched by this batch and stays open as recorded above.

**2026-11-16, §V.2, corrected: V.2.5(d) closes, V.2.5(b) and (c) gain the hypotheses of the statements they quote, and four records above are corrected.** Corrections of this round. (1) Hartshorne's Corollary 2.19 and its proof are on printed p. 381, not p. 380; the record above names p. 380 twice, and Corollary 2.18(b) keeps p. 380. (2) The adjunction formula in the V.2.10 card is Proposition V.1.5, printed p. 361, stated for a nonsingular curve, which is what the member $Y$ is; Theorem V.1.3 is the definition of the intersection number on printed p. 358. V.2.10 is unchanged in substance: its restriction isomorphism $H^0(\OO_X(H))\cong H^0(Y,K_Y)$ remains the card's own assembly of the book's count with $H^0(\OO_X(K_X))=H^1(\OO_X(K_X))=0$, and has no published statement behind it.

### §V.3 of `SRC-TEXT-HART77`: six cards have no complete published solution

**Object and need.** Six requests in `SRC-TEXT-HART77` §V.3 are proved on their cards without a complete published argument to check them against: `P-AGH531PABLOWUP` (V.3.1, printed p. 394), `P-AGH534MULTLOCRING` (V.3.4(d) and (e), p. 394), `P-AGH535HYPERELLGENUS` (V.3.5, p. 394, the request to compute $\delta_P$), `P-AGH536ANALYTICEQUIV` (V.3.6, p. 395), `P-AGH537EMBRESOLUTION` (V.3.7, p. 395) and `P-AGH538INEQUIVSING` (V.3.8, p. 395).

**Observed evidence.** Andrew Egbert, *Solutions to Hartshorne's Algebraic Geometry* (October 3, 2013), PDF pp. 273--284 for §V.3, is the only retained set that reaches the section; Park's Chapter V is §V.5 alone, and the other ten retained sets stop before Chapter V. What Egbert has: V.3.1 is "This follows from 3.4", and result (3.4) is the monoidal case, a point centre, while the exercise blows up a subvariety of any codimension; V.3.4(d) is an unfinished attempt with a worked example $k[x,y]/(y^7-x^9)$ and no general argument, and V.3.4(e) is "See Mumford, Algebraic Geometry 1, Proposition 5.11"; V.3.5 checks the singularity at infinity and counts genus by Riemann--Hurwitz branch points but never computes $\delta_P$, which the exercise asks for; V.3.6 is "See Wall's, *Singular Points of Plane Curves*" for both halves, with the pair $y^3+x^7$ and $y^3+x^5y+x^7$ asserted equisingular but not analytically isomorphic; V.3.7 is a Singular session printing chart trees, with $\delta_P$ absent and the equivalence check left at "these commands should show that (d) is not equivalent"; V.3.8 says "the configuration of infinitely near singular points can be seen as in 3.7", asserts it rather than computing it, and observes only that (a) needs three charts and (b) four. Wall's book and Mumford's red book are not among the retained files.

**Impact and owner.** The cards keep complete proofs: V.3.1 reduces to $R^j\pi_*\OO_{\widetilde X}=0$ for a projective birational morphism of regular schemes (Chatzistamatiou--Rülling, Compositio Math. 151 (2015) 2131--2144, Theorem 1.1); V.3.4(d) computes $\length(\OO_{C,P}/\mathfrak m^l)=rl-r(r-1)/2$ from $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m_C}\OO_{C,P}\cong k[u,v]/(f_r)$ and (e) gets the vertex multiplicity $d$ from the Hilbert polynomial of the cone's coordinate ring; V.3.5 gets $\delta_P=\binom{r-2}{2}+\lfloor(r-2)/2\rfloor$ from the strict transform $v^{r-2}=u^2\prod(1-a_iv)$ and the $A_{r-3}$ singularity its unit factor reduces to; V.3.6 proves the forward implication from the lifting of an analytic isomorphism to a formal coordinate change, and separates the standard pair by Tjurina numbers $12$ and $11$; V.3.7 gives the embedded resolutions and $\delta_P=4,4,3,4,4$; V.3.8 computes the multiplicity sequences. Two printed defects are recorded on the card: V.3.5 is printed without the hypothesis $\operatorname{char}k\ne2$ that its last two requests need (in characteristic $2$, $y^2=f(x)$ with $f$ squarefree is a purely inseparable double cover of genus $0$), and V.3.8 is false as printed, the two germs having multiplicity sequences $4,2$ and $4,3$ and $\delta_0=7$ and $9$, so they do not have the same infinitely near multiplicities and do have different delta invariants.

**Uncertainty.** Searched: all twelve retained Hartshorne solution files in `tmp/sources` by `pdftotext -layout` extraction, plus `assets/attachments/Hartshorne_Solutions.pdf` (the Cais notes). Chapter V occurs only in Egbert (V.1--V.6) and in Park (§V.5 alone). Conclusion: no complete published solution for the six requests above. Confidence: high for these sets. Gaps: a published treatment may exist outside them.

**Located sources.** Two published Chapter V solution sets outside the twelve previously inspected cover five of the six. Algebraic Geometry II, National Taiwan University, 2020 Spring, *Chapter V Surfaces* homework, downloaded to `tmp/sources/ntu-ag2-chapter5.pdf`: Exercise 1 of §3 (PDF p. 9) attempts V.3.1 for a centre of any codimension: its formal-functions reduction is right, but the induction that follows uses $H^i(\PP^{r-1},\OO(n))=0$, the cohomology of a fibre, which is the cohomology of $E$ only when the centre is a point; Exercise 4 of §3 (PDF pp. 10--11) proves all of V.3.4, with the length computation $\length(A/\mathfrak m^n)-\length(A/\mathfrak m^{n-r})=nr-\frac{r(r-1)}2$ for (d) and the cone for (e); Exercise 5 of §3 (PDF p. 11), in characteristic not $2$, gets $\delta_P=\frac12(r-2)(r-3)+\lfloor(r-2)/2\rfloor$ and $g=\lfloor(r-1)/2\rfloor$ for V.3.5; Exercise 7 of §3 (PDF pp. 12--13) blows each germ of V.3.7 up until its strict transform is nonsingular --- twice for (a), (b), (d) and (e), once for (c) --- and stops there, drawing the incidence graph of the curves produced and never blowing up at smooth points to make the total transform normal crossings, so it settles $\delta=4,4,3,4,4$ and the classification (a),(b),(d) equivalent, (c) and (e) separate, and not the embedded resolution; Exercise 8 of §3 (PDF pp. 13--14, its (a) on p. 13 and its (b) on p. 14) gets $\delta=7$ and $9$ for V.3.8, which refutes the printed claim, and then guesses a different equation for (b). Yang Pi-Yeh, *Hartshorne Solutions* (`tmp/sources/lfwin-hartshorne-solutions.pdf`, 2019): V.3.1 at printed p. 107 assumes codimension one and is not a proof of the exercise; V.3.4 at printed pp. 107--108 identifies $\mathrm{gr}_{\mathfrak m}A$ with a polynomial ring in (b) and gives a wrong length formula in (d); V.3.5 at printed p. 108 takes $\delta=(r-2)(r-3)/2$, omitting the residual singularity; V.3.7 at printed p. 108 writes the successive strict transforms, including the further blowup at a smooth point that produces the normal crossings, and closes "So $(a),(b),(d)$ are equivalent to each other. And $(c),(e)$ are not equivalent to any others" --- so he does decide the equivalence, and what he does not do is compute $\delta$; V.3.8 at printed pp. 108--109, its (a) on p. 108 and its (b) on p. 109, asserts without computing that the two $\delta$'s are the same, which is false, and that the curves are not equivalent. V.3.6 has the forward implication at printed p. 108 by a completion argument and asserts the counterexample; its published Puiseux criterion is Wall, *Singular Points of Plane Curves*, Ch. 3, which is not available here and is cited as printed.

**State after the transcription pass of 2026-11-16.** Three of the six are closed on published proofs, transcribed onto their cards with the page. V.3.4(d),(e) on NTU Exercise 4 of §3, PDF pp. 10--11: step `curve-length-formula` is its exact sequence $0\to R/\mfm^{l-r}\to R/\mfm^l\to B/\mfm_C^l\to0$ and its length computation $nr-\frac12r(r-1)$, and the order-additivity sentence the source leaves out is supplied on the step; its display names the two maps of that sequence the wrong way round, which the step records. V.3.5 on NTU Exercise 5 of §3, PDF p. 11: steps `infinitely-near-A-singularity` and `delta-invariant-formula` are its blowup chain, with the two terminal exponents written out, and its $\frac12(r-2)(r-3)+\lfloor(r-2)/2\rfloor$ agrees with the card's independent $A_{r-3}$ route. V.3.1 is closed on a published theorem rather than on a solution set: Chatzistamatiou--Rülling, *Vanishing of the higher direct images of the structure sheaf*, Compositio Math. 151 (2015) 2131--2144, Theorem 1.1 on p. 1 of the preprint arXiv:1404.1827v2, which is the copy saved as `tmp/sources/chatzistamatiou-rulling-2015-higher-direct-images.pdf` and is the one with no text version in `tmp/sources` yet --- the page is the preprint's, and the Compositio printing was not consulted, gives $R^if_*\OO_X=0$ for $i\ge1$ under a projective birational morphism of excellent regular schemes, which is the vanishing the exercise needs for a centre of any codimension; the card's remark now also records the defect in the NTU entry, since for $Y$ positive-dimensional $E$ is a $\PP^{r-1}$-bundle over $Y$ and $H^i(E,\OO_E(n))=H^i(Y,\operatorname{Sym}^n(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2))$, which is $H^1(Y,\OO_Y)$ at $n=0$. The other three keep their own proofs. V.3.6: the forward implication is Yang's completion argument at printed p. 108, but no located source proves that the two germs are *not analytically isomorphic* --- Yang asserts it, Egbert cites Wall, and Wall's *Singular Points of Plane Curves* is not held --- so the card's Tjurina computation stays its own. V.3.7: NTU, PDF pp. 12--13, writes the first two blowups of each germ in coordinates and stops when the strict transform is nonsingular, giving the incidence graph as a picture (five `<!-- image -->` blocks in the extraction), with $\delta_P=4,4,3,4,4$ and the same classes; the intermediate blowups and the graph data are not in its text, so there is nothing to transcribe, and the card keeps its hand resolution. V.3.8: the printed assertion is false, so no published solution can exist; NTU, PDF pp. 13--14, computes $\delta=7$ and $9$ in agreement with the card and then proposes a different equation for (b), a guess the card does not adopt. A correction of 2026-11-16, on V.3.7 alone: that card cited (3.9.3) and (3.9.4) on printed p. 408, which is the PDF page, their printed page being 393, and its remark now says so; the equivalence of (a), (b) and (d) on that card rests on the embedded-resolution data of (3.9.4) and not on the formal changes of step `abd-equivalent`, which alone need 3 and 5 invertible.

**Correction, 2026-11-16, on the reader's report of #121: the text version of Chatzistamatiou--Rülling is present.** The V.3.1 sentence above said that the retained Chatzistamatiou--Rülling theorem "is the one with no text version in `tmp/sources` yet". It has one, and it was read: `tmp/sources/chatzistamatiou-rulling-2015-higher-direct-images.md` is the extraction of the retained PDF `tmp/sources/chatzistamatiou-rulling-2015-higher-direct-images.pdf`, it runs over the whole preprint from title page to references, and its first page states Theorem 1.1 --- "Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective and birational morphism between excellent and regular schemes. Then the higher direct images of $\OO_X$ under $f$ vanish, that is, $R^if_*\OO_X=0$, for all $i\ge1$" --- on PDF p. 1, the page the extraction opens with under its marker for PDF pages 1--14, which is the PDF's fourteen pages. The card's remark on the preprint page now names that file beside the PDF, and the page cited remains the preprint's p. 1; the Compositio printing, 151 (2015) 2131--2144, was still not consulted, so no page of the printed article is given. Nothing else in the V.3.1 entry changed, and the proof of Theorem 1.1 was not read.

**V.3.6 corrected 2026-11-16.** The card's conclusion of equivalence from its two point blowups was not warranted as written: after those two blowups each strict transform is nonsingular but tangent to $E_2$ with contact order $3$, so the reduced total transform is not a normal crossing divisor and the two sequences are not embedded resolutions. Step `c1-c2-equivalent` now shows that the two germs present the same pair at the last point, $x=-y^{\prime\prime 3}$ against $x=0$, the second strict transform being $x(1+y^{\prime\prime})+y^{\prime\prime 3}$ and the first $x+y^{\prime\prime 3}$, the unit $1+y^{\prime\prime}$ removed by the coordinate change $x\mapsto x(1+y^{\prime\prime})$ that fixes the line $x=0$; the chosen embedded resolution is then the same for the two germs from that point on. Remark 3.9.4 is on printed p. 393, not p. 408: in the text version `tmp/sources/hartshorne-1977-algebraic-geometry.md` it sits between the markers for PDF pages 408 and 409, while exercise 3.6 follows the marker for PDF page 410, printed p. 395. The two germs are equivalent and not analytically isomorphic, so the card's last remark now says that it is the non-isomorphism, not an inequivalence, that carries the counterexample. The Yang Pi-Yeh entry cited above is read in its text version `tmp/sources/lfwin-hartshorne-solutions.md`, exercise 5.3.6, printed p. 108, and Egbert's in `tmp/sources/hartshorne-solutions-egbert.md`, exercise V.3.6, PDF p. 279; Wall's *Singular Points of Plane Curves* is not held and is cited as printed.


**Repair.** A published proof of each, checked against the card, or the owner's direction to accept the cards' own derivations.

**Corrected for V.3.5 (2026-11-16).** The paragraph after the statement had said that a hyperelliptic curve needs a *separable* degree-two morphism and that $\PP^1$ has none; both claims are false, since $\PP^1$ carries the separable degree-two maps $z\mapsto z^2$ away from characteristic $2$ and $z\mapsto z^2+z$ in characteristic $2$, whose derivative $2z+1$ is the constant $1$, and Hartshorne IV, Ex. 1.7, printed p. 298, asks only for genus at least $2$ and a finite morphism of degree $2$. The paragraph now gives the reason that holds, that in characteristic $2$ the field $k(Y)=k(\sqrt{x-a_1})$ is rational, so the normalization is $\PP^1$ of genus $0$ and no curve of the construction meets the printed definition. Step `delta-invariant-formula` had said that the terminal germ for $e=0$ meets no point; the strict transform meets the last exceptional curve in the two points $x=1$ and $x=-1$, and both statements are corrected on the card, whose audit note of 2026-11-11 keeps the withdrawn wording as the record of that pass.

The text versions: Hartshorne is `tmp/sources/hartshorne-1977-algebraic-geometry.md`, in which printed p. $N$ is PDF p. $N+15$, so V.3.8 on printed p. 395 is PDF p. 410; NTU, Exercise 8 of §3, is `tmp/sources/ntu-ag2-chapter5.md`, whose page markers are coarse, so (a) was read on PDF p. 13 and (b) on PDF p. 14 of the PDF beside it, and it gets $\delta=7$ and $9$ and then guesses $x^4-x^2y^2-x^2y^5+y^8$ for (b), a guess the card does not adopt; Egbert, Exercise V.3.8, is `tmp/sources/hartshorne-solutions-egbert.md`, PDF p. 284, where the equality of the configurations is asserted and the chart count is three for (a) against four for (b). Yang Pi-Yeh, Solution 5.3.8 in `tmp/sources/lfwin-hartshorne-solutions.md`, printed pp. 108--109, its (a) on p. 108 and its (b) on p. 109, blows up both germs, records multiplicity $2$ and then $3$, and concludes "So on these two curves, $\delta_{(0,0)}$ are the same", an equality computed nowhere in his entry and false for the printed equations; the card now records that entry. The card's note of 2026-11-11 gives "Example 3.9.3 on printed page 408"; the printed page is 393 and 408 is the PDF page, so the body now gives printed p. 393 where it cites (3.9.4), and that note is left as written. The card's note of 2026-10-29 had been rewritten and is restored to the text it was dated with; the statement it had been given, that the exercise had been changed to "Prove or disprove", is false: the printed "Show that" stands and the card disproves it.

**V.3.6 (`P-AGH536ANALYTICEQUIV`) transcribed 2026-11-16 from Greuel--Lossen--Shustin, and the passage to (3.9.4) is still the card's.** The source is Greuel, Lossen and Shustin, *Introduction to Singularities and Deformations* (2007), §3.4, read in the text version `tmp/sources/greuel-lossen-shustin-2007-singularities-deformations-pp200-220.md`, printed page = its marker minus 11, that offset checked against the retained PDF page by page. What it proves, and what is now on the card: Definition 3.30, printed p. 202, analytic and topological equivalence of a germ side by side, with analytic implying topological; Theorem 3.42, printed p. 217, the theorem of Brauner and Zariski that the topological type of a reduced plane curve singularity is determined by, and determines, the system of multiplicity sequences defined on printed p. 216; Proposition 3.41, printed pp. 216--217, that this data is the characteristic exponents of the branches together with their pairwise intersection numbers, which replaces the card's earlier citation of Wall, *Singular Points of Plane Curves*, a book not held and not read; Example 3.43.1(a), printed p. 218, the pair $y^3-x^7$ and $y^3+x^5y-x^7$ with multiplicity sequence $3,3,1,1,1$ and Tjurina numbers $12$ and $11$ printed as Singular output, which the substitution $(x,y)\mapsto(x,-y)$ carries to the card's pair $y^3+x^7$ and $y^3+x^5y+x^7$ up to the unit $-1$; and Remark 3.43.3, printed p. 219, that the Tjurina number is an analytic invariant. **Still without a published proof, and now recorded here rather than implied:** the passage from that data to equivalence in the sense of (3.9.4). The source's Theorem 3.42 is about topological type, and Hartshorne's (3.9.4), printed p. 393, defines equivalence by correspondences between the irreducible components of the reduced total transforms of two embedded resolutions, preserving multiplicities and incidence. GLS list the resolution graph on printed p. 216 as one of the data equivalent to the system of multiplicity sequences but prove the equivalence only for the Puiseux pairs and the characteristic exponents, so the step "same system of multiplicity sequences implies (3.9.4)-equivalence" is not in the cited pages, and both halves of the exercise need it: the forward implication and the equivalence of the pair. Steps `ambient-automorphism-lift`, `automorphism-identifies-resolution-data` and `c1-c2-equivalent` of the card remain its own argument for it. **A second gap, of the same kind:** Definition 3.30's analytic equivalence is an isomorphism of the analytic germs $(\CC^2,z)\to(\CC^2,w)$, while (I, 5.6.1) is isomorphism of completed local rings, and Remark 3.43.3 states Tjurina invariance for the former; the card's own proof of step `tjurina-number-invariant` is the one that covers the latter, by lifting an isomorphism of completions to a formal coordinate change. The source also prints its two Tjurina numbers as a Singular session rather than computing them, and steps `tjurina-f1-twelve` and `tjurina-f2-eleven` compute both by hand. Not read: Wall's book, and GLS Proposition 3.21, cited inside Proposition 3.41's proof.

**V.3.7 (`P-AGH537EMBRESOLUTION`) transcribed in part 2026-11-16: the National Taiwan University entry supplies the five blowup chains, their multiplicities, the five values of $\delta_P$ and the classification, and no embedded resolution.** The source is Algebraic Geometry II, National Taiwan University, 2020 Spring, *Chapter V Surfaces* homework solutions, Exercise 7 of §3 (Ping-Hsun Chuang), PDF pp. 12--13 of `tmp/sources/ntu-ag2-chapter5.pdf`, read in `tmp/sources/ntu-ag2-chapter5.md`, whose markers are coarse so the pages were read off the PDF. Transcribed onto the card: the two charts $x=sy$ and $(v,s)=(y/s,s)$ with the equations $s^3+y^2$ and $s+v^2$ for (a), $s^3+s^4y+y^2$ and $s+vs^3+v^2$ for (b), $s^3+y+y^2$ for (c), $s^3+y^2+y^3$ and $s+v^2+sv^3$ for (d), $s^3+sy+y^2$ and $s+v+v^2$ for (e), which are the card's own equations under the substitution $s=u$ and $v=w$; the multiplicities $3$ and $2$ of each germ; the five values $\delta_P=\frac12\cdot3\cdot2+\frac12\cdot2\cdot1=4$ for (a), (b), (d), (e) and $\frac12\cdot3\cdot2=3$ for (c); and the classification, stated at the end of the entry as "By the resolution graph, we conclude that the sigularity of (0,0) of (a) (b) (d) are equivalent and (c) (e) are different from the others". **Still without a published proof, and now recorded here rather than implied:** three things. An *embedded* resolution in the sense of (3.9.4), which needs the reduced total transform to have normal crossings: the entry stops when the strict transform of the curve is nonsingular, so the third and fourth blowup of (a), (b), (d) and the second to fourth of (c) and (e) are the card's steps `a-third-fourth-blowup`, `b-third-fourth-delta`, `d-third-fourth-delta`, `c-resolution-delta-three` and `e-resolution-delta-four`, and no published source carries them for all five germs together. The argument for the classification: the graphs the entry draws are five `<!-- image -->` blocks in the extraction, so its reason is a picture and not a sentence, and the equivalence of (a), (b), (d) and the separations of (c) and (e) are argued on steps `abd-equivalent`, `c-not-equivalent` and `e-not-equivalent` from the multiplicity data the entry does supply. And the identification of the double point of (e) as a node, which the entry records only as a multiplicity, with the card reading it off the tangent cone $v(u+v)$. Not checked this pass: the five graph images, Yang Pi-Yeh's printed p. 108 and Egbert's Singular session, which the previous pass read.

**V.3.8 (`P-AGH538INEQUIVSING`) transcribed 2026-11-16: two published computations give the first blowups and the two $\delta$ values, and they refute the printed assertion, so no published proof of that assertion can exist.** The sources are Algebraic Geometry II, National Taiwan University, 2020 Spring, *Chapter V Surfaces* homework solutions, Exercise 8 of §3 (Yi-Heng), PDF p. 13 for (a) and PDF p. 14 for (b) of `tmp/sources/ntu-ag2-chapter5.pdf`, read in `tmp/sources/ntu-ag2-chapter5.md` with its coarse markers checked against the PDF; and Math StackExchange question 2867504, "Configuration of infinitely near points", comments 5918658 and 5918691, in `tmp/sources/mse-2867504-hart-v38-infinitely-near-points.md`. V.4.3 is the whole line "See Algebraic Curves over Finite Fields by Hirschfeld, Theorem 3.27", and Hirschfeld's book is not among the retained files. V.4.4(a) he proves by Cayley--Bacharach on $PP'\cup QQ'\cup RR'$ and $L\cup L'\cup P''Q''$, but V.4.4(b) is "See Tate, Silverman: Rational Points. It's in the first chapter. His V.4.1 states $\pi\circ\psi=\mathrm{id}_{\PP^2}$ and $\psi\circ\pi=\mathrm{id}_Q$, which are false as written, though the identification it is used for is right.

In positive characteristic the projection from a bad point can be inseparable and the step that chooses the two auxiliary lines fails there; the card takes that case from Hirschfeld's Theorem 3.27, a book that is not in `tmp/sources` and was not read, and it now says on the step that this case is a citation and not a proof. **So the V.4.3 obligation is not met by the card's own proof**, which covers characteristic $0$ alone. V.4.4(b) is derived from part (a) by the configuration $A=P*Q$, $B=Q*R$, $V=P*T$, where part (a) applied to the triples $(P,Q,A)$ and $(T,B,P_0)$ gives $V,R,S$ collinear, so that $(P+Q)+R=\iota(V)=P+(Q+R)$.

### V.5.8(b) of `SRC-TEXT-HART77` has no complete published solution

**Object and need.** `P-AGH558E8SINGULARITY`, printed p. 420, asks for the resolution of $x^2+y^3+z^5=0$ at the origin by eight successive blowings-up and for the $E_8$ Dynkin diagram of the eight exceptional lines. Part (a), the unique factorisation property of the affine ring, is answered in the retained sets; part (b) is not.

**Observed evidence.** Two retained sets reach the section. Andrew Egbert, *Solutions to Hartshorne's Algebraic Geometry* (October 3, 2013), PDF pp. 300--302, gives part (a) in full; for part (b) he writes "Step 1: Start your computer. Step 2: Enter the following commands into Singular", records a `resolve` call, then follows two or three blowups by hand, arriving at the local equation $X^2+zY(Y+z)=0$ on the second strict transform, and ends "etc, etc." Jinhyun Park, *Algebraic Geometry by Robin Hartshorne, Exercises solutions*, gives part (a) in full as a UFD proof with the same claims ($z$ irreducible, $t=-u^2-v^3$, $A[z^{-1}]=k[u,v,t^{-1}]$, then UFD by the two lemmas on irreducibles and the localization) and stops there; his section is followed immediately by Appendix C.

**Impact and owner.** The card keeps the computation: the strict transforms after the first three blowups are $x_1^2+zy_1^3+z^3=0$, $x_2^2+y^2z_2+yz_2^3=0$ and the two germs $X^2+yZ+y^2Z^3=0$ (an ordinary double point, resolved by one blowup, giving $E_4$) and $X^2+zY(Y+z)=0$; the blowup of the second carries three ordinary double points, at $Z=0$, $Z=-1$ and $V=0$, which are resolved by the remaining three blowups. The incidence chain is $E_1-E_4-E_3-E_7-E_5-E_6-E_2$ with $E_8$ meeting $E_5$, which is $E_8$; the count of eight is consistent with the Milnor number $(2-1)(3-1)(5-1)=8$ of a weighted-homogeneous isolated surface singularity.

**Uncertainty.** Searched: all twelve retained Hartshorne solution files in `tmp/sources` by `pdftotext -layout` extraction, plus `assets/attachments/Hartshorne_Solutions.pdf` (the Cais notes). Chapter V occurs only in Egbert (V.1--V.6) and in Park (§V.5 alone, and in §V.5 only V.5.8, whose part (b) is missing). Conclusion: no complete published solution for part (b). Confidence: high for these sets. Gaps: a published treatment may exist outside them.

**Located sources.** Two published Chapter V solution sets outside the twelve previously inspected contain this exercise. Algebraic Geometry II, National Taiwan University, 2020 Spring (course of Chin-Lung Wang), *Chapter V Surfaces* homework, Exercise 8 of §5 (solution by Yi-Heng), PDF p. 21, downloaded to `tmp/sources/ntu-ag2-chapter5.pdf`, gives the eight successive blowups chart by chart — $x^2+y^3+z^5$, then $x_1^2+zy_1^3+z^3$, then $x_2^2+z_2y_1^2+y_1z^3$, then the two germs $x_3^2+z_3y_1+y_1^2z_3^3$ and $x_3^2+z_2y_3^2+y_3z_2^2$, then their three ordinary double points and their resolutions — and ends "the inverse image of $P$ is a union of eight projective lines corresponding to $E_8$". Miles Reid, *Chapters on Algebraic Surfaces* (arXiv alg-geom/9602006; IAS/Park City Math. Ser. 3, 1997), Chapter 4, §4.2, printed p. 82, downloaded to `tmp/sources/reid-chapters-algebraic-surfaces.pdf`, resolves $D_4$ in full with the divisor computation giving $\Gamma_0^2=-2$ and lists $E_8:x^2+y^3+z^5$ with "the resolution is a bunch of $-2$-curves whose configuration is given by the corresponding Dynkin diagram", which states the dual graph without the blowups. The card now cites both, and the NTU equations agree with the card's.

Checking the seven supplementary cards found three errors of substance, now corrected: the product table answered No for path connectedness under arbitrary products, on the grounds that $\{0,1\}^J$ is connected while every path into it is constant. That is false at the first clause: $\{0,1\}$ is discrete and not connected, so $\{0,1\}^J$ is not connected for any nonempty $J$ and witnesses nothing, and an arbitrary product of path connected spaces is path connected, a path in each coordinate giving a map whose coordinate functions are continuous and which is therefore continuous by Theorem 19.6 — the entry now reads Yes with that argument; separability, which the same card had claimed in every column while contradicting itself for $\RR^J$, now stops where the Hewitt--Marczewski--Pondiczery theorem stops it; the continuous-image card named the Hawaiian earring as a quotient of countably many circles, which it is not, the earring being a first-countable subspace of the plane while the quotient is the wedge, and each of its eleven negative entries now has an explicit witness; and the entry-by-entry check of the eleven-space table and of the four remaining tables named, for every Yes and every No, the theorem or example that decides it, which found no further error but left the ordinary-square, Sorgenfrey and box entries each tied to one numbered result.

**Located since, in five sources outside the sets above, and now landed on the cards.** A later pass located a published argument for each of the twenty-two; their PDFs are in `tmp/sources`, their text versions are MinerU extractions under the same names, and the card-to-place table lives in [#127](https://github.com/dzackgarza/new-qual-site/issues/127). The defects found in the sources, each checked against the book and each named on its card:

- Pearse, §58 Exercise 2 (i) and (j), answers *trivial* for `S^1 \cup (\RR_+ \times 0)` and `S^1 \cup (\RR_+ \times \RR)`. With `\RR_+` the positive reals (printed p. 31) neither space contains `\mathbf 0`, and the homotopy the source writes down, `H(x,t) = (1-t)x + t\,x/\norm x`, is a strong deformation retraction onto `S^1`; both groups are infinite cyclic. The source's own formula proves the opposite of its conclusion.
- Pearse, §58 Exercise 2 (e), argues from a picture that two loops generate and that the group is not abelian; the card decides it by retracting `\RR^3` minus the three rays onto `S^2` minus three points.
- Harvard Math 131, Solution Set 10, item 9.58.5, writes `f \circ g \simeq 1_X` where the composite with source `X` is `g \circ f`; `f \circ g` is a self-map of the one-point space, and the conclusion it draws is only right for `g \circ f`. Corrected on `E-6RQWT`.
- Pearse, §60 Exercise 2, applies the compact-to-Hausdorff theorem to `f^{-1}`, whose continuity is what the exercise wants; repaired on `E-V5CQ0` by applying it to the source's own continuous bijection `g: B^2/\!\sim \to P^2`.
- Pearse, §59 Exercise 4 (a), offers as its example of a trivial `j_*` a pair with `V = X`, where `j_*` is an isomorphism, and answers the case in which only `j_*` is trivial by saying that "there's not much you can say"; that omits what Theorem 59.1 does give there, that `i_*` is then surjective and `\pi_1(X)` a quotient of `\pi_1(U)`. `E-6C2JI` now proves that consequence and exhibits `X = U = S^1` with `V = S^1` minus a point, where `U \cup V = X`, `j_*` is trivial and both groups are `\ZZ`.
- The covering spaces of §60 Exercise 5 are pictures in both the source and the book, and neither text says in words which vertices its four named edges join; the incidence is nevertheless determined by Figure 60.3 together with the stated degrees, and it does make the map a covering: `A_1` through `e_0` and `e_2`, `B_1` through `e_0` and `e_1`, `A_0` attached to `B_1` at `e_1`, `B_0` attached to `A_1` at `e_2`, so that each of the three points over `x_0` carries four edge-ends, two over each circle. `E-UMMOE` states that incidence, checks that `p` is a three-sheeted covering, and reproduces the source's lift argument on it.

Parts of two exercises were the residue, and now carry a transcribed published proof as well: parts (a) and (c) of §58 Exercise 10 (`E-CVDAJ`) and parts (a) and (c) of §58 Exercise 7 (`E-R3LKO`). The first comes from Takumi Murayama, *Selected Solutions to Munkres's Topology, 2nd Ed.*, Exercise 58.10, its proof of (a) at lines 1646--1650 and of (c) at 1659--1667 of `tmp/sources/munkres-solutions-murayama-mat365.tex`; the second from the answer of JacobsonRadical to Math StackExchange question 848636, answer 3426310 of 2019-11-07, its (a) at line 61 and its (c) at line 84 of `tmp/sources/mse-848636-munkres-58-7.md`, which proves (a) by making `j` a homotopy equivalence and applying Theorem 58.7 rather than by Lemma 58.4, and takes the counterexample of (c) on `X = \RR^2`; Feryll's *Praying For Stockholm* post of 2015-02-01 was read as a second source for §58 Exercise 10 (a) and (c) and is not the one transcribed, since it misquotes both the degree in (c) and axiom (iii). The accepted answer in the 848636 thread, 848727, is not the source of any part: its surjectivity argument for (a) and (b) treats the homotopy `H` as fixing the base point, which the exercise does not assume. Two page corrections came with the pass: §58 Exercise 7 prints on printed p. 366, where `E-R3LKO` had carried p. 367, and §58 Exercise 10 prints on printed p. 367, not on p. 366 as the assignment for the pass stated; both were read off the page images.

**A reader's pass over these cards, and its fourteen repairs.** A reader audited the twenty-two cards against the MinerU text versions in `tmp/sources` and the book, and every item was checked against the card, the source and the book before the card was changed; each repair is recorded in the card's own audit note, and every card keeps a proof. Two were of substance and are the first two bullets above: `E-6C2JI` had replaced the source's invalid example by one whose two open pieces do not cover `X`, so that Theorem 59.1 never applied to it, and whose heading called `\pi_1(U)` nontrivial while its proof called `U` an arc; and `E-UMMOE` had claimed that no incidence of four edges over three points makes the picture a covering, which is false, and had therefore abandoned the exercise's covering for the one of Lemma 60.5. The other twelve:

- `E-CVDAJ` (§58.10(a)) applied the degree to the inclusion `S^n \to B^{n+1}` and to the retraction `B^{n+1} \to S^n`, but the exercise's three axioms define the degree only for self-maps of `S^n`; the card now argues `\operatorname{id} = r \circ i \simeq r \circ c` for the constant map `c`, and reads `1 = 0` off those two self-maps.
- `E-FV0KE` (§58.8) computed the disc of radius `1/2` about `(0,1)` as meeting the tooth at `1/n` in `(1/2,1]`, where the tooth meets it in `(1-\sqrt{1/4-1/n^2},1]`, and called every piece of the intersection clopen, where the piece on the `y`-axis is not open; the card now computes the intersection, proves each tooth clopen, and uses only that.
- `E-2M0XQ` (§58.2): part (e) projected stereographically from a point outside the three deleted points, which leaves `\RR^2` minus three points rather than the doubly punctured plane, and now projects from one of them; part (b) asserted that a homotopy descended to the quotient without showing that `q \times \operatorname{id}` restricted to `(I^2-c) \times I` is a quotient map, which the card now proves from Theorems 22.1 and 22.2 and §29 Exercise *11(a).
- `E-5CC0M` (§60.3) computed the points of `p'^{-1}(U)` from a formula that presumes `A` is the unit circle wrapped uniformly, which the book's construction of `p` does not make, and its "exactly when" holds only for `U` whose trace on `A` is the whole disc's; the argument is now the local one at `(1,0)` and needs no coordinates.
- `E-0LZE7` (§58.4) asserted that the two composites are the maps the source draws, which neither text settles because both retractions are given only by pictures, and described what is collapsed as "the region the figure eight encloses", where the source's own words put the points inside its dotted line. The clause "the lens between the crossing points" in this bullet was wrong in the same way: the figure eight is two circles meeting in a single point, and the correction is in the second reader's pass recorded below.
- `E-WUZ10` (§59.1) called the part of the first sphere in `U` the closed hemisphere, though `U` is defined by `x > -1` and the great circle `x = -1` is not in it.
- `E-1QY2X` (§59.2) described `B^2/\partial B^2` as "two closed discs glued along their boundary circles", which is not that quotient; the card now gives an explicit map `B^2 \to S^2` constant exactly on the boundary and proves the quotient is `S^2`.
- `E-LKUPH` (§58.1) claimed `G(x,t) = x` whenever `r(x) \in B`, where `G(x,t) = r(x)`; what holds, and all the conclusion uses, is `G(x,t) = x` for `x \in B`.
- `E-E79BA` (§59.3): the composite to `\RR^n_0` used `u \mapsto u+q`, which removes `2q` and not `q`; it is now `u \mapsto u-q`.
- `E-SKM03` (§55.3) concluded `\Delta^2 \cong B^2` "by convexity and compactness", which is not an argument; the card now proves that a compact convex set in the plane with nonempty interior is homeomorphic to the disc, through its radial function.
- `E-WRMSX` (§57.2): the last step's heading read "`g(x)=g(-x)` for some `x`, so `g` is surjective", garbling the contrapositive, since the coincidence was derived under the assumption that `g` misses a point.
- `E-97HXB`: the audit note attributed to the UCR sheet a remark that `A` must be nonempty; the sheet has no such remark, and the nonemptiness argument on the card is the card's own.

**Confidence:** high for the sets in the checkout. **Gaps:** a course sheet outside these searches may answer any of the twenty-two; the ETSU notes may be accompanied by exercise solutions elsewhere on that site, and were read only for their section content; the AoPS blog "shooting star", *Topology* — the one answer key located for the Chapter 4 supplementary exercises — renders its mathematics client-side and answers automated requests with a bot check, and was not readable for Chapter 9 either.

**Repair.** A published solution of each, checked against the card and cited with its page or URL, or the owner's direction to accept the checked proofs. Checking the twenty-two found two defects of substance, now corrected: `E-2M0XQ` justified the answer $\ZZ$ for $S^1\cup(\RR_+\times\RR)$ by a radial formula that is undefined on the part of the $y$-axis outside the circle and at the origin, and the answer is now derived from the contractibility of the half-plane and of its intersection with the circle; and `E-6C2JI` answered §59 Exercise 4 with the Seifert--van Kampen description of the fundamental group without saying that this is Theorem 70.1 of Chapter 11 rather than anything in Section 59, whose Theorem 59.1 gives only that the two images generate, and the card now says which is which. Checking the thirty-one sourced cards found one more: `E-SKM03`'s neighbour `E-N7AOD` had to correct dbFin's reparametrisation in part (c) of §52 Exercise 7, and `E-PTY7A`, `E-C0ZWV` and `E-5T90S` had each added an unstated nonemptiness hypothesis to the printed exercise, which is now restored with the exception named in the solution.

**A second reader's pass over seven of these cards, its repairs, and a papercut of the extraction.** A second reader audited `E-0LZE7`, `E-1QY2X`, `E-WRMSX`, `E-2M0XQ`, `E-6C2JI`, `E-FV0KE` and `E-5CC0M` against the MinerU text versions in `tmp/sources`, against Pearse and against the book, and every item was checked against the card, the source and the book before the card changed; each repair is in the card's audit note. The seven:

- `E-0LZE7` (§58.4) asks the reader for maps and described none: it named `f = r_Y \circ i_X` and `g = r_X \circ i_Y` through the two retractions of the doubly punctured plane, which the book gives by pictures -- of Example 3 it says only "we leave it to you to sketch the maps involved" -- and then said that no text fixes where a point goes. It also asserted that Pearse's Figure 7 draws the figure eight as two circles crossing in two points with a lens between them, where the figure eight is two circles meeting in a single point (Lemma 60.5, printed p. 373) and Pearse's text has no words for that figure at all. `f` and `g` are now given by formulas, `g` by the pasting lemma on the two semicircles and the bar of the theta space, and the two composites by explicit homotopies; the reader's own formulas close each loop along the bar in the direction opposite to the one `g` reads the semicircles, which runs each loop backwards and is not homotopy inverse to the identity, so the traversal direction is now part of the construction and is said on the card.
- `E-1QY2X` (§59.2) called `e: I^2 \to B^2` a linear homeomorphism, which no linear map is: it carries the square onto a parallelogram. The step needs only a continuous surjection and now uses `(s,t) \mapsto (s \cos 2\pi t, s \sin 2\pi t)`. The quotient `B^2/\partial B^2 \cong S^2` also needed that `B^2 \to S^2` is onto, which the card had used without stating; it is now proved, by the inversion formula that the injectivity argument already contained.
- `E-WRMSX` (§57.2) headed its last step with the statement `g(x) = g(-x)` for some `x`, which is false of the identity map: the coincidence holds only under the supposition that `g` misses a point, which two earlier steps used without saying so. The proof now opens with that supposition and every heading that uses it says so.
- `E-2M0XQ` (§58.2(b)) said that the homotopy `H` is constant on the fibres of `q_0 \times \operatorname{id}`; it is not, since the two points the quotient identifies are boundary points and `H` fixes them, so they stay distinct. `q_0 \circ H` is constant there, and the descended map satisfies `\bar H \circ (q_0 \times \operatorname{id}) = q_0 \circ H`. The card also now shows that `H` never takes the deleted value `c`, which the codomain requires.
- `E-6C2JI` (§59.4(b)) joined two points of `U \cap V` by "a polygonal path avoiding four points, four points not separating the sphere": a polygonal path on `S^2` is not defined, and the separation of the sphere by four points was the thing to be proved. The card now projects stereographically from `a_1` and joins any two points of the plane minus three points by two segments through a point off finitely many lines, and names the `x_0` that Theorem 59.1 asks for.
- `E-FV0KE` (§58.8) concluded that the identity of the comb is homotopic to the constant map at `x_0` "because `X` is contractible", where the contraction written out just above it ends at `(0,0)`; the step from `(0,0)` to `x_0` is the path `0 \times I` and the homotopy it gives, and the card now states it.
- `E-5CC0M` (§60.3) opened with "The proof is transcribed from Pearse", which had stopped being true when the argument was replaced; the preamble now says which two sentences are the source's -- the description of the preimage and the observation that no map of a cross onto an interval is injective -- and that the argument at `(1,0)` is the card's own.

**A papercut: the Munkres extraction has no page markers.** `tmp/sources/munkres-2000-topology.md` carries no per-page or per-printed-page markers, unlike the Hatcher extraction's `<!-- PDF page N -->` lines, so a card's printed page has to be recovered from `tmp/sources/munkres-2000-topology.pdf` page by page. In this checkout PDF page `n` is printed page `n - 15` throughout, checked on the PDF pages carrying printed pp. 100--115, 140--142, 184--187, 324, 330, 338 and 359--377. The cost is visible in these cards: §58 prints its Exercises 1 to 8, Exercise 4 and the starred Exercise 8 among them, on printed p. 366, read on the page image, while `E-0LZE7`, `E-2M0XQ` and `E-FV0KE` had each been recorded with p. 367 or pp. 366--367, and three audit notes had carried that page forward. The three cards now cite p. 366 and their notes record the correction. No expected result beyond that: the offset is a property of this PDF, and a card that cites a Munkres page should still read the page it cites.

### `SRC-TEXT-MUN00`: what each card of §74--§85 transcribes, and the forty-one that keep a proof of their own

**Object and need.** Every Munkres card is to carry a proof transcribed from a published solution or a complete published argument, with its source and printed page, or a checked proof plus this entry listing every source searched ([#129](https://github.com/dzackgarza/new-qual-site/issues/129), [#146](https://github.com/dzackgarza/new-qual-site/issues/146), part of [#106](https://github.com/dzackgarza/new-qual-site/issues/106)). All 51 cards of Chapters 12 and 13 (§74--§85) have been searched for. **Two** carry Takumi Murayama's solution, §74 Exercise 3 (`E-160XR`) and §75 Exercise 3 (`E-4349Q`). Of the remaining **forty-nine**, a located published solution proves the whole exercise under Munkres' hypotheses for **eight**, and the other **forty-one** keep their own proof of at least one part; every one of the forty-nine is named below with the sources read and the queries run for it, and each card's audit note carries the same record.

**The searches.** They were run on 2026-11-15 from a machine other than this VM, and the whole record — per card, the status, the files saved with their answer ids, what each source does and does not prove, every query, and each rejected thread with the reason — is `tmp/sources/mse-searches-146.md`. The engines, per card: the Stack Exchange API (site=math, anonymous, `/search/advanced` under the exercise's wording with "Munkres" and its section, and `/similar` from the exercise's own statement); Exa web search for the exercise statements and the named theorems; `gh search repos` for Munkres solution repositories and `gh search code` (with and without `extension:tex`) for the section's phrases. Each hit read is saved in `tmp/sources` as `mse-<questionid>-<card>.md` (Math Stack Exchange) or `gh-dyang5-MATH104-Topology-<card>.md`. **The sets located outside `tmp/sources`** are those two: Math Stack Exchange threads, and David Yang's *MATH104: Topology, Fall 2023* homework on GitHub, `dyang5/MATH104-Topology` at commit `12686a815d58f29aeaadb90a30449ae85c0a613f` (2024-05-04), files `HW/hw10.tex`--`HW/hw12.tex`. The repository search returned fourteen solution sets, none reaching §74: dbFin (index stops at §67), "9beach" (Chapters 1--4), "kyp44" (to §22), Murayama's selection (two exercises in these sections), and the sets in the checkout listed in the entry below for §37--§38. One further source was located and **not read**: B. Conrad, *Quotients by group actions* (Stanford Math 396 handout, `virtualmath1.stanford.edu/~conrad/diffgeomPage/handouts/qtmanifold.pdf`), Example 2.14 and Remark 2.15, cited for part of `E-CGJJG` through Exa; it is a PDF, it is not in `tmp/sources`, and the card records that it was searched and not read.

**What was transcribed.** Where a source proves the exercise under Munkres' hypotheses, the card now carries that proof, cited by author, title, URL and date or commit, with its location in the file or the answer id; the book's numbered results are cited at each step in place of the source's own references. Where a source proves a part, or proves the whole under a stronger hypothesis, the card states what it proves and which hypothesis differs, and keeps its own proof for the rest. A hint, an assertion, a figure, or an argument with a gap is recorded as a source searched and is not transcribed as a proof.

**The eight with a complete published proof.** `E-HC37E` (§74.6): Math StackExchange 1527539, answer by the account posting as user98602 (2015-11-13), to question 1527500 — the map onto $F_2$, which differs from the printed hint's and is transcribed with that difference stated. `E-B74TA` (§74.7): Yang, hw10.tex lines 35--70 — the printed hint carried out, with the factorisation step written out. `E-CEDQ9` (§79.1): answer 2813771 (2018-06-09) to question 2813729 — the lifting criterion and a contractible cover. `E-UYQU1` (§79.7): answer 1527797 by Tsemo Aristide (2015-11-13) to question 1527760 — the commutator map into the discrete fibre; the card's steps are that argument written out. `E-4RF8O` (§81.4): answer 412360 by martini (2013-06-05) to question 412317 — the finite-intersection separation argument, which the card also carries as its own proof; the answer prints "$U_g\cap V_g\ne\emptyset$" where Hausdorffness gives "$=\emptyset$", and the intersection and computation that follow use the equality, so the card records the slip and not a gap. `E-J7FPE` (§79.5): (a) answer 971387 by Sammy Black (2014-10-13) to question 971171, whose assertion $(\varphi_A)_*=A$ the card computes; (b) Yang, hw11.tex lines 35--77. `E-AL52O` (§85.1): Yang, hw12.tex lines 33--59. `E-CLZ18` (§85.2): Yang, hw12.tex lines 102--116, first solution by Theorem 85.3, and the card's own reduced-word proof of the transversal his second solution asserts.

Four cards carried raw `|` for restriction (`E-UYQU1`, `E-LV54B`, `E-79XXG`, `E-SF828`), which STYLE-04 forbids and the pre-commit hook rejects; they now write `\restrict`. Two page numbers were corrected against the PDF: Lemma 85.2 is printed p. 514 and Theorem 85.3 p. 515, and Theorem 69.4 with Corollary 69.5 p. 423.

### `SRC-TEXT-MUN00`: five cards of §37 and §38 have no complete located published solution

**Object and need.** Every Munkres card is to carry a proof transcribed from a published solution, or a checked proof plus this entry listing every source searched ([#125](https://github.com/dzackgarza/new-qual-site/issues/125), part of [#106](https://github.com/dzackgarza/new-qual-site/issues/106)). The fifteen cards of §37 and §38 were each searched for; ten of them carry a proof transcribed from a located published solution with its page, and the five below do not, so each keeps a proof checked line by line against the book.

**What the search added.** Two Chapter 5--6 sets and one per-section sheet were located and are now in `tmp/sources`, and are tabulated on [the topology solutions page](wiki/topology/resources/solutions.md). (i) Aleksey Zinger, *MAT 530: Topology & Geometry, I*, Fall 2005, problem-set solutions (`tmp/sources/munkres-solutions-zinger-mat530-ps2.pdf` … `-ps9.pdf`, from `math.stonybrook.edu/~azinger/mat530/`); its Chapter 5--6 items are §37 Exercise 1 (sheet 4, PDF pp. 1--2), §37 Exercise 5 (sheet 4, PDF pp. 2--3) and §41 Exercises 2 and 7 (sheet 6). The mathematics is settled on the cards meanwhile: §37.2 is the De Morgan correspondence between countable subcovers of the complements of closures and countable subfamilies with empty intersection; §37.3 (a) runs the Tychonoff argument with countable intersections in place of finite ones, (b) is Lemma 37.2 with countable intersections (a countable family of countable subfamilies is countable), and (c) locates the failure in the Zorn step, the union of a chain of countably-intersective collections need not be countably intersective, with (iii) failing at the Sorgenfrey plane whose antidiagonal is an uncountable closed discrete subspace; §37.4 carries the Zorn argument the exercise outlines, normality separating the two closed pieces of a separation of the intersection and compactness producing one chain member that misses their union; §38.1 proves each of the three statements Example 4 makes, including that $\sin(1/x)$ extends to the Example 3 compactification as a coordinate projection while $\cos(1/x)$ does not; §38.10 is the two functor laws, both from uniqueness of the extension into a Hausdorff space.

so what the printed proof gives is that each component is a countable union of compact subspaces); §42.1 against Theorem 42.1, Theorem 41.4 and Theorem 41.5; §42.2 against Theorem 42.1 and Theorem 28.2, its appeal to countable compactness replaced by the limit point compactness that theorem needs; **No card of the batch now rests on a borrowed theorem.** §50 Exercise 3 (the topologist's sine curve has dimension 1) had cited the countable closed-sum theorem of dimension theory by theorem number, from Engelking's *Theory of Dimensions, Finite and Infinite* and Hurewicz and Wallman's *Dimension Theory*, neither of which is in the checkout (the archive.org copies of the second are access-restricted, and a citation that was not read on its page certifies nothing). That citation is withdrawn, and $\dim\bar S\le1$ is now proved from the book alone: for an arbitrary open cover and a Lebesgue number $\delta$ (Lemma 27.5, $\bar S$ being compact by Theorem 27.3), the cover built in steps 2--5 of the card consists of the sets $W(I)=\bar S\cap\{y\in I\}\cap\{x<\eta\}$, whose index intervals cover $[-1,1]$ with multiplicity at most two and with multiplicity one near $y_0=\sin(1/\eta)$, of the slabs $C_k=\bar S\cap\{s_k<x<s_{k+1}\}\cap\{\abs{y-\sin(1/x)}<\delta/16\}$ and of the seam pieces $D_j=\bar S\cap\{\abs{x-s_j}<\nu\}\cap\{\abs{y-\sin(1/s_j)}<\delta/64\}$; each member has diameter below $\delta$ under the square metric (Theorem 20.3) and no point lies in more than two members, the three cases $x<\eta$, $x=s_j$ and $s_k<x<s_{k+1}$ being separated. The lower bound is the card of Exercise 50.2 with the connectedness of Example 7 of §24.

For the compact set $f(C)$ inside the open set $g^{-1}(U)$, each of its points has a compact neighbourhood inside $g^{-1}(U)$ because $Y$ is locally compact Hausdorff; finitely many of their interiors cover $f(C)$, and the union $V$ of those interiors has compact closure inside $g^{-1}(U)$. That is step 1 of the card, which agrees with it.
- `E-KS2BT` (§46 Exercise 10, printed p. 289): Math StackExchange 431747 (2013-06-28), where answer 432280 by Daniel Fischer builds the metric $\sup_n\varepsilon_n\min\{1,\sup_{K_n}d(f,g)\}$ on an exhaustion of $X$ by compact sets and proves both inclusions of topologies and the convergence of Cauchy sequences, and answer 3353044 by tadejsv proves that a space $\sigma$-compact in Munkres' sense is hemicompact: with $A_i$ the compact sets of the definition, $K_n$ the union of the first $n$, every compact subset is covered by finitely many interiors and so lies in some $K_n$. The card's part (b) is the exercise's own hint, the closed compatibility subspace of the product of the uniform spaces $Y^{A_i}$, which is the same construction; its part (a) is in neither answer.

The card's regular argument is its own.

**Conclusion.** No answer here proves its exercise: one defers to other books, one is an assertion through Alexander duality, one is a question with no answer, and six returned no question at all. None of these nine answers is transcribed, and each of the nine keeps its checked proof. **Gaps:** the printed manuals remain paywalled and unread; the record searched question titles, bodies and `/similar` but not question comments, and it is a snapshot, so an answer posted later to 2021341 or to any of the rejected questions would not be in it.

**The queries, card by card.** Besides the two corpus-wide searches `Munkres topology Chapter 10 separation theorems solutions exercises Jordan separation invariance of domain course homework solutions pdf` and `github repository Munkres Topology solutions chapter 10 "section 62" invariance of domain exercises`, and the two that located the hits (`math stackexchange Munkres section 62 exercise simply connected open set bounded component of R^2 - C lies in U`, and `"compact contractible" subset of the sphere does not separate Munkres Borsuk lemma proof math stackexchange`), each card was searched for as follows.
