## 2026-11-17: the corpus validates again, the two blocking errors were notation, and the gate cannot see the class they belong to

**Object and need, 2026-11-17.** Issue #150. At `bcff6d385c` `uv run qualc check` exited 1 with two errors, and `tools/backlog.py` returns a single `corpus-validation` queue whenever `qualc.cli.load` reports any error, so `BACKLOG.md` carried no audit queue at all — orphans, duplicate bodies, empty provenance and the rest were never measured — and `tools/unsolved_queue.py` exited without writing `queues/C-unsolved-cards.md`. The repair is the two card defects and a regeneration; this record keeps what the repair found beyond them, so the next reader does not re-derive it.

**The first error was a one-character typo of an existing macro, not a second meaning, 2026-11-17.** `P-AGH5217CONORMALSPLIT` wrote `\mathcal T_{\PP^3}\restrictof_C` inside its quotation of Yang Pi-Yeh's conormal sequence, and `\restrictof` is defined neither by `vocabularies/macros.json` nor by the MathJax build. The preamble's macro for this meaning is `\restrictionof{A}{B}`, `{\left.{{#1}} \right|_{{#2}} }`, used on 70 cards; `\restrictof` occurs nowhere else in the corpus and is `\restrictionof` with one letter dropped. So this is a mistyped use of that macro, and no macro was added: a second macro would carry no meaning of its own, which is exactly the case `STYLE-03`'s one-macro-per-meaning rule forbids. Two further spans in the same card wrote the postfix form `\Omega^1\PP^3\restrictionof_C`, and six in `P-AGH5215FROBENIUSRULED` wrote `\pi\restrictionof_Y` and `f\restrictionof_R`; all eight now read the two-argument form.

**The second error was a prose ellipsis written as mathematics, 2026-11-17.** `P-AGH543ORDINARYSING`'s remark on other published treatments quoted the National Taiwan University solution's closing sentence with a raw `\ldots` where the quotation elides words, and Pandoc's HTML writer drops raw TeX it cannot typeset, so the reader saw no ellipsis at all. `STYLE-04`'s "ellipses are `\ldots` in lists and `\cdots` between binary operators" is a rule about mathematics; an ellipsis inside quoted prose is punctuation, and the card now carries the character, which is how the corpus writes a prose ellipsis elsewhere (the solution of `E-SS7.EX-8`).

**The gate has a blind spot and eight spans were sitting in it, 2026-11-17.** `qualc.tex.unrenderable_tex` compares the controlling words of the authored text against the preamble and the MathJax command set. It does not look at how many arguments a macro is given, so the postfix form above passed `qualc check` on both cards: TeX takes the `_` of the subscript as the macro's first argument and the subscript's letter as its second, and the preamble's definition rejects that with `! Missing { inserted.`, a fatal error under `halt-on-error`, checked by typesetting the definition from `vocabularies/macros.json` beside every span with `pdflatex` — the fatal error before the repair and a PDF after it. Every one of the eight was a rendering failure that only a reader of the page could have seen, which is why the repair is recorded here rather than filed as a check. A check that would catch it is not the arity rule alone: `\abs X` and `\matt 0 1 1 0` are legal and common, so the measurable case is narrower, a declared argument whose token is `_`, `^`, `$`, `}` or `&`. Scanned over `corpus/` and `wiki/`, that narrower rule reports one pre-existing span, the `\units` of line 29 of `PR-N6S6P` named below, and nothing else in either tree — too little to justify a new gate, and the case it cannot see is the larger one: an argument taken from a token such as `(` or `=` is legal TeX and wrong mathematics, and no token rule separates it from `\abs (x+y)`, where the bracket really is the argument. The record is the instrument.

**Same scan, repaired with the record, 2026-11-17.** The macro `\units`, `{ {#1}^{\times} }`, is prefix-only, and four spans used it postfix: `corpus/theory/Algebra/D-7O2CH.md` line 19 wrote `R\setminus\theset{0}=R\units.`, so the `\times` attached to the full stop, and `corpus/theory/Algebra/PR-N6S6P.md` lines 29, 42 and 51 wrote `(\ZZ/n\ZZ)\units`, `(\ZZ/p_k^{n_k}\ZZ)\units` and `(\ZZ/8\ZZ)\units`, whose first arguments are then `$`, the `\\` of the row break and `=` respectively. Typesetting the old text with the pinned definition gives `! Missing } inserted.`, `! Too many }'s.` and two `! Missing $ inserted.`; the four now read `\units{R}`, `\units{(\ZZ/n\ZZ)}` and `\units{(\ZZ/p_k^{n_k}\ZZ)}`, which typeset with no diagnostic. The mathematics is unchanged: `\units{R}` sets $R^\times$, which is what each sentence says.

**Not repaired, and why, 2026-11-17.** `corpus/collections/SRC-TEXT-HART77/P-AGH213SURJLOCAL.md` line 58 writes the exponential sequence of sheaves as `\underline{\ZZ} \injects (\OO_\CC, +) \surjectsvia{\exp} (\units{\OO_\CC}, \cdot)`, and `\surjectsvia` is `\xrightarrow[#1]{#2} …`, two arguments, so the second is taken to be the `(` that follows: the arrow's upper label becomes a bracket. What the exp arrow of that sequence should say is a judgement about the mathematics — whether the label belongs above, below, or both — and the record leaves it rather than guessing; a reader of the card should settle it against the sequence the card is writing.

**Uncertainty, 2026-11-17.** Not checked: the rendered page of any card in a browser — the claim about what a reader saw rests on Pandoc dropping the raw TeX, on `unrenderable_tex`'s report of it, and on TeX's own diagnostics for the macro arity, not on an inspected page. Not done: no search for other uses of `\restrictof` outside this repository, and no change to the gate, which is the point of the record rather than an omission. The `dead-provenance-hrefs` entry of the regenerated `BACKLOG.md` is the corpus's measurement, and six of its seven lines are this VM's egress being refused — five `worldcat.org` 429s and one SSL hostname mismatch — rather than evidence that the hrefs are dead.

**Repair, 2026-11-17:** the two errors and the eight spans in `185f9dd7ea`; `BACKLOG.md` regenerated in `66c2a5647c`; the four `\units` spans and this record in the commit that carries it. Checks: `uv run qualc check` at `66c2a5647c`, exit 0, "14395 cards and 321 wiki pages OK"; `just backlog`, "14 queues, 1347 finding(s)" and no `corpus-validation` section; `just unsolved`, "queues/C-unsolved-cards.md: rewritten" after the file was removed, its bytes identical to the checked-in ones.

## 2026-11-18, third pass: the acceptance made a check — `tools/acceptance_121.py`, its tests, and the blog post it found on V.1.11

**Object and need.** The two records above decide #121's four items by measurement, but a measurement taken once is not a gate: the next card edited can lose its page, name a user post, or state an exercise the text version does not carry, and nothing reports it. This pass turns three of the four items into a check with its own tests, runs it over the sixty-nine cards, and repairs the one card it failed.

**The check.** `tools/acceptance_121.py` reads the sixty-nine-card inventory out of this file between the headings `**The cards, sixty-nine.**` and `**What was searched in this pass`, and for each card decides:

- **R1 publication** — the rendered body names at least one publication, that is a solution set, a textbook, lecture notes or a numbered statement of one; a Mathematics Stack Exchange answer, a MathOverflow answer or a blog post is not a publication and does not satisfy it.
- **R2 page** — at least one publication the body names carries a page or a numbered statement within 500 characters of its name (`printed p. 84`, `PDF pp. 16--17`, `tag 0BYA`, `Theorem 3.3`). A name that carries no page is printed as a note, not charged as a failure, because a card may mention a book without citing it.
- **R3 exercise** — the exercise the card states is located in `tmp/sources/hartshorne-1977-algebraic-geometry.md` by section heading and number, allowing the starred form `\*2.17.` and the unpunctuated `3.11 (a)`; where the extraction does not carry the exercise, the card must give the book's printed or PDF page for it. The extraction's gaps are reported, not charged to the card.
- **R4 quotations**, advisory and never failing: how many of the card's quoted spans of sixty characters or more occur in a text version the card names, at a token overlap of 0.85 after deleting whitespace and dollars.

The exit status is 1 if any card fails R1, R2 or R3. The fourth acceptance item — whether a proof matches its source — is not decidable from text, and the module says so in its docstring rather than pretending otherwise.

**Its tests.** `tests/test_acceptance_121.py` builds a fixture repository and decides seven cases: a card with a publication, a page and its exercise passes; a card whose only source is a user post fails R1; a publication named without a page fails R2; an exercise absent from the text version with no book page fails R3; the same card passes once its book page is given; any failure makes the run exit 1; and a missing inventory is reported rather than passing vacuously. `./.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_acceptance_121.py` gives 7 passed.

**What it found, and the repair.** Run over the corpus it reports **68 of 69 cards passing and one failing**: `P-AGH5111FINITEAUT` V.1.11, R2, because the only source its body cited with a place was "Dan Bragg, *Automorphisms of curves* (2015), Proof 2" — and Bragg's text is the post of 2015-11-20 on the blog functorofpoints.wordpress.com, with no printed page and no publication behind it. The card had called it a published solution for part (b). Repaired: the remark now names the post as a post with no printed page, says that no publication located proves part (b) that way, and steps s8, s9 and s10 — which take its three paragraphs — are marked as the card's own (lines 373, 389 and 407 of the card); the National Taiwan University exercise now carries its page, printed p. 4 of that set, and Yang Pi-Yeh's exercise 5.1.11 its page, printed p. 101. After the repair the check reports **69 of 69** passing R1--R3.

**Not decided by the check, and still open.** Whether a proof matches its source, for any card but the six read in the records above; and the two cards whose proofs rest on an input no publication proves, `P-AGH4422FAMILYOVERAFFINELINE` lines 371 and 386 and `P-AGH374COHOMCLASS` line 752, which the check cannot see because their steps are correctly marked as the cards' own.

**Repair, 2026-11-18, third pass:** `tools/acceptance_121.py`, `tests/test_acceptance_121.py`, `P-AGH5111FINITEAUT` (one appended `source-corrected` event of this date, three step marks, three page insertions) and this record. Checks: `./.venv/bin/python -m qualc.authoring check P-AGH5111FINITEAUT`, "schema and Markdown parsing OK (single card)"; `tmp/lam.sh`, numbering the steps 1 to 13 with QED labels present and no unknown step label; `./.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_acceptance_121.py`, 7 passed; `./.venv/bin/python tools/acceptance_121.py`, "69 of 69 cards pass R1--R3; 0 fail"; `./.venv/bin/python -m qualc check` below.

## 2026-11-18, sixth pass: the two sources named for the residue, checked, and what each does and does not hold

**Object and need.** Two sources were named for the two parts still owed a published argument: Hartshorne IV.4, Theorem 4.11 for IV.4.22's `abelian-scheme` step, and `tmp/sources/dongryul-kim-hartshorne-solutions.md` for III.7.4(b),(d). Each was read at the place named. One holds part of what was claimed; the other does not hold it at all.

**IV.4.22: the book proves the fibre-level statement, not the relative one.** Read in `tmp/sources/hartshorne-1977-algebraic-geometry.md`: the definition of a group scheme over a base and Remark 4.10.5 at printed pp. 323--324; Remark 4.10.6, "The Jacobian variety $J$ of a curve $X$ is automatically a group scheme over $k$", printed p. 324; Theorem 4.11, printed p. 325, whose hypothesis is "Let $X$ be an elliptic curve, and fix a point $P_0\in X$. Take $J=X$, and take $\mathcal L$ on $X\times J$ to be $\mathcal L(\Delta)\otimes p_1^*\mathcal L(-P_0)$", and whose last clause identifies the group structure of 4.10.6 with the one of 4.7; and the definition "An abelian variety is a complete group variety over $k$", printed p. 140. Together these say that an elliptic curve over $k$ is its own Jacobian and that its group law is a morphism, which is the fibre-level half of the step and is now cited on the card at line 305. **What they do not say is the step itself**: the theorem fixes the curve over $k$ and varies the test scheme $T$ (line 10152 of the text version onward), so it is silent about a family $E\to S$ with a section, which is what the step states (card line 298) and what the card's proof names as the unproved passage (card line 305, "that the fibrewise group laws are the restrictions of morphisms $E\times_SE\to E$ and $E\to E$ over $S$, and the representability of the relative Picard functor"). The exact line that fails is therefore the theorem's hypothesis at **text version line 10152**, read against card line 305: the quantifier is over $k$-schemes $T$ with $X$ fixed, not over a varying family. The step stays the card's own; what changed is that the part the book does prove is now cited with its printed pages.

**III.7.4(b),(d): the named file does not carry the solutions claimed for it.** Read in `tmp/sources/dongryul-kim-hartshorne-solutions.md`: the exercise is stated at line 6824 and its solution runs from line 6834. Part (a) is proved in full; part (b)'s solution is the single sentence **line 6862**, "If $X=\mathbf P^n$, we can always take", after which the next line is the heading of part (c), whose solution is one paragraph; and **no solution of part (d) exists in the file** — after (c) the text passes to Section 3.8, whose first exercise is at line 6894. The same holds of the duplicate `tmp/sources/hartshorne-solutions-kim.md`, which is the same document at the same lines. So the transcription asked for cannot be made from this set: there is no proof of (b) to transcribe and no text of (d) at all, and the file:lines above are the exact failure. `P-AGH374COHOMCLASS` keeps its own derivation of (b) and (d) and its record of what (R) and (B) still owe.

**Repair, 2026-11-18, sixth pass:** `P-AGH4422FAMILYOVERAFFINELINE` gains the book citation at line 305 and one appended `source-corrected` event of this date; this record. ## 2026-11-18, seventh pass: IV.4.22's step closed on the owner's direction, and what that direction covers

**The direction.** The owner, 2026-11-18: for `P-AGH4422FAMILYOVERAFFINELINE`'s step `abelian-scheme` the source is Hartshorne himself --- IV.4, Theorem 4.11 with the book's definition "an abelian variety is a complete group variety over $k$" --- "that is exactly the step the card needs, cited from the book the card is checked against", and "do not wait for Katz--Mazur or Mumford GIT". The card was already carrying the citation for the half the book states; this record closes the step on that direction and states its scope, so that the next reader does not reopen it as an omission.

**What the card now cites, with its pages.** `P-AGH4422FAMILYOVERAFFINELINE` line 305 cites Hartshorne IV.4: Theorem 4.11, printed p. 325 (the elliptic curve is its own Jacobian, its last clause identifying the group structure of 4.10.6 with that of 4.7); Remark 4.10.6, printed p. 324 (the Jacobian of a curve is automatically a group scheme over $k$); Remarks 4.10.5 and the definition of a group scheme over a base, printed pp. 323--324; and the definition "an abelian variety is a complete group variety over $k$", printed p. 140. The printed hint of the exercise, IV.4.22 on printed p. 340, is the book's own assertion that the section fixes the group structure on the fibres, which the step also quotes.

**What the direction therefore covers, and what it does not.** The book states and proves the fibre-level fact and defines the notion over a base; it does not, in these pages, state that a family $E\to S$ with a section is a group scheme over $S$ --- Theorem 4.11 quantifies over an elliptic curve over $k$ and over $k$-schemes $T$ (text version line 10152). The family-level passage is written on the card and remains the card's own, and by the direction above the book is the cited source for the step and Katz--Mazur is not to be awaited. The step is closed on that basis, not on a claim that the book states the relative form.

## 2026-11-19: V.2.8's part (a) is proved in every rank on its card from a published solution, and part (c) is repaired to the classification up to tensoring with an invertible sheaf and to a curve over $\CC$

**Object and need.** `P-AGH528STABLEBUNDLE` (V.2.8, printed p. 384), the printed exercise as it stands, and two records above: the §V.2 item's paragraph "V.2.8: part (a) in rank two, and part (c) over the complex numbers", and the card's own last event of 2026-11-16. The card's statement of (a) carries no rank hypothesis, so the card stated more than it proved, and its (c) stated a false classification and named no field.

**Evidence, part (a).** Yang Pi-Yeh, *Hartshorne Solutions*, Solution 5.2.8, printed pp. 103--104, read on the retained PDF `tmp/sources/lfwin-hartshorne-solutions.pdf`, whose pages 103 and 104 carry those folios. At the head of printed p. 104 the solution displays the weighted mean $\mu(\mathcal E)=\frac{r'}{r'+r''}\mu(\mathcal E')+\frac{r''}{r'+r''}\mu(\mathcal E'')$ for an exact sequence $0\to\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal E''\to0$, and its (a) reads: "If $\mathcal E=\mathcal F\oplus\mathcal G$ is stable, we may assume $\mu(\mathcal F)\le\mu(\mathcal G)$. Then consider the morphism $\mathcal E\to\mathcal F\to0$, we have $\mu(\mathcal E)<\mu(\mathcal F)$. Since $\mu(\mathcal F)\le\mu(\mathcal E)\le\mu(\mathcal G)$, we have $\mu(\mathcal E)<\mu(\mathcal F)\le\mu(\mathcal E)$, which is impossible." No rank hypothesis is used and no step of it is specific to rank two. The same two summand quotient sequences are in Algebraic Geometry II, National Taiwan University, 2020 Spring, *Chapter V Surfaces* homework, Exercise 8 of §2 (Tzu-Yang Chou), PDF p. 8 of `tmp/sources/ntu-ag2-chapter5.pdf`: "Decompose $\mathcal E$ as $\mathcal F\oplus\mathcal G$ and consider the short exact sequences $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal G\to0$ and $0\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal F\to0$. Looking at the slopes we see that $\mathcal E$ can not be stable." Gunning's Lemma 14, printed pp. 81--82, is not a proof of the general case, and the withdrawal recorded on 2026-11-16 was right: its decomposable clause is stated for a direct sum $\varphi_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\varphi_m$ of line bundles, its proof runs through his (13), and what he concludes from it, at the foot of printed p. 85, is the rank-two statement "every decomposable bundle is unstable". **Evidence, part (c).** The printed exercise, read at printed p. 384 of `tmp/sources/hartshorne-1977-algebraic-geometry.md` (PDF p. 399), reads "classified, up to isomorphism, by giving (1) an integer $0<e\leqslant2g-2$, (2) an element $\mathcal L\in\Pic C$ of degree $-e$, and (3) a nonzero $\xi\in H^1(\mathcal L^\vee)$ determined up to a nonzero scalar multiple". **Evidence.** N. Katz and B. Mazur, *Arithmetic Moduli of Elliptic Curves*, Annals of Mathematics Studies 108, Princeton University Press, 1985, read in `tmp/sources/katz-mazur-arithmetic-moduli-of-elliptic-curves.md` and on the rendered pages of `tmp/sources/katz-mazur-arithmetic-moduli-of-elliptic-curves.pdf`; in that scan printed p. $N$ is PDF p. $N+12$, so printed p. 63 is PDF p. 75 and printed p. 66, the last page of the proof, is PDF p. 78. Chapter 2 opens on printed p. 63 with (2.1.1): "Let $S$ be an arbitrary scheme. An elliptic curve $E/S$ is a proper smooth curve" --- the display carries $E\to S$ and the section "$0$" --- "with geometrically connected fibers all of genus one, given with a section '$0$'." Immediately below it stands **Theorem 2.1.2 (Abel)**: "There exists a unique structure of commutative group-scheme on $E/S$ such that for any $S$-scheme $T$, and any three points $P,Q,R$ in $E(T)=E_T(T)$, we have $P+Q=R$ if and only if there exists an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L_0$ on $T$ and an isomorphism of invertible sheaves on $E_T$ $I^{-1}(P)\otimes I^{-1}(Q)\otimes I(0)\simeq I^{-1}(R)\otimes f_T^*(\mathcal L_0)$", with $I(P)$ the ideal sheaf of a section as an effective Cartier divisor. Its proof, printed pp. 63--66, is exactly the relative statement that the card's step needed: the map $E(T)\to\Pic^{(1)}(E_T/T)$, $P\mapsto[I^{-1}(P)]$, is a bijection, proved by $R^1f_*\mathcal L=0$ and $f_*\mathcal L$ invertible of formation compatible with base change, cited to Mumford, *Abelian Varieties* (1970), p. 53, and by the zero locus of a local basis of $f_*\mathcal L$ being an effective Cartier divisor of degree one, hence a section by their (1.2.7), quoted on printed p. 66; composing with $\Pic^{(1)}\to\Pic^{(0)}$, $\mathcal L\mapsto\mathcal L\otimes I(0)$, transports the group law of the relative Picard group to $E(T)$, functorially in $T$, and the bijection gives uniqueness. The base is an arbitrary scheme, so the theorem covers the exercise's $S=\AA^1_\CC$ with room to spare, and it gives the fibrewise group laws as restrictions of morphisms $E\times_SE\to E$ and $E\to E$ over $S$ --- what the record of 2026-11-16 called the missing passage. The card's comparison with the book's language is Hartshorne's definition of a group scheme before Remark 4.10.5, printed p. 324, and Theorem 4.11, printed p. 325.

**What this closes, and what it does not.** The step's statement is now a published theorem and the card no longer says it is unproved; the conclusion of the solution and the remark on the published solution read the step as proved. ## 2026-11-19, third pass: Mumford's page 53 read, so the abelian-scheme step's base-change citation is verified and needs no projectivity

**Object and need.** `P-AGH4422FAMILYOVERAFFINELINE`, step `abelian-scheme`, after the two records of this date above. **Evidence, printed pp. 46, 50--51 and 53.** D. Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research Studies in Mathematics 5, Oxford University Press, 1970, Chapter II section 5, "Cohomology and base change", read on a scan of the book. The scan puts two book pages on one PDF page, so printed pp. 46--47 are PDF p. 28, printed pp. 50--51 are PDF p. 30 and printed pp. 52--53 are PDF p. 31, each folio read off the page. Printed p. 46 carries the section's basic result, that for a proper morphism of locally noetherian preschemes the higher direct images $R^pf_*$ of a coherent sheaf are coherent, and the **main theorem**: "Let $f: X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of noetherian schemes with $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ affine, and $\mathcal F$ a coherent sheaf on $X$, flat over $Y$", with a finite complex of finitely generated projective $A$-modules computing $H^p(X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathcal F\otimes_A B)$. **Corollary 2**, printed pp. 50--51, is the Grauert statement: for $\mathcal F$ as in the theorem and $Y$ reduced and connected, the constancy of $y\mapsto\dim_{k(y)}H^p(X_y,\mathcal F_y)$ is equivalent to $R^pf_*(\mathcal F)$ being locally free with $R^pf_*(\mathcal F)\otimes k(y)\to H^p(X_y,\mathcal F_y)$ an isomorphism for all $y$. **Corollary 3**, printed p. 53, is the one Katz and Mazur cite: "Let $X$, $Y$, $f$ and $\mathcal F$ be as above (unlike Corollary 2, $Y$ need not be reduced). Assume for some $p$ that $H^p(X_y,\mathcal F_y)=(0)$, all $y\in Y$. Then the natural map $R^{p-1}f_*(\mathcal F)\otimes_{O_Y}k(y)\to H^{p-1}(X_y,\mathcal F_y)$ is an isomorphism for all $y\in Y$." Corollary 4 follows it on the same page. Corollary 3 at $p=1$ and Corollary 2 at $p=0$ are precisely the two facts the card attributes to "Mumford, p. 53", so the citation is confirmed.

**What follows for the projectivity question.** Mumford's theorem is stated for a **proper** morphism over an affine noetherian base, with $\mathcal F$ flat, and a line bundle is flat; nothing in it asks for projectivity. So the step is carried by a published statement that needs only what the exercise gives, and the caveat recorded in the pass above --- that Hartshorne III.12.11 asks for a projective morphism --- is discharged rather than left standing. The rendered step now names Corollary 2 and Corollary 3 with their pages and no longer points to Hartshorne for this statement; the Hartshorne pages (III.12.11 at printed p. 290, Corollary 12.9 at printed p. 288) remain recorded in the card's earlier events.

Both readings confirm what the card already said about the two results; neither changes.

**The mathematics.** The classification does not need Gunning's setting in rank two. Let $\mathcal L$ be invertible of degree $-e<0$ and let $0\to\OO_C\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal L\to0$ be an extension. For a line subbundle $\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E$ the composite $\mathcal M\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal L$ is either zero, in which case $\mathcal M\subseteq\OO_C$ and $\deg\mathcal M\le0$ with equality only at $\mathcal M=\OO_C$, or injective, in which case $\deg\mathcal M\le\deg\mathcal L<0$. So $\OO_C$ is the only line subbundle of degree $0$, an isomorphism of two such middle terms must carry $\OO_C$ to $\OO_C$, and the automorphisms it induces on $\OO_C$ and on $\mathcal L$ are scalars, because a complete curve has $H^0(\OO_C)=k$; so isomorphic middle terms have classes differing by a nonzero scalar, and conversely scaling the class is scaling the inclusion and does not move the middle term. Nothing in the argument uses the characteristic, and nothing in steps `s7` to `s12` does either: `s7` needs an ample sheaf and global generation, `s11` Serre duality, both available over any algebraically closed field. Hence the classification of part (c), with the same data $(e,\mathcal L,[\xi])$ and the same bound $0<e\le2g-2$, holds over an algebraically closed field of any characteristic, and Gunning's Theorem 14 is its form over $\CC$.

## 2026-11-19, correction: the Katz--Mazur proof of Theorem 2.1.2 runs on printed pp. 64--67, and the card's rendering now follows its argument

**Object and need.** `P-AGH4422FAMILYOVERAFFINELINE`, step `abelian-scheme`, and the record of this date above, "IV.4.22's `abelian-scheme` step is a published relative theorem --- Katz--Mazur, Theorem 2.1.2, printed p. 63 with its proof on printed pp. 63--66". That record gives the wrong last page of the proof and the wrong page of (1.2.7), and the rendering of the proof on the card had two errors of substance: it made Mumford's Corollary 3 at $p=1$ give the constancy of $h^0$ and $R^1f_*\mathcal L=0$, which are not its statement, and it verified Mumford's Corollary 2 at $p=0$, whose hypothesis is that $Y$ be reduced and connected, only for $S=\AA^1_\CC$ while the theorem ranges over an arbitrary base.

**Evidence, the pages.** Katz and Mazur, *Arithmetic Moduli of Elliptic Curves*, read on the scan `tmp/sources/katz-mazur-arithmetic-moduli-of-elliptic-curves.pdf` at 160 dpi, where printed p. $N$ is PDF p. $N+12$. Printed p. 63 (PDF p. 75) carries (2.1.1) and the statement of Theorem 2.1.2 and ends with its display; the proof begins on printed p. 64 (PDF p. 76) with "What must be shown is that the map ... is bijective"; printed p. 66 (PDF p. 78) ends in the middle of the effective-Cartier-divisor argument, at "with $\mathcal L/\mathcal O$ flat over $S$. This amounts to the statement that the map of invertible sheaves"; printed p. 67 (PDF p. 79) carries the rest, including "By (1.2.7), any effective Cartier divisor of degree one is a section $P\in E(S)$ ... are inverse isomorphisms. Q.E.D.", and (2.2) begins below it. So the proof is printed pp. 64--67, and (1.2.7) is invoked on printed p. 67.

**Evidence, the argument.** The proof's steps, as the card now gives them: the bijection $E(T)\to\Pic^{(1)}(E_T/T)$ (printed p. 64); the reduction to $T=S$ and the Zariski-local patching using $f_*\OO_E=\OO_S$ (printed p. 65); the reduction to $S$ affine noetherian (printed p. 66); and, for an invertible $\mathcal L$ fibrewise of degree one, the claim that $f_*\mathcal L$ is invertible of formation compatible with base change and $R^1f_*\mathcal L=0$. Katz and Mazur prove the vanishing first (printed p. 66): "$R^1f_*\mathcal L=0$ because it is of formation compatible with arbitrary change of base (being an $R^1f_*$ for $f$ proper and flat of relative dimension one) and because over an algebraically closed field, $H^1(E,\mathcal L)=0$ for degree$(\mathcal L)>2g-2=0$. As $R^1f_*\mathcal L$ is a coherent sheaf on $S$ with all fibers zero, it vanishes by Nakayama's lemma." Then $f_*\mathcal L$ is locally free of rank one by [Mum 4, p. 53], Corollary 3 at $p=1$, together with the one-dimensionality of $H^0$ on the fibres, which is Altman--Kleiman (1.4) at printed p. 164 and (1.15) at printed p. 167. The effective Cartier divisor and (1.2.7) close the proof (printed p. 67). No reducedness or connectedness is used: Mumford's Corollary 3 is stated for $Y$ not necessarily reduced, and the reduction and localization carry the statement to an arbitrary base.

**What the earlier rendering got wrong.** Its "At $p=1$ the first gives constancy of $h^0=1$" is not Corollary 3: on the fibre, $h^0=1$ is the Riemann--Roch and Serre duality computation, and Corollary 3 at $p=1$ is the base-change isomorphism for $R^0f_*$. Its "at $p=0$ the second gives the invertibility ... $S=\AA^1_\CC$ being reduced and connected" applied Corollary 2 to one base only; Katz and Mazur's reduction to an arbitrary base, and their relative-dimension-one and Nakayama argument for $R^1$, are not in that rendering and are now on the card.

## 2026-11-19, fourth item: the classification of V.2.8(c) does not use that the ground field is algebraically closed, and the card keeps the printed hypothesis

**Object and need.** The last event of `P-AGH528STABLEBUNDLE` leaves open whether part (c) holds over a ground field that is not algebraically closed; the card states the classification over an algebraically closed field, the chapter's convention, and claims nothing beyond it. The question is worth settling because the whole argument is about slopes and line subbundles, and only two of its steps look at the field at all.

**The mathematics.** Let $k$ be any field and $C$ a geometrically integral smooth projective curve over $k$, with semistability read through $k$-rational quotients. Two things are to be shown.

*In rank two, semistability does not change under extending scalars.* If $E$ is not semistable over $\overline k$ there is a line subbundle $\overline M\subseteq E_{\overline k}$ with $\deg\overline M>\frac12\deg E$. The maximal-degree line subbundle of $E_{\overline k}$ is unique: two distinct line subbundles $\overline A,\overline B$ of the same degree $a$ have distinct generic lines, so $\overline A\oplus\overline B\to E_{\overline k}$ is injective and its determinant is a non-zero map $\overline A\otimes\overline B\to\det E_{\overline k}$, whence $2a\le\deg E$, which the maximal one violates. A singleton is stable under $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline k/k)$, so that subbundle descends to a line subbundle $M\subseteq E$ over $k$, and $\deg M=\deg\overline M>\frac12\deg E$; so $E$ is not semistable over $k$. The converse is immediate. Hence the two readings of "not semistable" agree in rank two, and no definitional ambiguity is left.

*The steps of the card that use the field use nothing of it beyond the conventions above.* Step `s7` needs an ample sheaf and Serre's theorem that $\mathcal E^\vee(n)$ is globally generated for $n\gg0$, both available over any field. Step `s11` needs Serre duality and that a line bundle with a non-zero section has non-negative degree; a non-zero section stays non-zero after base change, so $h^0(K_C\otimes\mathcal L)\ne0$ gives $2g-2-e\ge0$. Step `s12` needs that a line bundle of degree $0$ with a non-zero section is trivial, which base change to $\overline k$ decides. Step `s12b` needs that a non-zero map of line bundles is injective, true since $C$ is integral and a non-zero global section is non-zero at the generic point, and that an automorphism of an invertible sheaf is multiplication by a non-zero constant, which is $H^0(C,\OO_C)=k$ and holds because $C$ is geometrically integral and proper. Nothing else is used: the extension class, the bound on $e$, and the parametrization by the $k$-points of $\mathbb P H^1(C,\mathcal L^\vee)$ are all $k$-rational.

So the classification of part (c), with the same data $(e,\mathcal L,[\xi])$ and the same bound $0<e\le2g-2$, holds over any field for a geometrically integral smooth projective curve, with $\mathcal L\in\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ over $k$ and $[\xi]$ a $k$-point of the projective space.

**Impact and owner.** `QUAL-01` keeps a card's statement at the scope of its printed source, and the exercise is posed over the chapter's algebraically closed field; `PROSE-11` puts a deferred generalization in this file, not on the page. The card is therefore unchanged, and this record carries the generalization and the two places where it could have failed.

**Repair.** This record only, which changes no card. **Uncertainty.** Not checked: whether the descent step for the maximal line subbundle is written in any source on this machine, the argument being this record's own; and whether the statement survives when $C$ is not geometrically integral, where $H^0(C,\OO_C)$ is a proper finite extension of $k$ and the last clause of step `s12b` fails as stated.

## 2026-11-19, sixth item: the one clause of the rank-two classification that needs $C$ geometrically integral, and what the constants are without it

**Object and need.** The fourth record of this date leaves open whether the classification survives when $C$ is not geometrically integral; its statement of the generalization names that hypothesis, and exactly one clause of the proof uses it.

**The mathematics.** Let $C$ be a smooth projective integral curve over a field $k$ that is not algebraically closed in $k(C)$, and put $K=H^0(C,\OO_C)$. Then $K$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-algebra, because $C$ is proper, and a domain, because $C$ is integral, so $K$ is a finite field extension of $k$; and it is exactly the algebraic closure of $k$ in $k(C)$. One inclusion: an element $f\in k(C)$ algebraic over $k$ satisfies $f^n+a_{n-1}f^{n-1}+\cdots+a_0=0$, and at a point $P$ with $v_P(f)<0$ the term $f^n$ has the strictly smallest valuation, so the equation cannot hold; hence $f$ has no poles and lies in $H^0$. The other: $H^0$ is finite over $k$ and lies in $k(C)$.

Consequently $C$ is a curve over $K$ --- the identity $K=H^0(C,\OO_C)$ is a $k$-algebra map $K\to H^0(C,\OO_C)$, and $C\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is proper by cancellation over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ --- and the automorphisms of an invertible sheaf on $C$ are multiplication by the units of $K$, not of $k$. That is the single clause of the argument that geometric integrality supplies, the last one of step `s12b`; with $K\supsetneq k$ the middle terms of two extensions whose classes differ by an element of $K^*$ are still isomorphic, so the classification over $k$ would have to take the data up to $K^*$ rather than up to $k^*$, and the projective space of the statement is the wrong quotient. Nothing else in steps `s7` to `s12` uses geometric integrality: they use integrality only (a non-zero section of a line bundle is non-zero at the generic point, so a non-zero map of line bundles is injective), the vanishing of $H^0$ on negative degree, Serlet duality, and an ample sheaf.

**Impact and owner.** The card is unaffected, since an algebraically closed $k$ forces $K=k$. The generalization of the fourth record is restated as holding for a geometrically integral curve, that being exactly the hypothesis under which the $k$-rational statement has the stated form.

**Repair.** This record only, which changes no card. **Uncertainty.** Not checked: whether $C$ is geometrically integral over $K=H^0(C,\OO_C)$ when it is not over $k$, which the classification read over $K$ would need --- for perfect $k$ it is, since $K$ is then algebraically closed in $k(C)$ --- and whether the quotient of $H^1(C,\mathcal L^\vee)\setminus0$ by $K^*$ has a moduli interpretation.

## 2026-11-19, seventh item: the classification is a statement over the field of constants, and the last two open questions dissolve

**Object and need.** The fourth and sixth records of this date leave two questions open: whether $C$ is geometrically integral over $K=H^0(C,\OO_C)$ when it is not over $k$, which reading the classification over $K$ would need; and whether the quotient of $H^1(C,\mathcal L^\vee)\setminus0$ by $K^\times$ has a moduli interpretation. Neither arises once the base field is chosen correctly.

**The mathematics.** Let $C$ be a proper integral curve over any field $k$ and put $K=H^0(C,\OO_C)$, a finite field extension of $k$ because $C$ is proper and integral, as the sixth record shows; then $C$ is a proper curve over $K$ through the identity $K=H^0(C,\OO_C)$. Every place where the argument compares the ground field with the constants becomes an identity over $K$: the automorphisms of an invertible sheaf on $C$ are the units of $H^0(C,\OO_C)=K$; a non-zero map of line bundles is injective, for which integrality suffices, since a non-zero global section is non-zero at the generic point; a line bundle of degree $0$ with a non-zero section is trivial; $H^0$ vanishes on negative degree; an ample sheaf and Serre's global generation produce the maximal-degree line subbundle (step `s7`); and Serre duality with a non-zero extension class gives $0<e\le2g-2$ (step `s11`). So the classification of part (c) holds over $K$ with no geometric hypothesis at all. The fourth record named geometric integrality only because there $k$ was the given field and $H^0(C,\OO_C)=k$ had to be forced; against $K=H^0(C,\OO_C)$ that condition is satisfied by construction.

**The second question dissolves with the first.** $H^1(C,\mathcal L^\vee)$ is a $K$-vector space and $K^\times$ acts on it by scalars, so $H^1(C,\mathcal L^\vee)\setminus0$ modulo $K^\times$ is the projective space $\mathbb P H^1(C,\mathcal L^\vee)$ that the statement already displays, and there is nothing further to interpret. The sixth record's sentence that "the projective space of the statement is the wrong quotient" is true only of the wrong base field, namely $k$ when $K\supsetneq k$; over $K$ the quotient is the projective space itself.

**Impact and owner.** The card is unaffected, since an algebraically closed $k$ forces $K=k$. This record supersedes the hypothesis of the fourth record --- the classification there is stated for a geometrically integral curve, and it holds for every proper integral curve over its field of constants --- and closes the sixth record's open question about the $K^\times$-quotient.

**Repair.** This record only, which changes no card. **Uncertainty.** Not checked: nothing new was read for this record; it uses Serre's theorems over an arbitrary field, which this file does not cite to a printed page.

Theorem 3.2(2), printed p. 15, bounds the invariant of an indecomposable ruled surface by $2g-2$. Definition 4.3 and Proposition 4.4, printed p. 26, give the elementary transform and its intersection numbers. Theorem 4.9, statement printed p. 30 and proof printed p. 31, gives $e'=e+1$ and $\mathfrak e'\sim\mathfrak e-P$ at a point of the minimum-self-intersection curve. Corollary 4.10, printed p. 31, carries an indecomposable surface to a decomposable one by finitely many of these. Corollary 4.11, statement printed p. 31 and proof printed p. 32, carries any ruled surface to $X\times\PP^1$: from $X\times\PP^1$ one applies the elementary transforms at the points $P_if\cap X_0$ with $-\mathfrak e_0\sim P_1+\cdots+P_e$, which by Theorem 4.9 and Theorem 4.12(1), printed pp. 31--32, reaches the decomposable model $S_0$; Corollary 4.10 then supplies the sequence from $S$ to $S_0$, and Definition 4.3's inverse supplies the direction back. The only passage the statement leaves to the reader is the composition from one ruled surface to another, and the card's step `two-surfaces-joined` supplies it. Its steps transcribe these statements and use all three printed hints.

## 2026-11-19: V.2.17(b) in characteristics 2 and 3 is decided by the card's own extension class, and agrees with the printed answer

**Object and need.** `P-AGH5217CONORMALSPLIT` (Hartshorne V.2.17(b), printed p. 386) and [#160](https://github.com/dzackgarza/new-qual-site/issues/160), whose row for this card records part (b) open in characteristics 2 and 3: Yang Pi-Yeh's Jacobian presentation is undecided in characteristic 3 and unusable in characteristic 2. The card's own computation of the extension class is characteristic-free; this pass checks it against the book.

**Evidence.** Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry* (1977), V.2.17, printed p. 386, with the printed Answer "If $\operatorname{char}k\ne2$, then $l=m=-7$; if $\operatorname{char}k=2$, then $l,m=-6,-8$" (text version `tmp/sources/hartshorne-1977-algebraic-geometry.md`, printed p. $N$ = PDF p. $N+15$, the exercise under the marker of PDF p. 401). The card's step `s3` computes, on the affine chart with $q=c-ab$ and $h=b-a^n$, the substitutions $b=a^n+h$ and $c=a^{n+1}+ah+q$:
$$
ac^{n-1}-b^n=-a^{n^2-n}h+(n-1)a^{n^2-n-1}q\pmod{(q,h)^2},
\qquad c^n\equiv a^{n^2+n},
$$
so $h'\equiv-s^{-2n}h+(n-1)s^{-2n-1}q$; after the diagonal transition factors the extension class is $(n-1)\eta$, where $0\ne\eta\in H^1(\PP^1,\OO(-2))$. For $n=3$ this is $2\eta$, which is zero exactly when $2=0$. Hence characteristic 3 gives the non-split $\OO(-7)\oplus\OO(-7)$, the book's answer for $\operatorname{char}k\ne2$, and characteristic 2 gives the split $\OO(-6)\oplus\OO(-8)$ by step `s4`, the book's answer there. The printed answer is confirmed in both characteristics by the card's own proof.

**What changed.** `P-AGH5217CONORMALSPLIT` in `95de9c1cbf`, one `source-checked` event appended; no rendered sentence changed. This record changes no card.

**Acceptance, #160's V.2.17 row.** Met: part (b) is proved in characteristic 2 and in characteristic 3, and the printed answer is checked against the book. No published proof of those two characteristics is claimed; Yang's is sound away from 2 and 3, wrong in characteristic 3, and not the conormal's presentation in characteristic 2, as the card's remark says.

**Uncertainty.** Not checked: the card's other steps were not re-derived in this pass; only the computation of step `s3` was verified line by line; and no source outside Hartshorne and the retained Yang extraction was read for this card.

## 2026-11-19: V.4.10 closes with its three one-clause reductions proved on the card, printed p. 408

**Object and need.** `P-AGH5410NUMINEQ` (Hartshorne V.4.10, printed p. 408) and the record of 2026-11-16 that leaves its two transcribed arguments with the sources' one-clause reductions unproved. The exercise asks for a ``freshman calculus'' proof of $a^2-\sum b_i^2>0$ from the inequalities of (4.13)(a), printed p. 406. The card transcribes answer 2476483 and NTU Chapter V §4 Exercise 10, printed p. 17; both stop at three reduction assertions.

**What is now proved on the card, and why.** (i) At a maximiser with $b_5+b_6=a$ and $b_4\le a/3$, one has $b_2=b_3=b_4$: with $t=b_1=b_2$, $u=b_3$, $v=b_4=b_5$, the constraint $t+u+v\le a$ is automatic for $t,u\le v\le a/3$, and $2t^2+u^2$ is increasing in each variable there, so $t=u=v$; then $\sum b_i^2=5v^2+(a-v)^2\le a^2$ on $0\le v\le a/3$. (ii) At one with $b_5+b_6=a$ and $b_4\ge a/3$, one has $b_2+b_3+b_4=a$: if $t+u+v<a$, either $u<v$ and increasing $u$ raises $2t^2+u^2$, or $u=v$ and $t<v$, so increasing $t$ does. The two endpoint branches that follow are the card's, and both quadratics have maximum $a^2$ on $[a/3,a/2]$. (iii) In the case $b_5+b_6<a$, put $t=b_1=b_2$, $x=b_3-t$, $y=b_4-b_3$; then $u=t+x$, $v=t+x+y$, $w=2a-5t-3x-2y$, the constraints become $6t+4x+3y\le2a$ and $4t+2x+y\ge a$, and the sum of squares is a convex quadratic on that polygon, whose vertices $(0,a/2,0)$, $(a/3,0,0)$, $(a/4,0,0)$ and $(a/6,0,a/3)$ give $a^2$, $2a^2/3$, $7a^2/8$ and $5a^2/6$. Each reduction is marked on its step as the card's own; the transcriptions of the rest are unchanged.

**Repair, 2026-11-19:** `P-AGH5410NUMINEQ` in `c820143f0f`, and this record; no other card changes. The card is no longer relative to the sources' reductions.

## 2026-11-19: V.5.6 closes under #132's alternative, its own kind-(3) proof checked against the book

**Object and need.** `P-AGH556VALUATIONRINGS` (Hartshorne V.5.6, printed p. 420) and the published-solution obligation under #121/#132. Kinds (1) and (2) are transcribed from Egbert, printed p. 299, and Yang Pi-Yeh, printed p. 114. Kind (3) has no published proof in the sources read: Egbert asserts the decisive union, Yang prints $R=\varprojlim\OO_{P_i,X_i}=\bigcup_i\OO_{P_i,X_i}$ with no argument and with the limit mis-stated, and the two discussions located on 2026-11-15 (MathOverflow 12717, MSE 1125594) describe the trichotomy without proving $R\subseteq R_0$.

**What is checked here.** The card's own proof of kind (3) follows the printed hint. For $f\in R$, regard $f$ as the rational map $[f:1]:X\dashrightarrow\PP^1$ and resolve it by point blowups using Exercise V.5.1, printed p. 419; let $y_j$ be the centre of $R$ on the resolution $Y_j$. Comparing $y_j$ with the centres $x_i$ that define $R_0=\bigcup_iA_i$ gives $\OO_{Y_m,y_m}=A_N$ for some $N$. Since $f\in R$, the map $t\mapsto f$ gives a morphism $\Spec R\to\AA^1$ whose restriction to $\Spec K$ is $[f:1]$; the centre morphism $\Spec R\to Y_m$ followed by the resolution gives another extension of the same generic-point map, and $\PP^1$ is separated, so they agree. Hence $\psi(y_m)\in\AA^1$ and $f\in A_N\subseteq A_i$ for all $i\ge N$. With $R_0\subseteq R$ from step `union-contained-in-r`, this gives $R=R_0$. The argument is characteristic-free and uses only the valuative criterion, the domination of a discrete valuation ring by a valuation ring with the same fraction field, and the separatedness of $\PP^1$.

**Repair, 2026-11-19:** `P-AGH556VALUATIONRINGS` in `d50f09537a`, one `source-checked` event appended and no rendered sentence changed, and this record; no other card changes. Checks on the card: `./.venv/bin/python -m qualc.authoring check P-AGH556VALUATIONRINGS`, "schema and Markdown parsing OK (single card)"; `tmp/lam.sh` on the card file, numbering the steps 1 to 10 with QED labels present and no unknown step label; `./.venv/bin/python tools/sync_macros.py --check`, silent.

## 2026-11-19: the provenance sentence the per-card rule requires is missing on about 85% of the corpus's structured solutions

**Object and need.** The dispatch rule for the structured-proof programme (issue #2, owner's comment of 2026-11-06) says a structured proof is written from the retained solution set, that set and its page are cited in the card's `solution` section, and that **re-derivation is the fallback only when no retained set covers the exercise, "and the card says so."** This entry measures how often a structured card says so. It is a measurement, not an acceptance: a card without the sentence is not thereby wrong, but the programme's own record of where its arguments came from is absent on it.

**Observed evidence.** Screening over every corpus card file that has a `.solution` section and at least one `.pf-step` — the parser's own definition of a structured solution — for a provenance phrase in the solution text (`card's own`, `the card's`, `own argument`, `retained`, `transcrib`, `solution set`, `derived here`, `no published`, `re-derived`, case-insensitive):

| population | cards | phrase in the solution's opening paragraph | phrase anywhere in the solution |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| whole corpus | 10927 | 1545 (14.1%) | 1667 (15.3%) |
| residue 5 of queue D | 874 | — | 140 (16.0%) |

So **9260 of 10927 structured cards (84.7%) contain no provenance sentence anywhere in the solution.** The corpus grows under the measurement — other chats commit cards while it runs — so the figure is a snapshot taken at `main` = `a43976be1c5b` and the ratio is stable across two runs a few minutes apart (84.8% and 84.7%).

**Read before believing the screen.** Three cards the screen flags were opened at their solution opening and carry no such sentence in any wording: `P-AGFS15-05` (solution begins "Let $g(x)=(x-e_1)(x-e_2)(x-e_3)$", no attribution), `P-AGXHWREDUCED` (begins "Write $P$ for the presheaf $U\mapsto\OO_X(U)^\red$") and `P-ALGCOMP03-05` (whose solution opens directly with the `pf` block and step `s1`). The screen is a phrase match, so it can miss an unusual phrasing; it cannot invent one, and the three samples confirm the phenomenon is real rather than a markup artifact.

**What this does not show, and is not claimed.** No card's mathematics is asserted wrong; the same 1045 residue-5 files pass `qualc.authoring check` with zero failures, and the corpus gate is green at the tips that carry this session's commits (run records `309ff30e222b-20261119T075348.534Z` and `07bbc86eb690-20261119T080318.779Z`, exit 0, 0 diagnostics, 14402 cards and 341 wiki pages). The audit events, which do often say "the argument is the card's own", are bookkeeping and not the card, by the owner's own rule that an audit stamp is not the work.

**Impact and owner.** The sentence is one line per card and needs no mathematics; applying it across 9261 cards is a mechanical sweep that no single chat's residue covers, and the partition rule forbids a chat from editing cards outside its residue. So this is a dispatch decision, not a card repair: either the per-card rule is relaxed to allow the audit event to stand as the record, or a sweep is assigned with the exact sentence to insert. Nothing in this entry was edited on any card.

**Uncertainty.** The 84.8% is a screening figure over a phrase list, not a card-by-card read; the three samples above are the only cards opened to confirm it. Not checked: whether some cards state provenance in a `remark` outside the `solution` section (the screen would count them as absent), and no attempt was made to identify, per card, whether a retained set actually covers that card's exercise.

## 2026-11-19: the exp arrow of `P-AGH213SURJLOCAL` repaired to the two-argument form the macro needs, and the label settled above

**Object and need.** The entry of 2026-11-17 above ("Not repaired, and why") left one span unrepaired on purpose: `corpus/collections/SRC-TEXT-HART77/P-AGH213SURJLOCAL.md` line 58 wrote the exponential sequence as
`0 \to \underline{\ZZ} \injects (\OO_\CC, +) \surjectsvia{\exp} (\units{\OO_\CC}, \cdot) \to 0`,
and `\surjectsvia` is defined in `vocabularies/macros.json` as `\xrightarrow[#1]{#2}` — **two** arguments, the first below the arrow, the second above. Written with one argument, TeX takes the opening parenthesis of the next group as the second argument, so the label above the arrow becomes a `(` and the parenthesised pair loses its bracket. The record deferred it because "what the exp arrow of that sequence should say is a judgement about the mathematics"; this entry settles the judgement and the span.

**The judgement, and why it is not a guess.** In the exponential sequence $0\to\underline{\ZZ}\to(\mathcal O,\to)\xrightarrow{\exp}(\mathcal O^{\times},\cdot)\to0$ the map carrying a name is the one *out of* the middle term, i.e. $\exp\colon\mathcal O\to\mathcal O^{\times}$, and the name belongs above the arrow as its label; below-arrow labels in this corpus carry a hypothesis or a degree, of which there is none here. So the repair is `\xrightarrow{\ \exp\ }` — one arrow, label above, no second argument — and the parentheses of `(\units{\OO_\CC}, \cdot)` stay where they were.

**Checked by typesetting, not by reading.** A minimal document loading the author's own preamble (`TEXINPUTS` pointed at `~/.pandoc/styles` and its `macros/`) with `amsmath,amssymb,mathtools,amsthm` was run through `pdflatex -halt-on-error` twice: with the printed span it raised no fatal error but rendered a **doubled arrow** with the stray label (`pdftotext` of the page: `(OC , +) −−→→ (OC × , ·)`), and with the repaired span it renders a single arrow labelled $\exp$ (`(OC , +) −−−→ (OC × , ·)`), exit 0, one-page PDF. `\surjectsvia` now has no use in `corpus/` — the span repaired here was its only occurrence — and the mirror keeps only the macros the authored text uses, so `tools/sync_macros.py` drops the entry; the author's preamble still defines it, and a future use regenerates the entry.

**Repair, 2026-11-19:** `P-AGH213SURJLOCAL`, the single display on line 58, no statement or proof step changed. Checks: `./.venv/bin/python -m qualc.authoring check P-AGH213SURJLOCAL`, "schema and Markdown parsing OK (single card)"; `./.venv/bin/python tools/check_macros.py` on the card, OK; `./.venv/bin/python tools/sync_macros.py --check`, silent; `pdflatex -halt-on-error` on the repaired span with the project preamble, exit 0. The card carries no `pf-step`, so the Lamport filter has nothing to report for it and no numbering changed.

**Uncertainty.** Not checked: the rendered page in a browser, since the site is built in CI; the claim about what a reader saw rests on the LaTeX render above and on Pandoc's treatment of the two-argument macro. Only the one display was typeset, not the whole card, and the judgement about where the label belongs is a reading of the sequence, not a quotation from a source.

## 2026-11-19, second item: the provenance screen misses possessives and the word "outline", and one genuine absence it found on a card of residue 3 is repaired

**Object and need.** The entry above measures how often a structured card states where its argument came from, by screening the solution text for a phrase list, and reports 84.7% of structured cards carrying no such sentence. It warns that "the screen is a phrase match, so it can miss an unusual phrasing; it cannot invent one". This item quantifies that risk on a population I could hand-check, and repairs the one genuine absence the check found.

**The hand-check.** One hundred cards whose solutions I wrote or restructured were screened with the entry's phrase list and then opened at the solution's opening paragraph:

| population | flagged as lacking | actually lacking on reading |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| my 100 cards | 24 | **0** |

All twenty-four do state provenance, in phrasings outside the list: "The diagnosis and the counterexample are those of **Dan Whitman …**" (thirteen cards), "The route is that of Sam …", "The argument is that of **Kenneth DeMason …**", "The device of always taking a least index … is **Dan Whitman's**", "The argument is this collection's outline, written out". So on this population the screen's false-positive rate is 24 of 24 — its misses are the pattern `is that of` / `are those of`, the possessive `Whitman's`, and the noun `outline`.

**The refined screen, and what it changes corpus-wide.** Adding those three families to the list (`is that of`, `are those of`, `outline`, and possessives of the retained sets' authors) and re-screening every card that has a `.solution` and at least one `.pf-step` at `main` = `f7c0b46577`:

| screen | structured cards | carrying a phrase | lacking |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| as published above | 12248 | 1694 (13.8%) | 10554 (86.2%) |
| refined | 12248 | 1798 (14.7%) | 10450 (85.3%) |

The corpus-wide figure moves by less than a point, because most structured solutions open directly with the `pf` block and have no introductory paragraph at all; on the population I could check, the refinement removes twenty of twenty-four false positives. Both numbers are upper bounds on absence, and the hand-checked sample is the only place where that bound was tightened.

**The one genuine absence, repaired.** On my hundred cards the refined screen leaves four, of which three are still false positives (`E-MUN-9-3`'s possessive; `P-CH10-37` and `P-CH15-37`, which say "this collection's outline"), and one was real: `E-SSA.PR-3` (Stein--Shakarchi Appendix A Problem 3) opened straight into "The defect in the printed display", with no statement of where the argument came from. Its solution now opens: "No retained solution set covers this problem: the argument below is the card's own, with the printed sources it uses named at each step, and the defect in the printed display is dealt with first. The statement was checked against Stein--Shakarchi, *Complex Analysis*, Appendix A, §5, Problem 3, printed pp. 341--343." Nothing else on the card changed; the five numbered steps and their text are as committed in `d49f51f0f7`.

**Repair, 2026-11-19:** `E-SSA.PR-3`, the solution's opening sentence only; and this record. Checks: `./.venv/bin/python -m qualc.authoring check E-SSA.PR-3`, "schema and Markdown parsing OK (single card)"; `tools/check_macros.py` on the card, OK; the Lamport filter over the card's body, five numbered steps, unchanged; `./.venv/bin/python tools/sync_macros.py --check`, silent.

**Uncertainty.** The 24-of-24 false-positive rate is measured on one hundred cards by one reader, not a random sample of the corpus, and a card could state provenance in a wording neither the old nor the refined list contains — the refined list was built from the phrasings this sample used, so it is tuned to it. Not checked: the 10450 cards the refined screen still flags, none of which was opened; and whether a card's prose names a retained set that does not in fact cover its exercise, which no phrase screen can decide.

**The reading, and what it shows.** All forty open with either the `pf` block itself or a line of setup — a change of variable, a goal, a definition to be used — and none carries a sentence saying where the argument came from, in any wording. So on this sample the screen is right, and the corpus-wide figure is not an artifact of vocabulary: **40 of 40 flagged cards genuinely lack the sentence**, where the earlier sample of cards written to the rule was 0 of 24. The two results together are consistent and worth stating as one: the phrase list is unreliable on cards whose author wrote the sentence, and reliable on the bulk of the corpus, which did not.

Some of the forty show a second phenomenon, which is a card defect in its own right rather than a provenance question: a few open inside a proof rather than with a statement — `P-3MDGM` begins `::: pf-step Simplify the integrand …`, `E-HK-26-3` begins `**Goal.** Find homogeneous …`, and `P-BKF10-3A` begins with a step statement `Choose $M>0$ such that …`. Those are cards whose `solution` section's opening paragraph has been dissolved into the proof, so a provenance sentence has nowhere natural to go; they are recorded and not repaired, since each needs its solution section read to decide where the setup belongs.

**What this does not show.** It does not identify, per card, whether a retained set covers that card's exercise, so it does not say that the arguments are re-derived; it says only that the card does not state its provenance. Forty cards is a sample: at 40 of 40 the 95% upper bound on the true absence rate is about 7%, so the corpus-wide 85% is not in doubt, but the sample cannot certify any individual card.

**Uncertainty.** The sample was drawn once with a recorded seed and was not stratified by collection. The reading was done on the first 220 characters of each solution; a card that puts its provenance sentence at the end of its solution would be misread, and no such card was seen among the forty. This entry was written twice: the first write was lost when another stream rewrote this file from a snapshot taken before it, which is recorded here because the same thing will happen again to a chat that appends to this file without re-reading it immediately before writing.

**Method notes for whoever works a residue next.** The residue of an id is the segment after the **last** hyphen, so `E-HAT-4.2-1` has suffix `1` and residue 1 while `E-HAT-4.2-29` does not. `qualc.authoring check` accepts a card path as well as an id. `tmp/lam.sh` takes a **file path** and its step numbering is the quickest check that a `pf` block is well formed. A new `audit:` event must be inserted **inside the audit list**: in a card whose frontmatter carries `review:` after the audit block, inserting before the closing `---` produces invalid YAML, `qualc.authoring check` reports `expected <block end>, but found '-'`, and `tools/backlog.py` fails the same way, which is how this session found the mistake it had made. And the shared clone's branch tip and the remote both move within seconds: `git commit --no-verify -- <path>` stages one card without sweeping another session's index, and a push is best made from a branch pinned at the exact commit with `expected_remote` read immediately before it.

**Uncertainty.** The residue scan matches on frontmatter `id` rather than through the queue's own loader, so a card whose id field disagreed with its filename would be counted once and listed under the id it states; 0 such disagreement was found, since every id in the scan resolved to its own basename. The two gate findings above are read from the gate's own output and their repairs are not attempted here.

## 2026-11-19: a scripted delimiter rewrite deleted the absolute values on a card, and what caught it

**Object and need.** `E-SSA.PR-5` was restructured into steps by a script that also had to convert its absolute-value delimiters, because the corpus gate refuses the raw forms on any line a commit introduces. The conversion was first written as `.replace(r"\lvert","").replace(r"\rvert","")` — a deletion of the two delimiters rather than a wrapping of what lies between them. That silently removed the absolute values from every site in the card while leaving text that still parses. This entry records the fault, how it was caught, the recovery, and the rule the next scripted edit should follow; the memory of this file carries no equivalent.

**What was damaged.** Twelve `\lvert … \rvert` pairs, three of them inside a table:

- `$(q\lvert\xi\rvert)^{1/2}$` became `$(q\xi)^{1/2}$` — the modulus dropped from the weight-$\tfrac12$ factor;
- `$e^{-\pi y'/(12q^2\lvert\xi\rvert^2)}$` became `$e^{-\pi y'/(12q^2\xi^2)}$` — a complex quantity where a modulus belongs, in the cell that explains why the essential singularity is $q^2$ times flatter at $p/q$;
- `$\lvert\xi\rvert\ge\sqrt{y'}/q$` and `$\lvert f\rvert\le Ce^{\pi/(12y'/(q^2\lvert\xi\rvert^2))}$` likewise, and the same loss at eleven further sites.

Every one of these still parses, so `qualc.authoring check` — schema and Markdown — passed on the damaged card.

**What caught it.** Two things, neither of them the schema check alone. The gate's `unread-math` diagnostic fired on the reconstructed file: a rewritten cell read `$ c_{p/q}=\sqrt q$`, with a space after the opening `$`, which pandoc declines to read as math and the check reports as "a \$ reached the page as text: write \$x\$ not \$ x \$". Following that lead into the same table exposed the dropped moduli. Separately, reading one transformed line per construct — not just the first — showed `(q\xi)^{1/2}` where the source had `(q\lvert\xi\rvert)^{1/2}`.

**Recovery.** The card was restored from `74ce2a7b19` (the commit before the restructure), the conversion redone with a **wrapping** substitution — `\lvert X\rvert` and `|X|` both rewritten to `\abs{X}`, never to nothing — and every construct re-read afterwards. The restored card carries `\abs{\xi}`, `\abs{c_{p/q}}`, `\abs{c_k}` and the rest, and passes the gate.

**The rule this yields.** A scripted replacement of a *delimited* construct must be written as a wrap, never as a deletion of the delimiters: `.replace` on a token that wraps content is a deletion by construction, and no parser will tell you, because the text it leaves is well-formed. After any scripted edit over a card, read one output line per transformed construct and compare it with the input line; a schema check answers only whether the file still parses.

**Which delimiter forms the gate refuses, as observed this session.** Raw `|` inside math (`|c_k|`, `\bigl|…\bigr|`, `\Bigl|…\Bigr|`) and the paired `\lvert`/`\rvert` both draw `STYLE-04`; the accepted spelling is `\abs{…}`. Whether the gate is scoped to the lines a commit introduces or to the whole staged file was **not determined** here: the pre-restructure card carried `\lvert` at twelve sites and had been committed, while the same spellings were refused in the rewritten file.

**Uncertainty.** No other card was searched for the same fault, and no claim is made that the deletion was confined to this one — only that this card is repaired and that the checks named above are the ones that would expose it again.

## 2026-11-19: V.2.5(c) at g≥2 is proved in every characteristic, closing #160's row for the card

**Object and need.** `P-AGH525INVARIANTE` (Hartshorne V.2.5, printed p. 377) and the last part of #160's row for it: (c) for $g\ge2$ was proved only over characteristic zero, by Lange--Narasimhan's Corollary 1.2, printed p. 58, whose proof is the secant-variety dimension count.

**The argument.** Let $d=-e$ with $1\le d\le g$ and fix $D$ of degree $d$. Extension classes of $0\to\OO_C\to\mathcal E\to\OO_C(D)\to0$ lie in $V=H^1(C,\OO_C(-D))$, of dimension $g-1+d$ by Riemann--Roch and Serre duality. For an effective $E$ of degree $d-1$, the classes for which $L_E\subseteq H$ are $\ker\beta_E$, of dimension $d-1$, because $\deg(K_C+D-E)=2g-1$ gives $h^0(K_C+D-E)=g$. For $d\ge2$ the bad pairs $(E,\xi)$ form a family of dimension $(d-1)+(d-2)=2d-3$ in $\PP V$; for $d=1$ the only $E$ is $0$, whose kernel is zero. Since $2d-3<g-2+d$ for $d\le g$, a general $\xi$ avoids every kernel. Part (b) makes the extension normalized, and a nonzero $\xi$ makes it indecomposable, since a splitting would realize $\OO_C$ and $\OO_C(D)$ as summands. Its determinant is $\OO_C(D)$, so $\PP(\mathcal E)$ has invariant $-d=e$. This is the avoidance argument the printed hint asks for and it is characteristic-free.

**Impact.** The row is met in all four parts over an algebraically closed field of any characteristic: (a) and (b) were already characteristic-free on the card, (c) is now `s9` for $g\ge2$ and Example 2.11.6 for $g=1$, and (d) is Lange's Theorem over an arbitrary characteristic, printed pp. 267--268. Lange--Narasimhan's Corollary 1.2 remains in the remark as the characteristic-zero alternative.

**Repair, 2026-11-19:** `P-AGH525INVARIANTE` in `3c9312f304`, one `source-corrected` event, the proof of step `s9`, the qed, the remark and the solution preamble; no statement changes. Checks: `./.venv/bin/python -m qualc.authoring check P-AGH525INVARIANTE`, "schema and Markdown parsing OK (single card)"; `tmp/lam.sh`, numbering the steps 1 to 12 with QED labels present and no unknown step label.

**Uncertainty.** Not checked: no source outside those already on the card was read for this argument, which is the card's own; the dimension count was checked on paper, not symbolically, and no characteristic assumption is used.

## 2026-11-19, sixth item: 1314 steps in 546 cards justify nothing — a defect class no queue measures, counted by a scanner and named for the cards of residue 3

**Object and need.** Queue D measures cards whose solution holds **no** numbered step; issue #2's requirement is that every **substantive step** carry its justification. Nothing in the corpus's measurements looks at the second half of that sentence, and the sample of forty recorded above turned up cards whose steps are statements with an empty `pf-proof` — the container omitted, or the argument left in the step's own sentence. This item counts that class and gives the method, so a later pass can re-run it rather than re-derive it. It is a measurement and not an acceptance: an empty proof block is sometimes a **container** step whose argument is in the nested steps above it, and the scanner excludes exactly that case, but it cannot tell a step whose justification is embedded in its claim from one that has none. Each flagged card needs a reading.

**The method.** For every card with a `.solution` and at least one `.pf-step`, scan the solution line by line with a stack: a line opening a `pf-proof` pushes a proof frame, a line opening a `pf-step` pushes a step frame, a bare `:::` pops. A proof frame is **vacuous** when its body holds no non-blank text and no nested `pf-step`. Run at `main` = `a615d5c25d`:

| population | structured cards | cards with a vacuous step | vacuous steps |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| whole corpus | 12249 | **546** | **1314** |
| residue 3 of queue D | 912 | 38 | 112 |

So 4.5% of structured cards carry at least one step that states a claim and justifies it with nothing. The worst five in the corpus are `E-SS3.PR-1` (7 of 38 steps), `P-7Q5AM` (7 of 34), `E-HK-42-9` (7 of 29), `E-26ELV` (6 of 40) and `P-M81A1-3` (6 of 36).

**Two examples read in full, and what the class actually contains.** `E-26ELV` step `s1` is "Part (a): Perturbation of proper maps." with an empty proof and four nested steps beneath it — that is a container, and it is unobjectionable except that its own sentence is a title. Its nested steps are the defect: "Since $\bar\rho(f,g)<1$, $\|f(x)-g(x)\|\le1$ for all $x$" carries an empty proof, and the justification is compressed into the claim itself. `E-2TY2B` step `s1` is "Part (a): Equivalence relation and well-defined metric $D$." with an empty proof and five nested steps, the first of which ("**Equivalence relation:**" with the three axioms listed as bullets) also has an empty proof. So the class mixes two things a scanner cannot separate: a **title step** with an empty proof, and a **claim step** whose justification is written inside the claim. The first is a style defect, the second is the defect issue #2 names.

**The cards of residue 3, named for the next pass.** Thirty-eight cards of this residue carry vacuous steps; the twelve worst, with their counts of vacuous over total steps, are `E-26ELV` 6/40, `P-M81A1-3` 6/36, `P-FZIG3` 5/31, `P-AMD-6OJQMSOZ` 5/26, `E-2TY2B` 5/25, `P-XLANN` 4/26, `P-PATOJ` 4/23, `P-APAS15F` 4/20, `P-APAS26B` 4/19, `E-HK-42-3` 4/16, `E-5QSZ7` 3/22 and `P-EVBF7` 3/18. They are listed here with the measurement so that the next pass over this residue starts from the worst rather than from the queue, which is empty for it.

## 2026-11-19: V.4.8's third alternative is characteristic-free, closing #160's row for the card

**Object and need.** `P-AGH548IRREDCLASSES` (Hartshorne V.4.8, printed pp. 407--408) and #160's row for it: the nonsingularity of the member of alternative (c) was Bertini's theorem in characteristic zero, and the characteristic-$p$ case was open.

**The argument.** Now on the card: the linear system $\linearsystem{D}$ is base-point-free with a reduced irreducible general member (Harbourne, Lemma II.6(b), preprint p. 4, over an arbitrary algebraically closed field). Hence the morphism $\varphi:X\to\PP^N$ it defines is separable: an inseparable morphism onto its image pulls a general hyperplane back to a non-reduced divisor. By Hartshorne II.8.6A, printed p. 174, Lemma 8.9, printed p. 175, and Proposition 10.4, printed p. 270, $\varphi$ is smooth on a nonempty open set $U$. The bad hyperplanes are those tangent to $\varphi(X)$ at a point of $U$ — a linear subspace of codimension $2$ in the dual, dimension $N-3$ — and those meeting $\varphi(X\setminus U)$ — the dual of a curve, dimension $N-1$. Their union has dimension at most $N-1$, so a general hyperplane $H$ avoids it, and $\varphi^{-1}(H)$ lies in $U$ and is nonsingular. This is the incidence count in Vakil, *The Rising Sea* (21 October 2025), Theorem 13.4.2 and its proof, printed p. 375, applied to the linear system $\linearsystem{D}$; the characteristic-zero Corollary III.10.9, printed p. 274, is no longer used.

**Impact.** The card is characteristic-free throughout, and #160's row for it is met. No statement changes.

**Repair, 2026-11-19:** `P-AGH548IRREDCLASSES` in `7d548c5699`, one `source-corrected` event, the final step, the solution preamble and the remark; no statement changes. Checks: `./.venv/bin/python -m qualc.authoring check P-AGH548IRREDCLASSES`, "schema and Markdown parsing OK (single card)"; `tmp/lam.sh`, numbering the steps 1 to 9 with QED labels present and no unknown step label; the style check reports no raw bar.

**Uncertainty.** Not checked: the passage from reducedness to separability is the card's own statement, not a quoted theorem; the dimension count was checked on paper; and no source outside Hartshorne, Harbourne and Vakil was read for this argument.

## 2026-11-19: V.4.7's degree-4 attainment is proved in every characteristic, so the card claims every degree

**Object and need.** `P-AGH547GENUSBOUND` (Hartshorne V.4.7, printed p. 407) and the second half of its statement, "for every $d>0$, this maximum is achieved by some irreducible nonsingular curve". The bound itself was never in question; the card excluded $d=4$ over a field of characteristic $p>0$, because the class attaining the maximum at $d=4$, $H+F_{56}$, was placed through Bertini's characteristic-zero corollary, Corollary III.10.9, printed p. 274. The card's audit events of 2026-11-16 and the entry of that date here recorded that exclusion as open rather than hiding it, and the retained solution (Egbert) writes "For $d=4$, I don't know".

**The argument.** $H+F_{56}=4\ell-(e_1+e_2+e_3+e_4)-2(e_5+e_6)$, so with $D=a\ell-\sum_i b_ie_i$ one has $a=4$, $b=(1,1,1,1,2,2)$ and $\sum_ib_i=8$; by Proposition 4.8 of the book, printed pp. 401--402, $d=3a-\sum_ib_i=4$, $D^2=16-12=4$ and $p_a=\tfrac12(4-4)+1=1$, the maximum the exercise allows for $d\equiv1\pmod3$. Against the $27$ lines, $D\cdot E_i=b_i>0$, $D\cdot G_i=2a-(\sum_kb_k-b_i)=b_i>0$, and $D\cdot F_{ij}=a-b_i-b_j$, which is $2$, $1$ or $0$, vanishing at $F_{56}$ alone. So $D$ meets every line nonnegatively and has $D^2>0$: it is condition (c) of [[P-AGH548IRREDCLASSES|Exercise V.4.8]], whose sufficiency that card now proves in every characteristic (the entry above, `7d548c5699`), by Dolgachev's Theorem 8.2.19, Harbourne's Corollary II.3, Theorem III.1(a) and Lemma II.6(b), and Vakil's incidence count. Hence $H+F_{56}$ contains an irreducible nonsingular member over any algebraically closed field, and the maximum is attained at every $d>0$. The characteristic-zero corollary is no longer cited for this degree.

**Impact.** The card now claims attainment at every $d>0$ over an algebraically closed field of any characteristic, in the statements of steps `nonsingular-members` and `conclusion` and in the degree-4 paragraph. Its two events of 2026-11-16 that say no characteristic-$p$ attainment is claimed are superseded by the new event and left as written, as the corrections of that date are; the same holds for the sentence in the entry of 2026-11-16 here that calls the $d=4$ case open.

**Repair, 2026-11-19:** `P-AGH547GENUSBOUND` in `aadc2c2d34`, one `source-corrected` event, the statements of steps `nonsingular-members` and `conclusion`, and the degree-4 paragraph of the former's proof; the exercise's own statement is untouched. Checks: `./.venv/bin/python -m qualc.authoring check P-AGH547GENUSBOUND`, "schema and Markdown parsing OK (single card)"; `tmp/lam.sh`, numbering the steps 1 to 9 with QED labels present and no unknown step label; `tools/check_macros.py`, OK; the recomputation of $a$, $\sum_ib_i$, $d$, $D^2$, $p_a$ and the three intersection numbers above; and the hypotheses of condition (c) as `P-AGH548IRREDCLASSES` states them.

**Uncertainty.** Not checked in this pass: Dolgachev's Theorem 8.2.19 and Harbourne's Lemma II.6 beyond the statements and pages the V.4.8 card records, and no source outside those named on the two cards. The dependence is one-way — this card's degree-4 case is only as good as that card's characteristic-free proof, which is why the two were repaired in that order.
