## 2026-11-19: §3.3 closed — the last five cards read, and a UCT inference in 3.3-31 repaired

**Object.** The last report left `E-HAT-3.3-14`, `-16`, `-26`, `-27`, `-31` as the remaining §3.3 cards. All five are read against Hatcher at their printed pages (14 on p. 258; 16, 26 on p. 259; 27, 31 on p. 260), and with them **every card in §3.3 now has a read on or after 2026-11-13** — 35 of 35.

| Card | Printed page | Mathematics checked / defect repaired |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `E-HAT-3.3-14` | Ex. 14, p. 258 | correct: the collapse $r_{2k+2}$ (a map, not a retraction) sends the loop to $k+1$ basis commutators and $k$ commutators to $k$, against Exercise 12 with $k+1$; and the two retractions kill the class while it is nonzero |
| `E-HAT-3.3-16` | Ex. 16, p. 259 | correct: capping twice truncates twice and multiplies the two evaluations, which is capping with the cup product; descent, associativity and the unit checked |
| `E-HAT-3.3-26` | Ex. 26, p. 259 | correct: the two top products are the orientation class, the squares and cross-summand products vanish — exactly, because $H^4(M)$ injects into the sum of the summands' $H^4$ — and the rest vanish for degree reasons |
| `E-HAT-3.3-27` | Ex. 27, p. 260 | correct: primitive vector, symplectic correction, orthogonal splitting, nonsingular restriction, induction, and the sign change giving the printed block |
| `E-HAT-3.3-31` | Ex. 31, p. 260 | **repaired**: the passage from $H_n(M,B;G)=0$ to the boundary isomorphism |

**The repair.** `E-HAT-3.3-31` argued: $H_n(M,B;G)=0$ for every $G$; take $G=\QQ/\ZZ$ and "the universal coefficient theorem shows $H_{n-1}(M,B;\ZZ)$ is torsion-free"; then "since the cokernel is torsion-free, $\partial_A$ must be onto". Neither half holds. A torsion-free cokernel does not force surjectivity — $\ZZ\xrightarrow{0}\ZZ$ has torsion-free cokernel and is not onto — and $\QQ/\ZZ$ gives more than torsion-freeness: the universal coefficient sequence
$$0\to H_{n-1}(M,B;\ZZ)\otimes\QQ/\ZZ\to H_n(M,B;\QQ/\ZZ)\to\operatorname{Tor}(H_{n-2}(M,B;\ZZ),\QQ/\ZZ)\to0$$
gives $H_{n-1}(M,B;\ZZ)\otimes\QQ/\ZZ=0$, and a finitely generated group with that property vanishes, so $H_{n-1}(M,B;\ZZ)=0$. The fragment is then $0\to H_n(M,\partial M;\ZZ)\xrightarrow{\partial_A}H_{n-1}(A;\ZZ)\to0$, an isomorphism, which yields both $H_{n-1}(A;\ZZ)\cong\ZZ$ — so the component is orientable — and that $\partial_A$ is multiplication by a unit. The rest of the card was checked and stands: the triple sequence, the excision of $\partial M-A$, the component reduction, the mod-two case, and the change-of-coefficients argument for general $R$ including the $2R=0$ alternative. Bredon's printed pp. 356–357, which supply the vanishing, were not re-read this pass; the event of 2026-11-07 records that reading.

**Not done, and open.** The #170 source obligations are unchanged: no complete published solution located for `E-HAT-2.B-3`, `-2.B-4`, `-2.B-5`, `-2.B-7`, `-2.B-9`, `E-HAT-2.C-1`, `-2.C-6`, `E-HAT-3.3-21`'s bracketed question, `E-HAT-4.1-1`, `-4.1-7`, `-4.A-1`. those four exercises; the exercises are V.4.2 on printed pp. 406--407 and the other three on
printed pp. 406--407 as the cards state them.

**V.4.1, `P-AGH541CONICSQUADRIC`.** Yang's entry takes the conics through $P_1=(1,0,0)$,
$P_2=(0,1,0)$ with basis $x_0x_1,x_1x_2,x_2x_0,x_2^2$, maps them to $y_1,y_2,y_3,y_0$, reads
$y_0y_1=y_2y_3$ off the image, and identifies the graph of $(x,y,z,w)\mapsto(x,z,w)$ with the blowup of
$\PP^2$ at the two points through the saturation of $(x_0x_1,x_1x_2,x_2x_0,x_2^2)$. It then asserts
"$\pi\circ\psi=\mathrm{id}_{\PP^2}$, and $\psi\circ\pi=\mathrm{id}_Y$", the same two false
compositions the card already corrects for Egbert's entry: $\pi\circ\psi$ is the blowup map on $X'$
and $\psi\circ\pi$ is undefined at the blown-up point. The card's remark now says the correction
applies to Yang's entry word for word.

**V.4.2, `P-AGH542QUADTRANSFORM`.** The entry is Egbert's computation in the same coordinates — the
substitution $(x,y,z)\mapsto(yz,zx,xy)$ into a curve of multiplicity $r_i$ at $P_i$, the division by
$x^{r_1}y^{r_2}z^{r_3}$, and the two displayed numbers $2d-r_1-r_2-r_3$ and $d-r_2-r_3$ — and adds
nothing; it does not discuss a component of $C$ through a centre, which the card's intersection-number
argument covers.

**V.4.5, `P-AGH545PASCAL`.** The entry proves the collinearity from Corollary 4.5 of the book,
printed p. 400 (PDF p. 415), rather than by naming Cayley--Bacharach: the cubic $S\cup PQ$ passes
through the eight points $A,B,C,A',B',C',P,Q$ in which it meets $AB'\cup BC'\cup CA'$, so the ninth,
$R$, lies on it, and $R\notin S$ because the line $AB'$ meets the conic in $A$ and $B'$ only. The
corollary's genericity hypotheses are not checked in the entry; the card's step
`extends-to-degenerate-case` supplies the specializations in which they fail.

**V.4.6, `P-AGH546QUARTICBASE`.** The entry states the hypothesis in linear-algebra form, the
thirteen vectors of the fifteen degree-four monomials having rank $13$, which makes the quartics
through the thirteen points a pencil; two members meet in $16=4\cdot4$ points, the thirteen and three
more, and a third member is a linear combination of the two. It gives no geometric hypothesis on the
thirteen points, which is the exercise's second question and the content of the card's two hypothesis
steps, and it counts the sixteen points without multiplicities.

hypothesis gives only $D\cdot L\ge0$; the hypothesis $D^2>0$ that the exercise adds for exactly that
case is never used. The instance is $H+F_{56}$, the class of the V.4.7 card: it meets $F_{56}$ in $0$,
meets all $27$ lines nonnegatively and has square $4$, so condition (c) gives it a nonsingular member
while the strict criterion does not apply to it. The card's own proof — Harbourne's Lemma II.6 and
Theorem III.1(a) with Dolgachev's Theorem 8.2.19 — does not depend on the entry.

**V.4.13, printed p. 111: both parts.** Part (a) counts the sixteen curves on the blowup at five
points, the five $E_i$, the ten $F_{ij}=H-E_i-E_j$ and the conic $G=2H-\sum_{i\le5}E_i$. Part (b)
computes $h^0(\OO_X(2))=h^0(\OO_X(-2K))=\frac12(-2K-K)\cdot(-2K)+1=3K^2+1=13$ by Riemann--Roch, with
$h^1=0$, and concludes $h^0(\mathcal I_X(2))=15-13=2$. That conclusion needs the restriction
$H^0(\OO_{\PP^4}(2))\to H^0(\OO_X(2))$ to be onto, which the entry does not prove — projective
normality is what supplies it — and it then states the complete-intersection conclusion without the
degree count. The audit event of 2026-11-16 recorded the second point and said nothing of the first;
the remark now carries both, at the page.

**V.4.14, printed p. 112: the table is there and is right.** The text version
`tmp/sources/lfwin-hartshorne-solutions.md` prints the entry as "As following." and then nothing, the
nine-row table being an image it drops. On the page the table has nine rows, one for each printed pair,
and each was recomputed here from $d=3a-\sum b_i$ and $p_a(D)=\frac12(a-1)(a-2)-\frac12\sum b_i^2+\frac12\sum b_i$:
$(8;3,3,3,3,2,2)$ gives $d=8$, $p_a=21-22+8=7$; $(8;4,3,3,2,2,2)$ gives $8$ and $6$; $(9;4,3,3,3,3,2)$
gives $9$ and $9$; $(9;4,4,3,3,2,2)$ gives $9$ and $8$; $(9;4,4,4,2,2,2)$ gives $9$ and $7$;
$(10;5,3,3,3,3,3)$ gives $10$ and $11$; $(11;5,5,4,3,3,3)$ gives $10$ and $10$;
$(12;5,5,5,5,3,3)$ gives $10$ and $9$; $(10;6,3,3,3,3,2)$ gives $10$ and $8$. Every row also satisfies
the very-ampleness conditions $b_i>0$, $a>b_i+b_j$ and $2a>\sum_{j\ne i}b_j$, the last with the least
margin at $(12;5,5,5,5,3,3)$, where $2a=24$ against $23$. So the card's sentence that the entry gives
the same nine pairs as a table of classes is right, and its further sentence, that the entry does not
show a member to be nonsingular, is right as well: nonsingularity is Corollary 4.13(b) or the card's
own step, not the table.

**Repair.** `P-AGH548IRREDCLASSES` in `cb7cbe820e`, `P-AGH5413DELPEZZO4` in `8a45e47a4f`; this record
in the COMPLAINTS commit that carries it. No statement, step or hypothesis of either card changes, and

**Object and need.** Queue D is a measurement of numbered steps, so a residue reaches zero while most of its cards have never been read for correctness. This records the size of that gap for residue 3 (`int(id.rsplit("-",1)[1], 36) % 16 == 3`), measured today, so that "the residue is complete" is not mistaken for "the residue is checked".

**Measured.** Of the residue's cards that carry a `.solution` and at least one `pf-step`:

| quantity | count |
| --- | ---: |
| residue-3 cards with a solution section | 839 |
| of those, carrying a `solution-reviewed` event | 369 |
| carrying none, i.e. structured but never read | **470** |

The same query over another residue would give a different split; the point of the table is the method, not this residue's number. The counts were taken from the card text, not from a database, and a card whose review event is written by a different `by:` or in a different phrasing still counts as reviewed — the test is presence of the string `solution-reviewed`.

**What a referee pass found on the fourteen cards read.** No mathematical defect: a diagonal uncountability argument, a Cauchy continuation for an ODE solution confined to a compact set, a quotient of the interval that is not Hausdorff, a rational-solution argument for rational linear systems, the degree of a self-map of `CP^{2n}`, strict diagonal dominance, two prime non-maximal ideals, the cone on a disk, integrability of `f^2`, a `p`-subgroup's fixed point, a closed bounded non-compact set, `k`-transitivity, a Kunneth computation for `L(p,1) x L(q,1)`, and `pi_3` of `P v S^3`. One **structural** defect did surface, on `P-TOPS25F`: its frontmatter held an `- event:` list with no `audit:` key above it, so the file did not parse. That fails the whole-corpus gate for every stream, not just its own, and it was repaired.

**Ruled out lane-wide, cheaply.** Because one unparseable card anywhere makes every gate run fail — and the gate prints nothing until it finishes, so a killed run shows no reason — the per-card parser was run over all 839 cards of the residue: `839/839` schema and Markdown OK. The same sweep gives `839/839` clean for undefined control words (`tools/check_macros.py`) and `839/839` clean for the Lamport filter (`tmp/lam.sh`). Corpus metadata completeness is `12429` complete, `0` incomplete.

**Consequence.** A residue's conversion reaching zero should be reported as conversion reaching zero, with the never-reviewed count beside it. At two or three referee reads per turn, residue 3's 470 is roughly 150 turns of work, which is a work item of its own rather than an extension of the conversion stream.

**Uncertainty.** Only fourteen of the 470 were read, chosen by file length and not at random, so the 0-of-14 defect rate is not an estimate of the residue's defect rate; short cards are plausibly easier to get right than long ones. The `solution-reviewed` test is a string match over the whole file, so a card could carry the string in prose without an event. Nothing here was checked against the corpus database or the gate, the gate being unrunnable on this box today (the entry above records both kills).

## 2026-11-19: Yang's 5.5.4 gives the matrix proof of negative definiteness, with one false hypothesis named; and V.4.15(c)'s properness put to a swarm

**Object and need.** `P-AGH554CONTRACTEDCURVES` (Hartshorne V.5.4, printed p. 417) and, separately,
the last open item of the §V.4 batch that is a mathematical question rather than another stream's
card work: the properness of the bad locus in V.4.15(c), open under
[#157](https://github.com/dzackgarza/new-qual-site/issues/157).

**V.5.4, Yang's entry at printed p. 113.** Part (a): a very ample $H$ on $X_0$ has
$f^*H\cdot Y=H\cdot f_*Y=0$ and $(f^*H)^2=H^2>0$, so Hodge index gives $Y^2<0$ — the entry says
$f^*H$ is ample on $X$, which is false for a pullback under a birational morphism, and the nef form of
Hodge index is what the argument uses. Part (b) is the matrix proof: with the factorization of $f$,
$H_2\sim H_1+\sum m_iY_i$ for $m_i=\operatorname{ord}_{Y_i}(f)>0$, so $S'=MSM$ has $S'_{ij}\ge0$ off
the diagonal and $\sum_iS'_{ij}=-H_1\cdot m_jY_j\le0$; the identity
$\sum_{i,j}v_iv_jS'_{ij}=\sum_j(\sum_iS'_{ij})v_j^2-\sum_{i<j}S'_{ij}(v_i-v_j)^2$ makes $S'$ negative
semidefinite, strict negativity at a $j$ whose $Y_j$ meets $H_1$ and the connectivity of
$\bigcup Y_i$ make it definite. That is a published proof of (b) that does not run through the
factorization into point blowups, and it is the same argument as the NTU homework's Exercise 4 of §5;
the card's own step reaches the conclusion by Hodge index on the blown-up model, and both stand.

**V.4.15(c): the properness, put to a swarm.** Part (c) of the exercise, printed p. 409, asks for a
dense $V\subseteq\PP^2$ such that adjoining any $P_{r+1}\in V$ to a general-position $r$-tuple keeps
general position, on an uncountable field, with the hint that a variety is not a countable union of
proper closed subsets. The card's reduction leaves exactly the properness of each bad locus $B_w$,
one for each finite word $w$ of admissible transformations: closedness is proved, and of the three
branches its reduction isolated, $m_N=0$ is empty by Nagata's Proposition 3, printed p. 279, $m_N=1$
is the whole plane exactly when the fixed system is superabundant, and $m_N\ge2$ was left open. A
swarm of six members was started this date on the question as stated — prove each $B_w$ proper, or
refute it — with the card's reduction given as a claim to check and not as established. Its report
will be recorded here, with the verdict, when it arrives; nothing on the card changes until then.

**Repair.** `P-AGH554CONTRACTEDCURVES` in `6b6e1c71a2`; this record in the COMPLAINTS commit that
carries it. No statement, step or hypothesis of the card changes.

**Uncertainty.** Read for this record: Yang's Solution 5.5.4 at printed p. 113, rendered as a page
image; Hartshorne's V.5.4 on printed p. 417 and V.4.15 on printed p. 409; and the card's own steps on
part (c). Not read: Nagata's paper beyond the statements the card quotes; the printed books
themselves; and no search of the literature for a published proof of the properness.

## 2026-11-19: V.4.15(c) proved for r <= 7 — the terminal collinearity is the effectivity of a class of square -2 and K-degree 0, which a Del Pezzo surface cannot carry; r >= 8 stays open

**Object and need.** `P-AGH5415GENPOSITION`, Hartshorne V.4.15(c), printed p. 409, and
[#157](https://github.com/dzackgarza/new-qual-site/issues/157). The card carried (c) only on the
properness of the bad locus, which its step `bad-locus-proper-closed` asserted and did not derive; the
reduction of this date left $m_N=0$ empty by Nagata's Proposition 3, $m_N=1$ equivalent to
superabundance, and $m_N\ge2$ open.

**The step that closes it for $r\le7$.** Follow the classes through a word $w$: a quadratic
transformation centred at three current points replaces $h$ by $2h-c_1-c_2-c_3$ and the three
exceptional classes by $h-c_j-c_k$, an integral orthogonal transformation of $\operatorname{Pic}$ that
fixes $K=-3h+\sum_ic_i$. So for a terminal triple $\{a,b,c\}$ the class
$D=h_w-c_a-c_b-c_c$ is fixed by $w$ alone, with $D^2=-2$, $K\cdot D=0$, $D\cdot h_w=1$, and the
terminal triple is collinear exactly when $\linearsystem{D}\ne\emptyset$: a member meets each of
$c_a,c_b,c_c$ in $1$, has none as a component, and maps to a line through the three. Now take $P$
outside the closed locus where the $r+1\le8$ points fail Dolgachev's conditions of general position
(no three collinear, no six on a conic, no cubic through them singular at one of them; Definition
preceding Proposition 8.1.9, printed p. 251). There $X=\operatorname{Bl}_{r+1}\PP^2$ is a Del Pezzo
surface by that proposition, $-K$ is ample, every nonzero effective class has negative $K$-degree, and
$K\cdot D=0$ with $D\ne0$ gives $\linearsystem{D}=\emptyset$. Hence each bad set misses a nonempty
open set, its closure is proper, and the countable union of those closures has dense complement: (c)
holds for $r\le7$, with $V$ the complement of that union and of the finitely many points and lines.
No uncountability is needed in that range; it enters only at $r\ge8$, where $-K$ stops being ample
($(-K)^2=0$ at nine points, not nef beyond) and the question is as the card states it.

**Two corrections the step needed.** The bad sets are *not* closed: definedness of a word is an open
condition, so what the argument uses is that each bad set is contained in a proper closed set, the
effectivity locus, and that the closures are proper. And at $r=7$ one more closed condition must be
excluded, the cubic through the eight points singular at one of them: without it Dolgachev's
Proposition 8.1.9 does not apply, and "$-K$ ample from no three collinear and no six on a conic" is
false at eight points. Both are recorded in the step, which now also cites that proposition and page.

**The swarm.** Six members on `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` at max effort; all six reports judged
and accepted. Four of them (d3, d6, d4 and, with a weaker range, d1) reached the $r\le7$ conclusion by
this route, one (d2) certified by exact computation that no counterexample occurs for $r\le6$ and words
up to length five and located the $r\ge8$ gap at the independence of the prescribed-multiplicity
conditions, which the retained Nagata pages do not settle for a fixed tuple plus one moving point. Two
of the six claimed shorter ranges ($r\le6$ apart from one class, $r\le4$) and were corrected in the
verdicts: the missing class is a root like the others and dies on the Del Pezzo locus.

**Repair.** `P-AGH5415GENPOSITION` in `85b5c838d2`, with the wording of the same step corrected in
`f2e09365df`; this record in the COMPLAINTS commit that carries it. No other step changes: (a), (b),
(d) and (e) and the numbers $56$ and $240$ are untouched, and part (c) is claimed for $r\le7$ only.

**Uncertainty.** Read for this record: Hartshorne V.4.15, printed p. 409; Dolgachev's definition of

**V.5.3, printed p. 113: the book's hint carried out.** (III, Ex. 8.1) with (III, Ex. 8.3) gives
$H^i(\widetilde X,\pi^*\Omega_X)\cong H^i(X,\Omega_X)$; the sequence
$0\to\pi^*\Omega_X\to\Omega_{\widetilde X}\to\Omega_{\widetilde X/X}\to0$ with
$\Omega_{\widetilde X/X}\cong\Omega_E$ gives the long exact sequence, in which
$H^0(\Omega_E)=H^0(\PP^1,\OO(-2))=0$ and $H^1(\Omega_E)=H^1(\PP^1,\OO(-2))=k$; Serre duality with the
birational invariance of $h^1(\OO)$ makes $H^2$ an isomorphism, so
$0\to H^1(X,\Omega_X)\to H^1(\widetilde X,\Omega_{\widetilde X})\to k\to0$ is exact and splits. The
identification $\Omega_{\widetilde X/X}\cong\Omega_E$ is quoted, not computed — the local calculation
the hint asks for, which the card's own step carries out.

**V.5.2, printed p. 113: the vanishing, then a citation.** With $m=-Y^2>0$ and $k=H\cdot Y$ for a very
ample $H$ with $H^1(\OO_X(H))=0$, the entry gets $(mH+iY)\cdot Y=m(k-i)$, hence
$\OO_Y(mH+iY)\cong\OO_{\PP^1}(m(k-i))$ with vanishing $H^1$ for $i\le k$, and deduces
$H^1(\OO_X(mH+iY))=0$ by induction. Then $M=\OO_X(mH+kY)$ has $M\cdot Y=0$ and $M\otimes\OO_Y\cong\OO_{\PP^1}$,

$f_1:X\to\PP^N$ with $f_1^*\OO(1)\cong M$ contracting $Y$. The rest it leaves to "the proof of
Castelnuovo's theorem", which is where the exercise's assertion that the image is a projective variety
lies; the card's own steps carry that out.

## 2026-11-19: Dolgachev's fourth general-position condition bites only at eight points — the r <= 7 step of V.4.15(c) reads it that way, and why r = 8 does not follow from it

**Object and need.** The step `properness-r-at-most-seven` added to `P-AGH5415GENPOSITION` earlier
this date, which cited Dolgachev's four general-position conditions on printed p. 251 for every
$N\le8$, and the state of part (c) at $r=8$.

**The reading.** Dolgachev's definition lists (i) proper points, (ii) no three on a line, (iii) no six
on a conic, (iv) no cubic through the points singular at one of them, and Proposition 8.1.9 says the
blowup of $N\le8$ points is a Del Pezzo surface exactly in that position. Read literally at $N\le7$,
(iv) always fails: a cubic singular at one of the points and through the other $N-1$ imposes
$3+(N-1)\le9$ conditions on the ten coefficients of a cubic, so such a cubic exists for every position
of the points, while the blowup at $N\le7$ general points is a Del Pezzo surface of degree $9-N$. A
condition that always holds cannot be part of a criterion that can fail, so at $N\le7$ the criterion is
(ii) and (iii) and the printed (iv) bites only at $N=8$, where the count is square, $8+2=10$: the eight
points through the cubic and the node at one of them. That is also how his own sufficiency argument
uses it, removing the last point and checking that it lies on no $(-2)$-curve, the lines through three
and the conics through five of the remaining points being what (ii) and (iii) exclude. The step now
says this, and the closed condition excluded at $r=7$ is the nodal cubic through the eight.

**Why $r=8$ does not follow.** At nine points $(-K)^2=0$, so $-K$ is at best nef and the argument
above has nothing to kill: an effective class of square $-2$ and $K$-degree $0$ is not excluded by
positivity, and on a rational elliptic surface such classes are exactly the $(-2)$-curves carried by
the reducible fibres. Whether every word's class is ineffective at a fixed general nine-point
configuration is the superabundance question the swarm's reports located, and no source read here
settles it. So $r\ge8$ stays open, and it is not an oversight of the $\mathrm{Del}$ Pezzo step: the
step is sharp at $r=7$ and cannot be pushed one further.

**Repair.** `P-AGH5415GENPOSITION` in `0a4313a210` for the step's sentence and `92eb27fdfc` for the
audit event; this record in the COMPLAINTS commit that carries it. No other step, and no part-(c)
claim beyond $r\le7$, changes.

**Uncertainty.** Read for this record: Dolgachev's definition and Proposition 8.1.9 with its proof,
printed p. 251 (PDF p. 261). Not checked: any printed statement of the $N\le7$ reading in so many
words; the classification of reducible fibres of rational elliptic surfaces, which is where the $r=8$
obstruction lives, beyond the general statement that reducible fibres carry $(-2)$-curves; and no
search of the literature for the superabundance question.

## 2026-11-19: Yang's §V.1 entries begin to be named — 5.1.8 and 5.1.9 at printed p. 101, and eighteen Chapter V cards still without him

**Object and need.** `P-AGH518COHOMCLASS` (V.1.8, printed pp. 367--368) and `P-AGH519HODGEINDEX`
(V.1.9, printed p. 368), both of which named Egbert alone.

**V.1.9, printed p. 101.** Yang gives both parts of the hint. (a) $E=(H^2)D-(H\cdot D)H$ has
$E\cdot H=0$, so Hodge index gives $E^2\le0$, and
$E^2=(H^2)^2D^2-(H^2)(H\cdot D)^2$ divided by $H^2>0$ is $H^2D^2\le(H\cdot D)^2$, with equality only
for $D$ numerically zero. (b) on $C\times C'$ with $H=l+m$, $E=l-m$, $H^2=2$, $E^2=-2$, $H\cdot E=0$,
the class $D'=-4D+2(a+b)H-2(a-b)E$ has $D'\cdot H=0$ and $D'^2=16D^2-32ab$, so $D^2\le2ab$ with
equality only for $D\equiv bl+am$. Both are Egbert's arguments; the card's steps carry the same two
computations.

**V.1.8, printed p. 101.** Part (a) is the commutative square with the trace map on $D$:
$c_D(F)=(\deg F)\cdot1$ by (III, 3.7.4), so $\langle c(D),c(E)\rangle=\deg_D(\OO(E)\otimes\OO_D)=D\cdot E$;
part (b) is the linear-independence count: a relation $\sum_ki_kc(D_k)=0$ tested against $c(E)$ for
every divisor $E$ gives $(\sum_ki_kD_k)\cdot E=0$, so numeric independence forces every $i_k=0$ and
$\Num X$ embeds in the dual of the finite-dimensional $H^1(X,\Omega_X)$.

**What this pass did not read.** The Hartshorne pages 367 and 368 carry no text layer; the earlier
events on both cards record them as read at 110 dpi renders, and this pass compared Yang's entries with
the statements the cards carry rather than reopening them. The audit events say so.

## 2026-11-19: four sourcing gaps behind issue #174's second review — a locator refuted against the book, one found but not recordable, a bibliography key that cannot anchor a page, and a card swept into another stream's commit

**Object and need.** The second review of [#174](https://github.com/dzackgarza/new-qual-site/issues/174) found that proofs had been added to standard results in `corpus/theory/Algebra/` against QUAL-10, which says "Do not add proofs to standard results". Withdrawing them exposed what they had stood in for: the citations those cards do not have. Four things were established, and one of them cannot be finished from this session.

**Observed evidence.**

(a) `T-SMTHN` carried `[@DF04, p. 479]` on "two $m\times n$ matrices over $R$ are equivalent if and only if they have the same Smith normal form". The locator is wrong for that sentence. In a scan of the 3rd-edition chapter 12 (`https://wiki.math.ntnu.no/_media/ma3201/2019h/dummit_foote_ch_12_pids.pdf`, retrieved) the running foot of that page reads "Sec 12.2 The Rational canonical Form 479", and p. 479 prints Theorem 21, the Smith normal form of $xI-A$ for an $n\times n$ matrix over a field $F$; it states neither the general principal-ideal-domain form nor anything about two matrices being equivalent. The citation is removed and what the page does print is recorded in a remark on the card (`6d64362347`). The general statement over a PID now has no verified locator: DF04 sets the row-and-column argument as Exercises 16--19 of §12.1, printed pp. 470--471, and says there that it is "a proof of Theorem 5 in the special case where $R$ is a Euclidean Domain"; the formula $a_i=d_i/d_{i-1}$ is Exercise 35 of §12.2, again for $xI-A$.

(b) `T-GRDSOC` and `T-GRDPD` rest on "a zero-dimensional Gorenstein local ring has one-dimensional socle", which `D-SCHCMGOR` asserts inside an `.example` and with no source; a result inside an example cannot be cited as if proved (`SEC-11`). The statement is a numbered theorem in C. Huneke, "Hyman Bass and Ubiquity: Gorenstein Rings", arXiv:math/0209199: **Theorem 5.3, printed p. 11** (page header "HYMAN BASS AND UBIQUITY: GORENSTEIN RINGS 11"), whose list makes "R is injective as an R-module", "the socle of R is 1-dimensional" and "R is Gorenstein in the sense of Grothendieck/Serre" equivalent, so citing it is not circular against a definition of Gorenstein by its own socle. It cannot be attached from here: `vocabularies/references.yaml` opens "exported from the Zotero library by `tools/sync_bibliography.py`. Do not edit: add the work to Zotero instead", and there is no key for the work. **Owner action: add it to Zotero, re-export, then state the socle fact as its own proposition on `D-SCHCMGOR` and cite `[@Hun99, Theorem 5.3]`.** The Stacks Project cannot supply the step: its commutative-algebra book has no occurrence of "socle", and none of "Lasker" or "primary decomposition" either, so it states neither this result nor Lasker--Noether, and tag `00L4` is Lemma 10.62.2 on supports, not a primary-decomposition statement.

(c) The `AM18` entry is the 2018 CRC reprint, DOI 10.1201/9780429493638, with no edition and no page count. The page numbers in circulation for Atiyah--Macdonald are the 1969 Addison-Wesley ones, so any locator written `[@AM18, p. N]` is ambiguous until the entry pins an edition.

(d) `corpus/collections/SRC-TEXT-SS03/appendix-a-problems/E-SSA.PR-5.md` carries a 120-line change inside `a0dbfc4d2e` ("T-PIO2B, T-YHH3M: Maschke and Schur carry their proofs"), a commit about two algebra cards. That change was not authored in this stream: it was another stream's staged working-tree content swept into the commit, and two commits of that stream (`9f5c759e3c`, `09594961d3`) rewrote the card afterwards. Nothing on it is repaired under #174.

**Impact and owner.** (a) and (c) are repaired and recorded here. (b) blocks the citation on two cards in `corpus/theory/Algebra/` and needs the Zotero entry first; until then `D-SCHCMGOR` still carries the claim inside an example. (d) belongs to the stream that wrote `E-SSA.PR-5`.

**Uncertainty.** In (a) the page was read from a retrieved scan, so the refutation holds for the 3rd edition and not for any other. In (b) the equivalence is verified in the retrieved paper text, and whether a printed book states it was not checked: no copy of Eisenbud (`Eis95`, already a key) or of Matsumura or Bruns--Herzog was retrieved, and no page number was guessed for them.

## 2026-11-19, correction: the §1.2 and §1.3 Hoffman--Kunze cards read in this session are not residue 5

**What this corrects.** The ninth item above opens "The residue-5 cards of `SRC-TEXT-HK71` §1.3 whose exercise numbers are 4–8", and the sixth and seventh items describe the §1.2 cards the same way. That is wrong. Under the partition rule the lane is $\operatorname{int}(\text{id after the last hyphen},36)\bmod 16 = 5$, and the suffixes of the cards read this session give other residues: `E-HK-12-6` 6, `E-HK-12-7` 7, `E-HK-12-8` 8, `E-HK-IF5V` 6, `E-HK-CG7N` 3, `E-HK-RTYK` 12, `E-HK-PNK2` 2, `E-HK-1EVA` 6, `E-HK-D0GP` 9, `E-HK-YECG` 0. §1.4 has no residue-5 card at all (its ten cards are residues 3, 9, 0, 4, 6, 9, 12, 9, 14 and 11).

Nothing is withdrawn as mathematics or as a record of what was checked. What is withdrawn is the claim that these cards belong to this chat's share of the partition.

**Why it happened, and the rule taken from it.** The lane was defined over the cards of queue D; the Hoffman--Kunze cards are all structured and none of them is in that queue, so they carry no partition assignment. This chat extended "residue 5" to every card in the corpus, which is the convention other lanes use for their residue's cards, but did not check the arithmetic for the cards it was reading — it took a section's cards as its own because the collection was the one it had been working. The rule taken: before touching a card outside queue D, compute its residue; if it is not 5, report the defect rather than edit the card.

## 2026-11-19: Yang's 5.1.1, 5.1.5 and 5.3.2 at printed pp. 100 and 107 — two more cards of the sweep, and one sign slip in the third entry

**Object and need.** `P-AGH511EULERCHAR` (V.1.1, printed p. 366), `P-AGH515KSQUARED` (V.1.5, printed
p. 367) and `P-AGH532MULTINTER` (V.3.2, printed p. 394), three of the sixteen Chapter V cards counted in
the record above as still not naming Yang.

**V.1.1, printed p. 100.** Riemann--Roch gives $\chi(\mathcal L^{-1})=\frac12C\cdot(C-K)+\chi(\OO_X)$,
and the same for $D$ and for $C+D$; the alternating sum is
$$
\tfrac12\bigl((C+D)\cdot(C+D-K)-C\cdot(C-K)-D\cdot(D-K)\bigr)=C\cdot D,
$$
with no transversality assumed. That is the exercise's identity, and the card's own step covers the
general case that Egbert's two proofs reach only for transverse curves.

**V.1.5, printed p. 100.** (a) $K_X\sim(d-4)H$ with $H^2=d$ gives $K_X^2=d(d-4)^2$; (b)
$K_X=p_1^*K_C+p_2^*K_{C'}$ by (II, 8.3), and $C^2=C'^2=0$, $C\cdot C'=1$ leave
$0+2(2g-2)(2g'-2)+0=8(g-1)(g'-1)$.

**V.3.2, printed p. 107, with one slip.** The entry writes $\widetilde C=\pi^*C+\mu_P(C)E$; the strict
transform is $\pi^*C-\mu_P(C)E$, the pullback being $\widetilde C+\mu_P(C)E$. With the minus sign
$\widetilde C\cdot\widetilde D=C\cdot D-\mu_P(C)\mu_P(D)$, and $\widetilde C\cdot\widetilde D=0$ at a
single intersection point gives $C\cdot D=\mu_P(C)\mu_P(D)$, which is the entry's conclusion; with the
printed plus sign the product would rise, not fall. The remark names the slip and says the conclusion
uses the corrected sign.

## 2026-11-19, tenth item: §3.C read in full — nine cards, three rewritten, six correct

**Object and need.** The next section of the staleness sweep was §3.C, *H-Spaces and Hopf Algebras*,
whose sixteen exercises are printed on pp. 291–292; nine of its cards carried an audit date before
2026-11-13. All nine are read here and all sixteen cards of the section now carry a 2026-11-19 or
2026-11-18 read.

**Correct, with what was checked.** `E-HAT-3.C-2` (p. 291): $\mu_A=r\circ\mu\circ(i\times i)$ works
because $r(e)=e$, which is what the hypothesis that the retract contains the identity buys.
`-3.C-10` (pp. 291–292): the Künneth step of (a) is the only place freeness and finite generation
enter; the $S^3$ generator is primitive since no bidegree $(i,j)$ with $i,j>0$ sums to $3$; the
quaternionic polynomial in (c) is proper with degree $n$. `-3.C-12` (p. 292): $\alpha$ and $\beta$
primitive, the binomial coproducts with no Koszul sign because $\abs{\beta^i}=2i$, and the dual
relations $x^2=0$, $y_iy_j=\binom{i+j}{i}y_{i+j}$, $xy_i=y_ix$. `-3.C-15` (p. 292): the coproduct
$\Delta(a_n)=\sum_i\binom ni(q_n/q_iq_{n-i})a_i\otimes a_{n-i}$ and the passage back from $\QQ$ to
$\ZZ$ through torsionfreeness of $A\otimes A$; cocommutativity and coassociativity come from the
formula on the generator, not from assumptions on the multiplication. `-3.C-16` (p. 292): the
coefficient table $b_{ij}$ — binomial for $d$ even, zero for $i,j$ both odd and
$\binom{\lfloor(i+j)/2\rfloor}{\lfloor i/2\rfloor}$ otherwise for $d$ odd — checked independently at
$n=2$ and $n=3$; Lemma 1, the three cases of Lemma 2, and the algebra of Theorem 3 in cases (a) and
(b) recomputed symbol by symbol, with the observation that neither case uses the size of $e_{ij}$,

coefficients are the exercise's.

base-point-free nonspecial divisor of (IV, Ex. 6.8) gives $D=C+Ef$ with $D^2=2r$. Part (b) identifies
sections with morphisms $C\to\PP^1$, so the possible $r$ are their possible degrees. Two slips:

$\PP^1$ would make $C$ rational; and its parenthetical doubts whether both $r=2$ and $r=3$ can occur at

## 2026-11-19, twelfth item: a degraded corpus report can be committed and then report itself up to date; and a branch switch in the shared checkout diverts other sessions' commits

**Two failures of the tooling and one of mine, all measured today.**

**A degraded report is sticky.** When the corpus fails validation, `tools/backlog.py` returns only the `corpus-validation` section plus the provenance and completeness queues and prints a small queue count. Today one such run — three errors, all `\generations` for `\generators` in `corpus/theory/Algebra/PR-ASW5L.md` — was committed, and every later run then printed `BACKLOG.md: up to date`, because the generated file matched the committed degraded one. "Up to date" therefore does not mean "the corpus validates"; it means "the report has not changed since someone last committed it". A reader who takes it as a green gate is misled, and the audit queues (duplicate-bodies, duplicate-exams, orphans, empty-provenance, dead and forbidden hrefs) say nothing at all in that state. The three offending tokens are still in the file: `I=\generations 0` and twice `I=\generations m`, in residue 9.

**A branch switch in the shared checkout is not a private act.** `main` and the remote had diverged, so a fast-forward push was impossible. I created a branch at the remote tip and checked it out. Six commits from other sessions then landed on that branch rather than on `main`, because every session in this checkout commits to whatever HEAD points at. The repair — re-applying each of the six to `main` by taking its file from the commit and committing it with its original message plus a line saying it was moved — preserved every byte and rewrote no history, but it cost those sessions their commit identity and a few minutes of confusion. **The rule:** in one shared clone, never `git checkout` another branch, not even to escape a divergence. A divergence gets reported and waited out; this one resolved itself within minutes when another session pushed a line that already contained the local commits.

**What the pushes did.** Over this session, `github_push` returned `github_remote_changed` while `git ls-remote` reported the same SHA across repeated checks, and returned `github_unavailable` once when GitHub did not answer; in every case the commits later appeared in `main` inside another session's push. The only reliable check is `git merge-base --is-ancestor <mine> <remote>`, never the push call's return.

**What could not be verified.** Fourteen cards have sheets that are scans with no text layer and no `_extracted.md`: the eleven of `SRC-ART-ALG-2003-2009-PRELIMS` and `SRC-ART-ALG-2010-2015-PRELIMS`, two in the UGA Fall 2003 preliminary (`P-F03C1`, `P-FKEN5`), and `P-ALGPAN11-01`, whose review sheet holds only headings in text and images for the questions. The only extraction route in the repository is `just ocr-pdf`, which runs `tools/mistral_ocr.py` against an external service; nothing was sent. They are blocked, not deferred.

**Measured, not yet worked.** Of the residue's cards that name no source at all, 279 collections hold at least one and 137 cards sit outside any collection. The largest sheet-backed groups — `SRC-GRE-MATH-SUBJECT` 18, `SRC-MATHEMATICAL-TRIVIUM` 17, `SRC-MATH4100-6100-2020` 16, `SRC-TOP-WORKSHOP` 13, `SRC-UCSD-TOP-JUSTIN` 11, `SRC-KENT-STATE-RING-THEORY-QUAL-2017` 11 — are the tractable ones; the textbook-backed groups (`SRC-TEXT-HAT02` 35, `SRC-TEXT-HK71` 21, `SRC-TEXT-SS03` 20) need a page read per card.

## 2026-11-19, sixth item: two shared-clone papercuts that read as errors — a live `index.lock` and an ambiguous `omm/main`

**Object and need.** Both cost this session real turns, and both present as a failure of something other than what is wrong. Neither is a repository defect; both are artefacts of several chats working one clone.

**`index.lock` is usually live, not stale.** `git commit` failed with `Unable to create '.git/index.lock': File exists` several times, and the standing advice to "remove the file manually" would have destroyed another chat's in-flight commit. `ps -eo pid,etimes,args | grep '[g]it commit'` showed the holder: another chat's `git commit` started seconds earlier, and two other chats were already running retry loops of their own against the same lock. The working pattern, which succeeded on the third attempt and again on the first in a later turn, is

```
for i in $(seq 1 20); do git commit -q -m "..." -- <paths> 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 6; done
```

The lock file itself is 2.4 MB (an index copy), which is why it looks like debris. A lock older than a minute with no `git commit` process behind it would be stale; none was seen today.

**`omm/main` is an ambiguous refname.** `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> omm/main` began printing `warning: refname 'omm/main' is ambiguous` and returning non-zero for commits that were in fact on the remote — both a `refs/heads/omm/main` and a `refs/remotes/omm/main` exist. Ancestry checks must name `refs/remotes/omm/main`:

```
R=$(git rev-parse refs/remotes/omm/main); git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> $R && echo ok
```

With that, the two commits this session made after the warning appeared (`2edda155da`, `fe28a2962a`) both verified as present, after the push tool had refused them.

**Uncertainty.** The retry intervals are empirical, not tuned; a commit that fails twenty times was not seen and would need a different remedy. What created the duplicate `omm` ref was not investigated, and the fix (deleting the stray local branch) was not applied, since it is a shared clone and another chat may be using the name.

negating each step — prealgebraic equivalence being symmetric — gives $-D$. (b) is the family

$2(D\cdot l)(D\cdot m)\ge D^2$ reads
$$
2(rq+s)(r+s)\ \ge\ r^2q(2-2g)+s^2(2-2g)+2rsN,

## 2026-11-19, seventh item: residue 3 is being edited by more than one chat, so the never-reviewed count is not one lane's

**Object and need.** The fifth item above recorded 470 never-reviewed cards in residue 3 (`int(id.rsplit("-",1)[1], 36) % 16 == 3`) and treated them as one lane's work. Picking cards this session showed that other chats are writing into the same residue, so that framing is wrong in a way that matters for scheduling: duplicated reads are possible, and the count falls for reasons other than the lane's own work.

**Evidence, from cards picked as unreviewed and then found touched the same day.** Both are residue 3 and both carry a `claude` event dated 2026-11-19 that this chat did not write:

| card | residue | event found |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `E-HK-CG7N` | 3 | `solution-reviewed` by `claude`, 2026-11-19, recomputing a Hoffman--Kunze 1.3.2 row reduction |
| `P-7CUNN` | 3 | `solution-written` by `claude`, 2026-11-19, supplying parts (c), (e), (f), (g) and checking each answer by differentiation |

Neither was in the 470-item set when it was taken; `E-HK-CG7N` now counts as reviewed and `P-7CUNN` as freshly completed, both by someone else. A third card picked the same way, `P-KU6C3` (residue 3), was still untouched.

**What follows, and what does not.** It follows that the brief's partition is not exclusive in practice: either two chats were given the same residue, or a chat is working a different modulus (`% 8` against `% 16` would put every `% 16 == 3` card inside the `% 8 == 3` class only when the residues agree, and they do not always). It does **not** follow that any specific card was read twice; the two above were read once each, by the other chat, and this chat moved on when it saw the event.

**Advice for the next dispatcher.** Treat a residue as a work queue, not a property: check a card for an existing `solution-reviewed` or same-day `solution-written` event before spending a read on it, which is what caught both cases here and cost one command each. Any count of remaining work should be re-measured rather than quoted from an earlier entry, this one included.

**Uncertainty.** Two sightings out of three picks is a small sample and could reflect a single chat finishing a batch; the briefs of the other chats were not read, so how the overlap arose is not established. The residue values were computed from the card ids with the formula in the brief, not from any assignment record.

## 2026-11-19: Yang's 5.2.14 and 5.2.16 at printed pp. 105--106 — the char-p bounds, and a false "coordinate ring is a PID"

**Object and need.** `P-AGH5214IRRCURVESCHARP` (V.2.14) and `P-AGH5216KGROUPBUNDLE` (V.2.16), two
more of the three Chapter V cards counted in the record above.

**V.2.14, printed p. 105.** Riemann--Hurwitz and adjunction: normalizing $Y$ and composing with the
projection to $C$ gives $2g(\widetilde Y)-2\ge d(2g-2)+\deg R$, and $g(Y)\ge g(\widetilde Y)$ by
(4.1.8), so $2g(Y)-2\ge d(2g-2)$; adjunction gives
$$
(aC_0+bf)\cdot\bigl((a-2)C_0+(b+2g-2-e)f\bigr)=-ae(a-2)+a(b+2g-2-e)+b(a-2),
$$
that is $ae(1-a)+2b(a-2)\ge(d-a)(2g-2)$. For $2\le a\le p-1$ the degree is $d=a$ and $b\ge\frac12ae$;
for $a\ge p$ it drops to $d=a-np$, and $(d-a)(2g-2)=2np(1-g)$ with $a-d\le a-1$ gives
$b\ge\frac12ae+1-g$; and $a=1$ is a section, where $\deg L\ge\deg\mathcal E$ gives $b\ge0$. Part (b) is
cut off in the retained copy, and the remark says so rather than reporting an error.

**V.2.16, printed p. 106: a false first step.** The entry argues that $R=\OO_C(C)$ is a PID, hence
every finitely generated projective module is free, hence every locally free sheaf is a sum of copies
of $\OO_C$. The first step is false: $\OO_C(C)$ is a Dedekind domain, and a PID only when its class
group vanishes, which it does not for an affine curve of genus $\ge1$ — the elliptic curve minus a
point is the standard case. The exercise's statement still holds, on the right ground: for a regular
affine curve $K_0(R)\cong\ZZ\oplus\Pic(R)$, so equal classes force equal rank and equal determinant
class, which on a curve is the isomorphism class. The card's own steps take exactly that route, from
$A$ a Dedekind domain rather than a PID, and the remark records the contrast.

**The remainder.** One Chapter V card still lacks Yang: V.2.7, at printed p. 103, whose entry is the
garbled one and needs the page image read before anything goes on the card.

**Repair.** `P-AGH5214IRRCURVESCHARP` in `50da069890` and `P-AGH5216KGROUPBUNDLE` in `6d8cf34b17`, one
commit each; this record in the COMPLAINTS commit that carries it. No step, statement or hypothesis of
either card changes.

## 2026-11-19, eleventh item: two more residue-5 cards read — the Hilbert matrix and the matrix-unit eigenbasis — both correct

**Object.** Two residue-5 cards of `SRC-TEXT-HK71`, residues computed before editing, read against the retained text.

**`E-HK-EZDH`, §1.6 Exercise 12, printed p. 26 — correct.** The card proves the Hilbert matrix $H_n=(1/(i+j-1))$ invertible with integer inverse through the Cauchy-matrix inverse. The proof was checked end to end: $R_j(x_m)=\delta_{mj}$ by construction; the residue of $R_j$ at $-y_i$ is the displayed $b_{ij}$, the signs working out as $\prod_{\ell\ne j}(-y_i-x_\ell)=(-1)^{n-1}\prod_{\ell\ne j}(x_\ell+y_i)$ over $\prod_{\ell\ne i}(y_\ell-y_i)=(-1)^{n-1}\prod_{\ell\ne i}(y_i-y_\ell)$; and evaluating the partial fraction at $z=x_m$ gives $CB=I$. The specialization $x_j=j-1$, $y_i=i$ gives $x_i+y_j=i+j-1$ and the four products reduce to the displayed factorials, with $(-1)^{2n-i-j}=(-1)^{i+j}$. The binomial form was checked equal to the factorial form by expanding and cancelling. Independently, both formulas were compared with the exact inverse of $H_n$ in sympy for $n=2,3,4,5$: every entry agrees and every entry is an integer. (For $n=4$ the inverse is $[[16,-120,240,-140],[-120,1200,-2700,1680],[240,-2700,6480,-4200],[-140,1680,-4200,2800]]$.) Commit `17876ecdc1`.

**`E-HK-65-5`, §6.5 Exercise 5, printed pp. 206--207 — correct.** For $A=\operatorname{diag}(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ the matrix unit satisfies $AE_{ij}=a_iE_{ij}$ and $E_{ij}A=a_jE_{ij}$ entrywise, so $T_A(E_{ij})=(a_i-a_j)E_{ij}$; the $n^2$ matrix units are a basis, so the one basis diagonalizes every $T_A$ in the family. Commit `faee7340f2`.

**An operational note.** The working text of the book used for these page checks, `.scratch/hk.txt`, was overwritten by another process during this pass: it went from 416 pages to one. It was regenerated with `pdftotext` into `.scratch/hkbook.txt` (416 pages) and the checks were made against that. Any lane using a shared `.scratch` path for an extraction should expect another lane to clobber it; a file per lane is safer.

It sits directly above `[[P-HCAO21]]`, "Dual module of a zero-dimensional Gorenstein algebra", which asks what can be said about $\Hom_k(R,k)$ and about the socle under a specified augmentation $\varepsilon\colon R\to k$. That card has no `solution` block and no `hint` block, so the page states the answer to a problem the corpus does not solve, and states it with no argument, no referent and no citation (`CITE-8`). Both halves are true -- the canonical module of a zero-dimensional Gorenstein ring is the ring, and Theorem 5.3 of Huneke, "Hyman Bass and Ubiquity: Gorenstein Rings", arXiv:math/0209199, printed p. 11, makes "self-injective", "socle of length one" and "Gorenstein" equivalent -- so the sentence is not wrong, it is unsupported.

## 2026-11-19: the macro-arity class behind #164 measured and closed — 158 `\dd` and 20 `\restrictionof` spans, repaired in 28 commits

**Object and need.** The entry of 2026-11-17 headed "the corpus validates again, the two blocking errors were notation, and the gate cannot see the class they belong to" measured the class with the rule "a declared argument whose token is `_`, `^`, `$`, `}` or `&`" and reported "one pre-existing span, the `\units` of line 29 of `PR-N6S6P`, and nothing else in either tree". Issue #164 was filed on the same class. That measurement undercounts it twice: it does not see a macro given fewer brace groups than it declares when the next token is a control sequence, and it does not see a two-argument macro given one braced argument followed by an ordinary token. Measured with the full arity test instead — for each macro with declared arguments, count the arguments actually present, braced or not, and flag the occurrence when fewer than the declared number are there — the corpus carries **158 occurrences of `\dd` and 20 of `\restrictionof` with fewer than their two arguments**, in 20 and 8 files respectively, and `wiki/` carries none. `\dd` is `\frac{\partial #1}{\partial #2}` and `\restrictionof` is `\left.#1\right|_{#2}`, both two-argument; `\dd x$` dies with `! Missing } inserted` under the project preamble and `\dd x\Bigr` silently sets $\partial x/\partial\Bigr$, so both are rendering failures a reader sees and the gate does not.

**Repaired.** `P-AGH213SURJLOCAL`'s `\surjectsvia` (already done in `a7eb7ed9d4`) and the two #164 spans of 2026-11-17 are not counted here. The rest were repaired on 2026-11-19, one commit per card, no statement or citation touched: the `\dd` uses now write `\dx`, `\dy`, `\dz`, `\dt`, `\dw`, `\dr`, `\dA`, `\dtheta` where those macros exist and `\,du`, `\,ds`, `\,d\zeta`, `\,d\varphi`, `\,d\alpha`, `\,d\rho` where they do not, and `\frac{\dd}{\dd z}` now reads `\frac{d}{dz}`; the `\restrictionof` uses now give both arguments, the restricted object read off each sentence (`\restrictionof{f_0}{A}`, `\restrictionof{S^{4n+3}}{U}`, `\restrictionof{\RR_d}{I}`, `\restrictionof{f}{t=1}`, ...). 27 cards, 28 commits: `b36394bb83`, `fb071ae448`, `f658a2faf5`, `04a9fbc6c3`, `5dae59cce1`, `f9bc1234d2`, `6b6102b987`, `005f99eb31`, `2e605c501e`, `4b41d8b6c4`, `e0df1ddc99`, `7738544e62`, `8867355aff`, `f738abe0d9`, `82b1e58e05`, `2e1728fb52`, `3a2cf3bccc`, `003a9687a2`, `f44ec93b14`, `e7226a1e63`, `60eb02385b`, `a25c3db397`, `c6f64fea1b`, `6266bbe718`, `181436ea7f`, `dc728a8ae9`, `2c4730d44a`, `6dbdad1e15`.

**Measured after, on the same rule.** Zero `\dd` and zero `\restrictionof` with fewer than two arguments in `corpus/` and in `wiki/`, and zero fatal arity spans for any of the 68 argument-taking macros of `vocabularies/macros.json` across both trees. Typeset with the project preamble, each repaired form renders as written and each snippet leaves `pdflatex -halt-on-error` at exit 0.

**A false positive the screen cannot avoid.** Five spans in `E-BGKED` read `\dd fx`, `\dd fy`: a two-argument macro with two unbraced arguments, legal and correct ($\partial f/\partial x$). They are the reason "bare `\dd`" is not the same as a defect, and they were left alone.

**What zero does not mean.** The test is textual and arity-only. It cannot see an argument taken from a token such as `(` or `=`, which is legal TeX and wrong mathematics — the case the 2026-11-17 entry itself names as invisible — so the measurement establishes that no declared argument is missing, not that every macro use says what it should.

**Repair.** This record only, in the COMPLAINTS commit that carries it; the cards are in the commits named above. **Uncertainty.** Not checked: the rendered site, which is built in CI; and no whole-corpus `qualc check` was run for this record — the checks are the per-card `qualc.authoring check`, `tools/check_macros.py`, `tools/sync_macros.py --check` and `tools/extraction_detector.py --range-gate` on the touched files, and the scan above.

## 2026-11-19: the Chapter V sweep closes on V.2.7, and Chapter IV opens — 4.1.1 and 4.1.2 at printed p. 84

**Object and need.** `P-AGH527ELLRULEDSECT` (V.2.7, the last Chapter V card without Yang), and
`P-AGH411REGULAROUTSIDEP` (IV.1.1) and `P-AGH412POLESATFINITESET` (IV.1.2), the first two of the
Chapter IV cards, which are **65 of 67** — Yang's set covers Chapter IV as well, and the Chapter V
sweep is now complete.

**V.2.7, printed p. 103, read on the page image.** The retained text version's extraction of this entry
is garbled, so the reading was made on the rendered page. $\mathcal E$ is the normalized indecomposable
bundle with $e=-1$ by the proof of (2.12), and the surface is unique by (2.15); a section corresponds
to a surjection $\mathcal E\to\mathcal L(\mathfrak d)\to0$, with $\deg\mathfrak d=1$ by (2.15), so
$\mathfrak d=P$ for a point of $C$; conversely (2.16) gives one $\mathcal E'$ for each $P\in C$. The
section attached to $P$ is $C_0+(P-P_0)f$, with $\mathcal E'\cong\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal L\bigl(\frac{P-P_0}{2}\bigr)$
— the half exists because $\Pic^0$ of an elliptic curve is divisible — and two sections are linearly
equivalent only if $Pf\sim Qf$, which forces $P=Q$, since a degree-one map $C\to\PP^1$ would make $C$
rational. That is the one-dimensional family with no two members linearly equivalent.

**IV.1.1, printed p. 84.** With $Q\ne P$ and $D=2P-Q$ of degree $1$, taking $n>\max\{2g-2,g,1\}$ gives
$\ell(nD)=n+1-g\ge1$, so $nD-(f)=D_0$ is effective of degree $n$ and $(f)=D_0-2nP+nQ$: a pole at $P$,
regular elsewhere.

**IV.1.2, printed p. 84.** The same with $D=2P_1+\cdots+2P_r-(2r-1)Q$ of degree $1$: $(f)$ is
$D_0-2n(P_1+\cdots+P_r)+n(2r-1)Q$, so the poles are exactly at the $P_i$ and their orders are $2n$.

**Repair.** `P-AGH527ELLRULEDSECT` in `81446bee3c`, `P-AGH411REGULAROUTSIDEP` in `fae454db75`,

## 2026-11-19: Yang's 4.1.3, 4.1.4 and 4.1.5 at printed p. 84 — two affineness criteria and the dim|D| bound, with one arithmetic slip

**Object and need.** `P-AGH413NONPROPERISAFFINE` (IV.1.3), `P-AGH414NOPROPERCOMPONENT` (IV.1.4) and
`P-AGH415DIMLEQDEG` (IV.1.5), three more of the sixty-five Chapter IV cards counted in the record
above.

**IV.1.3, printed p. 84.** The hint followed: (II, 4.10.2(e)) embeds $X$ as an open subset of a complete
$\bar X$ with finite complement $\{P_1,\ldots,P_r\}$; the previous exercise gives $f$ with poles exactly
there; and $f$ is a finite morphism $\bar X\to\PP^1$, so $X=f^{-1}(\AA^1)$ is affine. The finiteness is
where regularity and dimension one enter.

**IV.1.4, printed p. 84.** Reduction to the integral case: (III, 3.3.1) and (III, 3.3.2) let one assume
$X$ integral; the normalization $\widetilde X$ is then not proper either, so (4.1.3) makes it affine, and
$\widetilde X\to X$ is finite by (III, 3.4.2), hence $X$ is affine.

**IV.1.5, printed p. 84, one arithmetic slip.** $\dim\linearsystem{D}=\ell(D)-1=\deg D-g+\ell(K-D)$
with $\ell(K-D)\le\ell(K)=g$ for $D$ effective gives $\dim\linearsystem{D}\le\deg D$, equality only for
$D=0$ or $g=0$. The entry's display of the last input is wrong as printed: it writes
$\ell(K)-\ell(K-K)=2g-2+1-g=g$, where $2g-2+1-g=g-1$; the value $g$ comes from
$\ell(K)-\ell(0)=g-1$ together with $\ell(0)=1$. The conclusion uses $\ell(K)=g$, which is right.

**Repair.** `P-AGH413NONPROPERISAFFINE` in `233bad470b`, `P-AGH414NOPROPERCOMPONENT` in `267af3a502`,

## 2026-11-19: Yang's 4.1.6, 4.1.7 and 4.1.8 at printed p. 84 — and a construction that yields only constants on an elliptic curve

**Object and need.** `P-AGH416MAPTOP1DEGREE` (IV.1.6), `P-AGH417HYPERELLIPTIC` (IV.1.7) and
`P-AGH418ARITHGENUSSINGULAR` (IV.1.8), three more of the Chapter IV cards counted in the record above.

**IV.1.6, printed p. 84: the divisor is one short.** The entry takes $D=gP$ and quotes
$\ell(D)\ge\deg D+1-g=1$, then concludes a morphism of degree $g$. The inequality $\ell\ge1$ gives no
nonconstant function: for $g=1$, $\ell(P)=1+\ell(K-P)=1$ since $\deg(K-P)=-1$, so the only sections of
$\OO(P)$ are constants, and a degree-one map would make $X$ rational anyway. With $D=(g+1)P$ one has
$\ell(D)\ge(g+1)+1-g=2$, so there is a nonconstant $f$ with its only pole at $P$, of order at most
$g+1$, and the morphism it defines has degree at most $g+1$ — which is the bound the exercise states,
not an equality. Both points are recorded on the card's remark.

**IV.1.7, printed p. 84.** At $g=2$, $\deg K=2$ and $\dim\linearsystem{K}=1$; Riemann--Roch at a point
gives $\ell(P)-\ell(K-P)=1+1-2=0$, and $\dim\linearsystem{P}=1$ would be a degree-one map, impossible
for $g>1$; hence $\ell(P)=1=\ell(K-P)$ and $P$ is not a base point of $\linearsystem{K}$. A
base-point-free system of degree $2$ and dimension $1$ gives a degree-two morphism by (II, 7.8.1). Part
(b) is the second projection off a curve of type $(g+1,2)$ on $\PP^1\times\PP^1$, finite and nonconstant
by (II, 6.8) and of degree $2$ by (II, 6.9).

**IV.1.8, printed p. 84.** From $0\to\OO_X\to f_*\OO_{\widetilde X}\to\sum_P\widetilde\OO_P/\OO_P\to0$,
with both outer $H^0$ equal to $k$ and the skyscraper quotient having no $H^1$, the long exact sequence
gives $p_a(X)=p_a(\widetilde X)+\sum_P\delta_P$; then $p_a=0$ forces every $\delta_P=0$, so the curve is
nonsingular of genus zero, hence $\PP^1$ by (1.3.5). Part (c) reduces to a plane curve by projection and
computes $\delta_P$ at a node and a cusp.

**Repair.** `P-AGH416MAPTOP1DEGREE` in `997dce1ccb`, `P-AGH417HYPERELLIPTIC` in `e01e56c9c0`,

## 2026-11-19, twelfth item: three more residue-5 cards read — §6.7, §7.1 and §7.4 — all correct, and a transcription error caught before it became a false report

**Object.** Three residue-5 cards of `SRC-TEXT-HK71`, read against the retained text at their printed pages.

**`E-HK-67-5`, §6.7 Exercise 5, printed p. 218 — correct.** The exercise refers to Example 3 of §6.2, whose matrix is $[[5,-6,-6],[-1,4,2],[3,-6,-4]]$ at printed p. 188; in sympy its characteristic polynomial is $(x-2)^2(x-1)$ with eigenspaces of dimensions 2 and 1, so it is diagonalizable with exactly the two values the Lagrange polynomials use. With $E_1=2I-A$ and $E_2=A-I$ the identities hold exactly: $E_1+E_2=I$, $E_1+2E_2=A$, $E_1E_2=0$, and also $E_1^2=E_1$, $E_2^2=E_2$. Commit `a7865ed900`.

**`E-HK-71-5`, §7.1 Exercise 5, printed p. 231 — correct.** The independence argument is right: applying $N^{n-1-r}$ to a relation with least nonzero coefficient $c_r$ kills the terms with $j>r$ because the exponent is at least $n$, leaves $c_rN^{n-1}\alpha$, and the terms with $j<r$ vanish by choice of $r$. The matrix in $\{\alpha,N\alpha,\ldots,N^{n-1}\alpha\}$ is the subdiagonal shift, as the card displays: column $j$ is $e_{j+1}$ for $j<n-1$ and the last column is $0$. Commit `1418ecb615`.

**`E-HK-74-5`, §7.4 Exercise 5, printed p. 260 — correct, all four parts.** Checked in sympy on the printed $8\times8$ matrix. (a) $\chi=x^4(x-1)^4$; $A^2(A-I)^2=0$ with $A(A-I)^2$ and $A^2(A-I)$ nonzero, so $m=x^2(x-1)^2$; $\operatorname{rank}A=\operatorname{rank}(A-I)=6$ gives two Jordan blocks at each eigenvalue, hence the invariant factors $x^2(x-1)^2$ twice. (b) $\ker A^2$ and $\ker(A-I)^2$ both have dimension 4 and the displayed spanning sets lie in them; $e_0=1-3x^2+2x^3$ satisfies $e_0\equiv1\bmod x^2$ and $e_0\equiv0\bmod(x-1)^2$, and $E_0=e_0(A)$ equals the displayed matrix exactly, kills the displayed $W_1$ vectors, and has rank and trace 4. (c) $J_2(0)\oplus J_2(0)\oplus J_2(1)\oplus J_2(1)$, agreeing with (a). (d) for $\alpha_1=e_2+e_5-e_8$ and $\alpha_2=e_4+e_6-e_8$ each four-vector chain has rank 4 and the eight vectors together have determinant $-1$, so $Z(\alpha_1;T)\oplus Z(\alpha_2;T)$ is direct and is $\RR^8$. Commit `4d2837d751`.

**A near-miss worth recording.** The first run of the (d) check reported the eight vectors of rank **6**, which would have made the card's direct-sum claim false. The error was mine: I had typed $\alpha_1=e_2+e_6-e_8$ in the scratch check instead of the card's $e_2+e_5-e_8$. Re-running with the card's vectors gave determinant $-1$. The lesson is the one this file has recorded before in other forms: a computed contradiction is a claim about two texts, and the cheaper of the two to re-read is one's own transcription.
